texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s7-2: the main access control on the building’s outer wall stopped us dead. The terminal was glowing red. We had no way to shut down the deeper generator from outside, and could only retreat along the route we had come, carrying the access-denied error log with
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s7-3:
us.
By the time we withdrew beyond the Zone Eight boundary marker, the heavy soundproof hood had bruised the roots of her ears. After confirming there was no ambush nearby, she released the clasps and tried to get some air.
At that instant, the wind vanished.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s8-1:
Her movement froze halfway through.
There was no scream, no struggle. I watched her knees give way, her whole body slamming heavily into the muddy weeds. I didn’t know who was in the darkness,
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s8-2: but I knew what had happened in that second—a portable directional sound-emission device had been aimed at her in the blind spot where we thought we were safe, and someone had pressed the switch.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s9-1:
I knelt in those weeds, my palm pressed against her shoulder. The soundproof hood had fallen into the muddy water. The ring of bruising around her ears was still bright red, but she was no longer breathing.
Before
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s9-2: I could even feel her body losing its warmth, my consciousness was abruptly severed. She remained forever in the mud of that world, while I opened my eyes again in the eight o’clock morning of the current new world.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s10-1: Back at the White Tower, I told the version of her standing here and now everything: the dead end at the main access control, the error log and V-3 interface information we had bought with our lives.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s11-1: After hearing it all, her perpetually calm eyes froze for the briefest moment. After a short silence, she went alone to the White Tower to verify the maintenance records and the hood’s production specifications.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s11-2: Once she confirmed that the ordinary deterrent setting and the lethal setting did in fact share the V-3 interface, she took the hidden system version number I had dug up earlier and knocked on Sera’s door.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s12-1: Just as it had in the previous world, Sera verified the version number and immediately found in the local system that her own program signature had been privately invoked by a maintenance supplement she could not see. To reclaim
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s12-2: the right to know that the Technical Seat had hollowed out, Sera used Estelle’s formal appeal to issue a limited, deniable procedural audit order, approving checks of three directories: the Contract Explanation Section, the Candidate
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s12-3:
Disposition Index, and the Body Rights Witness Section.
The authorization still covered only those three. But this time, with the previous round’s error log, Estelle understood the system’s permission tree. The log showed that
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s12-4: the control node for the outer-wall main access that had once rejected us was attached directly beneath the root directory of the “Old Dispute Explanation Section.” The approved “Contract Explanation Section” was a lower-level
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s12-5:
branch of that root.
She submitted the paper audit order’s number to the system. Taking advantage of the underlying logic that required requests for subdirectories to pass through their superior physical node first, she cleverly
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s12-6:
used the limited legal procedure to trick open the outer main access.
Then she went to Supplies and checked out this M-114 sealed soundproof hood. She also found an old survey map and marked out a high ridge along a dried riverbed.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s13-1:
Just as in the loop that had been deadlocked moments earlier, Sera verified the version number and discovered that her own program signature had been called in a maintenance supplement she herself could not see. To keep Otto and Galon from reducing the candidate procedure to a mere stamping process, Sera, protecting her seat’s interests, used Estelle’s formal appeal to issue on the spot a limited procedural audit order for the “Dispute Explanation Section,” the archive originally used to handle candidates’ objections to their contracts.
With the audit order in hand, Estelle used the flaw in the White Tower’s old system classification that I had memorized. She pointed out that the guard room was attached to a subdirectory of that section in the authorization tree, cleverly extending the legal procedure to cover the guard room’s access controls.
Then she went to Supplies and checked out this M-114 sealed soundproof hood. She also found an old survey map and marked out a high ridge along a dried riverbed.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s14-1: Knowing that pursuit parties carrying out the judgment could appear at the boundary marker at any moment, begging for mercy or forcing our way through would be pointless. We had to take the ridge line, passing through the blind spot of the perimeter sentries’ direct view.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s15-1: The notebook and pen that never left her side were both there. Replacing the paper copies from the previous round, which could not cross the cycle with our memories, was the heavy soundproof hood she had checked out. In addition, she had cut four strips of cotton to the same length and clenched them in her hand.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s18-1: When we were about three hundred paces from the ring of thin iron posts standing in the wilderness, she stopped. At that distance, the wind could still be heard, and far away, the abandoned building stood quietly.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s19-1: She found a flat stone and sat down, spreading the four rolled strips of cotton across her knees.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s21-1: “This is a heavy soundproof hood. Once it’s on, the entire ring of sealing padding around the ears will bite tightly against the skull.” She pinched up the cotton cloth, her tone leaving no room for discussion. “But I can’t
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s21-2: guarantee that the seal will remain perfectly fitted while we’re moving. If sound leaks in, the V-3 band will get through instantly. So both ear canals need two additional layers of cotton each, as a second physical barrier.”
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s23-1: “Sera’s audit order this morning didn’t authorize an escort. If I go in, I’ll be trespassing in violation of procedure.” I looked at the strips of cloth. “Once you put it on, besides making it impossible to hear anything, the pressure from the hood will affect your balance. You won’t even hear what you’ve stepped on, and you could lose your direction at any moment.”
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s25-1: “For dangers I can’t verify precisely, I can only add more protection on myself. As for the audit order, it’s a hook. Going in without it would also be a violation. With it, as long as I find a result, Sera will be happy to retroactively recognize it as legal.” She put the document back into her pocket unchanged.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s28-1: Once the cotton was ready, she rested the soundproof hood on her legs and turned to look at me.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s30-1: “There are three hand signals for entering.”
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s32-1: “First, tap the back of my hand twice. That means we’ve arrived. Second, tap me once. That means ‘stop.’ Whenever you need me to stop, tap once. If we’re going to keep moving, after I stop, take hold of my sleeve again and lead me half a step in the direction you want to go. I’ll follow.”
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s35-1: She turned her wrist and seized mine from the other side, tightening all five fingers around it.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s37-1: “Third, if I grip your wrist tightly like this from the other side, it means I want to retreat. When you feel this movement, take me back along the route immediately.”
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s39-1: Her gaze turned cold, as if she were issuing a military order. “Once we’re inside, I’ll be behind you. You won’t keep turning around while you’re finding the way. So you recognize this movement and this movement only. Don’t ask why, and don’t try to dissuade me. Understood?”
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s42-1: Looking into her unquestioning eyes, I swallowed hard, forcing back every attempt to bargain.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s44-1: “All right. As soon as you grip my wrist from the other side, I won’t ask why, I won’t try to stop you, and I’ll take you back immediately.”
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s45-1: Only after hearing that assurance repeated back did some of the tension leave her shoulders. She nodded hard.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s48-1: After explaining everything, she took out the notebook. She pulled out the pen and bent over it on her knees, writing three lines in quick strokes. Once the ink had dried a little, she closed the notebook and handed it straight to me.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s50-1:
Entering today. Route determined by Arno.
From the moment the ears are sealed until the outer acoustic barrier is shut down, nothing seen or heard by the undersigned is to be recorded.
Within this section, the recorder is absent.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s53-1: I stared for a moment. “You’re giving it to me?”
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s55-1: “Completely cutting off my hearing will take away some of my balance, and the terrain is unknown. I don’t know whether I can walk through steadily. I won’t have the capacity to make sure it stays protected.”
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s56-1: Her tone sounded perfectly ordinary. But just as I reached out to take it, the fingers gripping the edge of the notebook tightened slightly, their knuckles paling.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s58-1: “Don’t let it fall into the mud with me. These are seven years of original records.”
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s61-1: I took it in both hands and secured it against my body. She drew a deep breath and began sealing her ears.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s62-1: She stuffed the four strips of cotton into her ear canals, two on each side. Once the second barrier was in place, she forced the gray soundproof hood down over her head. The moment she fastened it tight, she raised her head and stared straight at my lips.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s63-1:
I asked at a normal volume whether she could hear me. She shook her head. I raised my voice and shouted. She still shook her head.
She waved her hand forcefully beside her ear, confirming that even the
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s63-2:
hurried sound of the wind had been blocked.
She closed her eyes and adjusted for two seconds. When she opened them again, she extended her left hand toward me, the back facing up, holding steady in the air.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s68-1: This time, her hearing was sealed completely. If the maintenance specifications were not lying, the heavy soundproof hood and the cotton packed inside it formed a multilayer acoustic impedance—the only barrier we had against lethal sound patterns.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s69-1: For the first hundred paces, she walked fairly steadily. But during the second hundred, the symptoms of imbalance began to show. The heavy soundproof hood’s tremendous clamping force pressed against her temporal bones, squeezing the vestibular system of her inner ears along with the deeply packed cotton.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s70-1:
When we were fifty paces from the ring of iron posts, the uneven ground made her misstep.
The mechanical pressure had disrupted not only her inner ear’s sense of balance; she also could not hear the faint friction
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s70-2: of gravel rolling beneath her feet, and could not correct her steps instantly through environmental feedback as she normally would. Her center of gravity unconsciously shifted outward, and her steps became hesitant.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s71-1: I didn’t say anything or pull hard on her. I only lowered my shoulder imperceptibly inward. Holding my sleeve, she used the slight resistance beneath her hand to find a stable point of balance again, and her route naturally adjusted back with my body.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s73-1: In front of a gravel pit, she suddenly released my arm once, having lost her anchor in the complete silence because she had lost her sense of direction.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s76-1:
The instant she let go, I stopped as if nailed to the ground.
I didn’t turn around to grab her. I stood there quietly, like a statue, and waited patiently.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s77-1:
I counted a dozen or so times silently in my head.
Her hand came back. After feeling through the air and finding my arm, she gripped it a little tighter than before. I counted three more times in my head before taking the first step again.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s80-1: After passing through the iron posts, she did not stop right away. Her arm trembled slightly, but her steps did not falter. One after another, they continued, mechanical and firm.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s81-1:
Crossing the abandoned courtyard overgrown with weeds, we finally reached the lifeless Dispute Explanation Section building.
The limited audit order I had bought with the information brought back
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s81-2: from the previous round temporarily unlocked the outer door leading to the dispute section. This blast door, meant to open for the End-of-Cycle candidate ceremony, now showed a yellow access light.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s82-1:
I stepped back half a pace to make room.
She drew the candidate badge from her pocket and pressed it against the access panel, then pressed her index finger into the venous-blood reader below. The heavy door gave a low mechanical clack and slowly slid inward.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s83-1:
Only after we were fully inside the building did she stop, breathing heavily.
A moment later, she took a deep breath and once again held the back of her hand steadily in front of me. She did not take my wrist.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s87-1:
Beyond the door was a long, dim corridor.
The building’s ordinary lighting grid had gone down long ago. I switched on the small flashlight in my hand. Its weak beam could barely illuminate the dust-covered floor a few steps ahead.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s88-1: The surroundings grew darker and darker. Once we had fully entered the lightless depths, the walls on both sides of the corridor felt exactly the same, while her ears remained tightly sealed.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s88-2: Her hand instinctively reached toward her pocket, searching for the pen so she could record the route and her condition. But halfway there, it suddenly froze in place as if pinned down.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s89-1:
She remembered. Her notebook was now tucked against my chest.
A trace of deeply unfamiliar struggle flashed in her eyes. In the end, she pulled her hand back.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s92-1:
Three branches appeared at the end of the corridor.
The flashlight could no longer reach into the depths on either side. The ground at the mouths of all three passages was covered in an even layer of dust, and their outlines looked identical.
I
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s92-2: stopped. In an ordinary ruin, I could still prick up my ears and use the faint airflow from ventilation ducts deeper inside to rule out a dead-end passage. But now there was no sound at all. The building’s entire air-supply system had stopped long ago.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s93-1: Without an auditory clue, I could only rely on instinct and lead her into the passage on the left.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s94-1: However, after about twenty steps in the dark, I swept the flashlight across the ground and found the dust beneath our feet smooth as a carpet. No heavy object had passed through or been dragged here in decades. Clearly, this was not a passage leading to the core facilities room.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s95-1:
Realizing something was wrong, I stopped and, at the same time, lightly tapped the back of her hand with my other hand.
She stopped at once, without hesitation.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s96-1: Holding her sleeve, I turned her around and led her back along the steps we had just taken. After retreating all the way to the fork, I crouched and swept the flashlight close along the ground. At last, deep inside the middle passage, I found a faint gray-white drag mark that had disturbed the dust.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s99-1: Once I had found the right direction again, I had her grip my sleeve once more and continued inward along the middle corridor.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s100-1: As she followed me back to the fork and began walking again, I felt the fingers clamped around my forearm suddenly spasm, uncontrollably.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s101-1: She didn’t know what had happened. She couldn’t ask, and I couldn’t explain. As long as her hand slid down my sleeve and gripped my wrist from the other side, we would retreat safely at once.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s102-1:
But she didn’t do that.
Her fingers clamped tightly around my arm through the sleeve, the knuckles gone white. Only after we stepped back onto the correct track did that force ease slightly.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s105-1: Following the middle passage to the end, we finally reached a control room that looked like an electrical distribution room.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s106-1: Estelle walked to the control console. A whole row of circuit breakers stood out on the wall. Beneath the leftmost blade was an encrusted metal plate covered in verdigris. The writing was blurred, but after checking three times, I finally confirmed that it was this one. Then I turned around and tapped the cold back of her hand twice, hard.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s109-1: After receiving the signal, she walked quickly to the circuit breaker and examined the metal plate. Once she had confirmed it, she gripped the rough handle and pulled it down.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s110-1: After a dull metallic clack, the mechanical structure inside the breaker disconnected.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s111-1: She pressed her palm flat against the cold wall and stood with her eyes closed, feeling for about ten seconds. The cessation of the mechanical equipment’s vibration was the only indirect indicator she could rely
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s111-2: on. Only when the faint numbness deep inside the wall had disappeared did she raise both arms and remove the soundproof hood. Then she reached into her ears and pulled out the four strips of cotton underneath.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s114-1:
The moment she pulled out the last strip of cotton, she squeezed her eyes shut in pain.
The rough cloth scraped her ear canals raw, and the faint sound of air moving through the corridor poured back in. A moment later,
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s114-2:
she finally opened her eyes and let out a long breath.
I handed her the notebook, still warm from my body.
She reached out and took it. She did not open it immediately. Instead, she raised her head and looked at me.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s116-1: “When we came back and walked through again just now, about how many paces did we stray from the original route?”
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s119-1: She nodded. Her gaze swept over the three lines she had written herself before entering. She pulled out the pen and quickly added several more lines.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s121-1:
The first three lines completed for today. One deviation during execution, twenty paces, confirmed afterward by questioning the undersigned. Right ear: water-film sensation after sealing.
This section is an after-the-fact addition.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s123-1: After writing the last stroke, she put the pen away neatly.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s126-1:
She slowly raised her hand and lightly pressed the outline of her right ear with her fingertip.
Only then did I see the mark clearly. It had been carved into her skin by the soundproof hood’s thick padding, running from the edge of her ear all the way around to its root. One place along the edge had been rubbed raw, with a trace of blood seeping out.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s130-1: “This right ear is still giving off a periodic ringing.” Her brow tightened slightly as she rubbed the root of her ear with a knuckle, her voice carrying an exhaustion she could not conceal. “When you speak now, it sounds to me as though there’s a thick layer of water between us.”
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s131-1: She lowered her hand and took a deep breath, forcing down the fatigue.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s133-1: “The generator for the outer acoustic barrier is off. As long as we stay inside this building, buried behind its thick walls, the directional equipment has neither a direct line of sight nor a path through.” She looked at me. “Let’s go. To the records foyer.”
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s136-1: We felt our way through the pitch-dark, deathly silent building. With the outer barrier no longer in the way, we used the flashlight to find our path and pushed open a double door beside the guard room. This was the records foyer of the three audit areas formally approved by the limited audit order.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s137-1: The terminals were still connected to the internal network’s weak backup power. Estelle logged in with her candidate badge and called up the three directories within the approved scope: the Contract Explanation Section, the Candidate Disposition Index, and the Body Rights Witness Section.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s138-1:
The blue light from the screen fell across her pale profile. She leafed rapidly through the old electronic files. Soon, her finger stopped on an archived record called “Disposition Completed.”
It was a public explanation under the Candidate Disposition Index.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s140-1: “This public archive has had its chain of evidence deliberately severed.” She stared at the screen. “It claims ‘Disposition Completed,’ but contains only a single conclusive system log entry.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s140-2: Even if something really happened in the system, there should at least be dual readings—the underlying feedback from both physical nodes being online at the same time. There’s nothing here.”
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s142-1: “If it was a copy between two devices, there would indeed be underlying feedback from both ends. But consciousness transfer doesn’t necessarily have that. The two ends might not even be online at the same time.” I looked at the simple
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s142-2: log entry. “And this briefing for candidates doesn’t even list which physical parameters and termination conditions can be changed later after a candidate signs the contract. That means there must be another hidden execution supplement.”
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s143-1:
She did not answer directly. Instead, she dragged the incomplete explanation into the cross-index. The progress bar blinked several times before a red access-denied notice appeared.
The system provided the path to the original source, but the highest-level lock of the Technical Seat hung conspicuously in front of it.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s145-1: “The source is in the core area sealed by the Technical Seat.” She pulled out the candidate badge.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s146-1:
Just then, the thin supply issue slip slid out of her pocket.
I bent down and glanced at it. The return due was clearly written: same day.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s148-1: “We probably won’t be returning this hood today. If we trigger an alarm and draw Kane here, he’ll know we entered this building if he follows this slip back to Supplies.”
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s150-1: “I left the slip there so they would find it.” She put the issue slip back into her pocket. “Now that the core area has the highest-level lock, no one
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s150-2: will believe anything we tell them about what we uncover today. I need the elders to follow the overdue record here themselves and witness what I found.”
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s151-1: She turned her head. The flashlight beam passed over the scattered filing cabinets in the foyer and shone straight at the heavy blast security door leading deeper inside. Crossing that door meant leaving the audit order’s protection completely and entering an area under the Church’s absolute taboo.
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s153-1: “The execution supplement hidden in the core area is behind that door.” She drew a deep breath, fixing the flashlight beam on the security door. “The highest-level lock, the undisclosed
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s153-2: underlying feedback… If continuance were truly a perfect transfer of consciousness, the Technical Seat would have no reason to conceal its strongest evidence so thoroughly. Unless
texts.chapter:v15-21b:event:text-s153-3: the so-called transfer never existed at all, and the original body was physically destroyed after being brought into this building. Let’s go. Cross the boundary and investigate.”
texts.chapter:chapter-22-silent-switch:title: Chapter Twenty-Two: The Mute Switch
texts.chapter:chapter-22-silent-switch:event:t:
Mill · Shutdown Rules (a sheet of paper nailed to the earthen wall, copied word for word):
“No one may shut down the mill alone.
Shutting it down requires two people. One checks the pin, one pulls the gate.
The one pulling

the gate cannot touch the pin. The one checking the pin may not touch the gate.
Once the checker confirms that the pin is seated, they report one sentence. The one pulling the gate repeats that sentence exactly before acting.”
At the end of the records foyer stood the blast door sealed by the Highest Technical Council.

“The electronic lock is dead, but the physical sensors in the door are still alive. Find the hydraulic monitoring port at the bottom of the frame.” Without looking back, she crouched down. “We don’t need to crack the permissions. Short the return line of the anti-crush sensor directly. That will make the lower-level system think the heavy door is crushing a living person.”

I used the pry bar to force open the concealed metal plate at the bottom of the doorframe. She precisely pulled out two yellow sensor cables and shorted them together.
“In the highest engineering regulations of the old era, the underlying physical command

preventing machinery from crushing people to death takes priority over digital security at any level.” She watched the gap in the door.
With a dull grinding of metal, the shorted line sent an alarm to the lower-level hydraulic system. Once it determined that the

heavy door was crushing bones, the system had no choice but to forcibly abandon its highest lockout state and execute an emergency retreat release. The heavy blast door slowly withdrew into the walls on both sides, revealing the dim production-line area beyond.

I already knew this place by heart. The cultivation troughs used to cast vessel shells, the conveyor tracks crossing overhead, were all where they had always been. After we crossed the silent area, the sliding door ahead opened without a sound and let us into the control room.

The first time we came to this control room, Yuna had tried to push the heavy metal case set into the console. It had not moved at all. The white skeleton in the faded uniform still sat withered before the slightly

tilted control panel, sunk into the broad swivel chair. His skull still hung slightly lowered, facing the dim instruments. One hand bone drooped at his side. The other still rested quietly on the heavy metal work case.

Estelle stopped in the doorway. She lowered her head and, without the slightest hesitation, quietly performed the most solemn gesture the dead were owed—both hands crossed and pressed hard against her heart.
When she raised her head again, her eyes had already locked back onto the console.
“There’s something on the terminal,” she said. Her voice sounded a little dry in the empty room.
I approached the terminal. There was only one solitary line on the screen, flickering faintly:
“Calibration recordings: One through Eight. Play?”
I stared at the line. I knew what was in them. On another timeline, I had already used the data key brought out of the ruins to unlock their protocol, and watched these technical review
recordings with their names and political identities erased. The safety limit of eight thousand people, the annihilation plan based on the conservation of information—all of it was in my head.
But out of the instinct to confirm this world’s condition, I still reached out and pressed the play button.
The screen flickered once and displayed a cold line of red text:
“Insufficient privileges. Access to this recording group was revoked by Central Command in the facility’s seventh year.”
I withdrew my hand. In this world, the recording group was locked tight.

“Let’s go. Forcibly accessing something whose permissions have been revoked will destroy it.” She turned around and took out the list she had recopied at the White Tower that morning from the information I had provided. “But the

trail hasn’t ended. I copied down the anti-counterfeiting registration number at the bottom of the public contract in the square. According to the network-topology records, that is the lookup code leading to the underlying data.

When this batch of shells was made, the ‘body-rights attestation’ section was originally used to define the baseline health records for harm inflicted on living people by hostile environments. But it also locked the original ownership

of these shell templates at the lowest level. All this data is stored in the peripheral node rooms. Once we enter the registration number there, we can find out how this batch of bodies was written into ‘voluntary candidates.’”

Over the next nearly four hours, we moved through the enormous facility, searching our way through it like an underground labyrinth. To avoid network surveillance, we could only piece together clues from one disconnected abandoned terminal after another and scattered paper records.

Among rows of rusted, cramped cells, we first found the facility’s bloodiest origin. Estelle pulled an early construction-period Camp Detention Log from beneath an overturned iron table. This had never been a research

institution at all, but a special camp for political prisoners. The first prisoners sent here were not even given the status of laborers. They were fed alive into the equipment, and their extracted capacity became

the first charge that drove the time machine into operation. It was a successful murder and soul extraction. Lysenko immediately submitted his appalling “Ten-Thousand Expansion Plan” to the upper levels of the Empire.

But beside the log lay a rejection order bearing the Sovereign’s red-letter seal. The dictator had seen through Lysenko’s ambition—the time machine’s political credibility had already collapsed, and if Lysenko gained control

of such a vast soul field and such technology, he would become an independent center of power no longer constrained by natural death or the Empire’s resources. The Sovereign needed to preserve the “AI Operator Project” to

provide the lower levels with their next false hope. So he used the most decisive means available to stop Lysenko: he allowed the AI project to complete body manufacture and memory writing as the Empire’s public façade, but

cut off the facility’s supply of coercive force. No more prisoners or guards were sent in. The institutional deadlock between two ambitious men brought the extraction of living bodies from ten thousand people to a complete halt.

In the enormous “Body Specifications Area,” we saw how Lysenko responded to that deadlock. Among the dust-covered independent workstations, he had begun secretly inserting his own additions into the vessel blueprints.

The screen displayed a public project file titled “National Operator Continuity Project.” To preserve operators’ experience during jumps, the state required White Towers and relay nodes around the world to establish

external life-record chains. But in a hidden directory on the same terminal, I found Lysenko’s “Private Permissions and Reserved Body Specifications.” Under the highest permissions he controlled externally, he had kept

this record chain for himself alone. Once this new human awoke, the original Lysenko, still outside, would gather its complete life record—the operator could not see this hidden administrative layer, change the target,

delete records, or stop it early. To mark this private device, he had abruptly drawn a pair of animal ears on the outside of the head in the blueprint. Beside them was an arrogant approval note: “Add them. Reason: better.”

He had not only reserved this absurd body. He had also inserted a voiceprint backdoor made from localized neuroendocrine editing into every ordinary person later produced in batches from the cat-eared
blueprint. The specification beside it stated coldly that this ineradicable genetic mark produced physiological submission to specific frequency bands, and that higher frequencies could cause
irreversible autonomic collapse—and that it could be easily blocked with suitable soundproofing material. That was why sound waves had become a weapon for maintaining political rank in the village.

At the final stretch of ruins, two old data hubs stood before us, completely divided by physical isolation barriers. They presented, with brutal clarity, the two independent gates involved in making a new human. One side was the

“soul-field capacity” interface, responsible for providing a first-person subject. If the anonymous capacity supplied was insufficient, the body emerging from the production line would be alive but empty of any “I.” The other was the

“personality source” interface, responsible for pouring past memories into a living person who already had a subject. If the system detected even the slightest discontinuity in the life record being entered, it physically blocked the

writing at the instant of insertion. That was why the so-called “Initiation Library” ultimately became only a row of teaching terminals for old language and arithmetic, meant to provide basic instruction to new humans who knew nothing.

Only after passing through these silent remains did the air gradually change from the stifling heaviness of stagnant water to a dry cold. A faint cooling-fan noise came from ahead. At last, we found the node room she had copied down.

The node room was a long, narrow room, its air murky. Farther inside, a heavy physical isolation plate had descended from the ceiling, sealing off the deeper section completely. Red warning text was printed across it. We did not touch it.
The two cabinets we needed to check stood quietly in plain view, their lights glowing dimly.
Estelle opened the record book and lowered her eyes to it.

“Sera’s paper authorization for the inspection is still valid, but its permissions only cover the peripheral archive-index area.” She closed the book and walked to the side of the cabinet. “But this node room we’re standing in has already crossed the physical approval boundary. The moment we leave an access record, it becomes a violation.”
“What if she checks the system logs afterward?”

“The terminals in the abandoned areas are offline. No one oversees what you check there. But the node room is connected to the main network. The moment we enter a query, it leaves an access record in the system that cannot be erased.

” She pointed to a separate auxiliary panel set apart beside the console. “Under the old lower-level two-person separation-of-powers procedure, the system doesn’t check whether the second person has advanced permissions. It only

needs to confirm that ‘operation’ and ‘supervision’ are independent. ‘Operation’ enters the command. ‘Supervision’ must independently confirm the risk warning on the screen. Both sides have to pass before the command can execute.”

“Keep your left hand on the assistant operator’s fingerprint area and watch the auxiliary screen on your side. I’ll enter the lookup code. If an escalation warning appears, press confirm.” She glanced at my position to make sure I could not reach her main keyboard. “First step: prepare for input.”
As her fingers tapped across the keyboard, a red escalation-query warning appeared on the auxiliary screen in front of me.
“Boundary-crossing warning. Confirmed.” I pressed the authorization key on the auxiliary console.
“Warning confirmed. Executing first step.”

During the long input process that followed, neither of us said a word about why we were doing it this way. It was only when the second credential went through and she crisply repeated, “Green light,” that I suddenly remembered an accident at the mill when I was ten.

That night, it was my and Roy’s turn to shut down the mill. Wanting to get home and sleep early, we did not check one another at all during the two-person separation-of-powers inspection. When Roy read the final step from outside the door—“Safety pin”—I felt the empty hole in the main shaft, but lied because I was afraid of being scolded.
“Pin, engaged.”
“Pin, engaged. Record.”

We hastily signed our names in the duty ledger. According to the record, the two operators had mutually verified one another, and the procedure was flawless. Until a flash flood broke out late that night and forcibly drove the waterwheel into motion. Without the iron pin to protect it, the millstone spun freely and caught fire, nearly burning down the entire mill.
At dawn the next morning, Gallon looked over the wreckage and held up the duty ledger as he questioned us.

Just as Gallon was about to take the record to the town for verification, Yuna stepped out from the corner. Looking at the ledger being treated as flawless evidence, she said, “That afternoon I found the pin cracked. I was afraid something would happen on the night shift, so I ran to town to have a blacksmith weld it. I didn’t get it back before dark.”

She did not expose the lie we had written in the sign-in ledger. She only used one present and certain fact to drag the source of the accident onto herself. At that moment, shame burned across the back of my neck like fire, but I didn’t even have the courage to look at her.

Gallon looked deeply at Yuna, then at the duty ledger in his hand. He did not write what Yuna had just said into the report. If he recorded it and assigned blame, this safety record, signed “compliant”

by two operators and supposedly a perfect reflection of what had happened, would become forged evidence when the missing pin could not be accounted for. The town would revoke the mill’s license outright.
In front of us, he brushed his oil-stained finger across the perfect sign-in page.
“Report the repair to the town.” He locked the ledger heavily inside a drawer. “The gears jammed from age. The pin was in the hole the entire night.”
A low hum from the cooling fan at the bottom of the cabinet pulled me back to reality.
The final verification in the underground node room had gone through.

No personal consent form appeared on the screen. Estelle had entered the lookup code used to trace the source of this batch of shell templates. The system pierced through the many public contracts at the surface, and at the bottom of the provenance chain for the batch master returned only one cold prompt.

“Archive 404 (original rights holder: Y): Original underlying record of shell template.
Status: Ownership of this template was forcibly overwritten by the

highest authority in the facility’s seventh year.
Overwrite operation serial number: A-773-9092.
Legal consent field invocation signature: [Sera_Archivist_Core]”
Estelle lowered her head. The pen that had been hovering above the book suddenly stopped. She stared fixedly at the operation serial number on the screen and the signature beneath it.

“A-773-9092…” she murmured. The pen point left an ink blot where it stopped on the paper. As an investigator in the Church records office, she knew this string of numbers and the invocation signature beneath it all too well.
“All the ‘Continuation Contract’ notices posted in Bluestone Square have this same anti-counterfeiting registration number in the lower-right corner.” She raised her head and looked at
me. “In the Empire’s system architecture, the same globally unique serial number can correspond to only one underlying operation. Look here: ‘legal consent field invocation signature.’”

That meant the system operation that produced those so-called “voluntary recruitment contracts” was the same operation that stripped the original rights holder of Archive 404 of ownership of the shell template.

No one had to forge a consent form, and no one had to sign under another person’s name—because in the “legal consent” field the supposed candidates were required to sign, the system had forcibly inserted an

execution command using Sera’s stolen program signature. Behind those public contracts covered in compliance stamps lay the brutal fact that someone had been robbed of ownership of an entire set of shell blueprints.

She drew a deep breath and wrote “Overwrite serial number: A-773-9092” in the first column of the record book. In the second column, “Independent corroboration,” she wrote “Pending.” She left the third column, “Original rights holder’s name,” blank as well.
“The name of the original rights holder of Archive 404 has been completely erased. Only an incomplete letter code remains.” Estelle looked at the screen and stated it objectively. “Y.”
I stared at the capital letter.
The status displayed on the screen was the facility’s seventh year, clearly an old-era designation. Reason told me it was only a code. It could represent anyone swallowed by the system. But in a
world where she had never been born, in a place where the entire village had no memory of her, seeing that solitary letter and the brutal record of the ownership stripped away behind it still sent
an uncontrollable shiver through me. It was like a hollow gouged out by force from a seemingly complete picture of reality, silently reminding me of the logic by which this system truly operated.

“Without independent corroboration, I can’t arbitrarily give this code a name.” She crisply closed the record book, without fabricating any conclusion on paper. “Our original plan was to use the overdue record on the requisition slip to draw the elders here as witnesses. But I’ve changed my mind.”
She looked at the system operation that had forcibly borrowed Sera’s signature.
“Evidence involving tampering at the core level won’t be acknowledged by the elders. They may even destroy it here underground.” She shoved the record book into her bulletproof vest. “We
have to get back to the village before they track us here and drive this result into the iron cabinet in the archive room. The way we came is too far. We’ll take the maintenance route.”

After leaving the node room, we followed the collapsed areas along the edge of the ruins and found an old maintenance exit. Returning the way we had come would mean crossing several hours of labyrinth again, and we could easily run into patrolling guards. To have the evidence archived before the final deadline, we had to take the shortest route.

At the end of the corridor, we found the heavy airtight door. I pulled down the largest lever with all my strength. With a dull grinding of metal, the airtight door slowly opened, revealing the maintenance

shaft leading to the surface. In the dim light, I scanned the interlock markings of the hydraulic locks on the doorframe and fixed the order for releasing their pressure in reverse from the outside in my mind.

When we climbed out of the shaft, the night wind was already cold. The shaft exit happened to lie behind a steep cut in the mountainside, in the shadow beyond the sweep of the searchlights. To force open the old cover that had been locked shut from inside, we had to crudely destroy its interlocking frame with a pry bar.

The moment Estelle left the shelter, she pulled the four strips of barrier cloth serving as a physical double safeguard from her tactical vest. Without hesitation, she stuffed them tightly into both ear canals, then put on the heavy soundproofing headset and locked the metal clasps firmly behind her ears.

We had left the heavy protection of the underground base. From now until we returned to the village, she was exposed once again to the lethal angle of Kane’s portable sonic black box. The slightest sound leak while moving—even the faintest voiceprint resonance—would be enough to make good on her death.
I climbed out after her and looked back. The edge of the cover was badly deformed, with a glaring gap pried upward.

“The cover doesn’t close properly. Anyone passing by will immediately be able to tell that someone just came out from inside.” She lowered her voice and pressed her fingers against the edge of the soundproofing headset to check the seal.

“This area will definitely be completely sealed off tomorrow morning.” I gently set the pry bar in the grass. “But opening this direct route from outside is the only way we can get in ahead of them next time.”

There was nothing more to say. In the oppressive silence, where even breathing was restrained, Estelle signaled for cover. We kept close to the shadows along the rock face, alert to every high point where pursuers might be hiding, and slipped back toward the village through the night.
The clock in the records office ticked.
Sera looked over the physical archiving application Estelle had drafted, her gaze passing across its contents.

“Subject of investigation: observed person, Arno.
Attachment One description: The inspection team crossed the physical approval boundary and entered the node room to obtain underlying data.
Attachment Two description:

By checking the anti-counterfeiting registration number A-773-9092, it has been confirmed that the forced-overwrite mechanism for the ‘body-rights attestation’ is invoking a program signature from the records office.

Fact: The underlying operation that stripped Old Experimental Area 404-Y of its body rights and the surface-level generation of the ‘Continuation Contract’ share the same serial number. The electronic system can

silently overwrite this record. This paper document will be permanently retained.
Person acknowledging the unauthorized boundary crossing and accepting punishment: __________
Person authorizing archiving: __________”

Sera’s fingers struck twice against the line describing the program signature. That morning, outside the ruins, she had already learned from us that her signature was being borrowed covertly. Now, the evidence retrieved through this unauthorized investigation had established exactly where that mechanism lay.
“So it isn’t only being hidden in an attachment. They’re using my program’s authority to underwrite the theft of the original body’s ownership.” Her voice grew heavy as she pressed the
order against the desk. “I’ll accept this part of the facts. If you had only reported it to me verbally, I would have privately recognized this unauthorized verification as legitimate.”
She raised her eyes to the investigator across the desk.

“But what you want now is to turn it into a physical record in black and white.” Sera tapped the bottom of the application with her finger. “To turn the black box completely into a record, there can be no procedural ambiguity. I maintain the system boundary. I cannot

officially endorse an unauthorized crossing in writing. If this is to be archived, you, as the investigator, must sign this acknowledgment of violation and take responsibility. As for the two-person access records in the electronic system, with this paper penalty

notice as cover, I can disguise them as an operational error committed by you alone. And the ‘observed person’ beside you, who does not even have investigative authorization, I’ll remove entirely from my internal report and treat this as a mess you made by yourself.”

Sera shook her head, her tone carrying a harsh warning. “Once the violation is established, the Church will directly revoke your permission to act alone. From then on, every step you take outside the White Tower

will have guards following close behind. For an accusation with no independent corroboration, you would trade your own mobility for a case file that can never be silently deleted. Have you thought this through?”
The ticking of the clock echoed through the silent records office.

Estelle’s eyes remained on the order for a long time. An investigator accustomed to moving like a ghost through ruins and dark corners, she knew better than anyone what “round-the-clock surveillance” meant. It was the only mobility she had for seeking the truth in this world full of dangers.
But she did not retreat.

“The underlying electronic data can be flattened again at any time through their maintenance interface. Only a physical record cannot be deleted by a string of code. Independent corroboration doesn’t matter. As long as this page bearing our signatures enters the iron cabinet, they can forget about pretending none of this ever happened.”
She reached out and took the pen.

“Add my name.” I stepped forward and placed my hand on the desk. “You entered the commands on the main keyboard. I confirmed the boundary-crossing warning. If someone has to carry this, it belongs to both of us.”

My voice sounded a little dry in the quiet records office. A few hours earlier, in my memory, I had been too ashamed to look at Yuna because I had tried to escape responsibility at the mill. Now I did not want to hide behind someone who was taking the blame for me.
Estelle turned to look at me. A flicker of surprise passed through her eyes. But she immediately tapped the back of my hand lightly with the pen cap and pushed my hand away from the desk.

“Stop getting in the way. If Sera puts you in the violation report, the White Tower will throw you, an unaffiliated nobody, out of the village tomorrow.” She did not look at me, turning her gaze back to the paper. “I’ll only be restricted in my mobility. At least I can stay here and keep investigating.”
In the “Person acknowledging the unauthorized boundary crossing and accepting punishment” field, Estelle firmly signed her own name, surrendering her freedom.
Sera looked at the signature, sighed silently, and turned the order around. In the “Person authorizing archiving” field, she signed the two characters “Sera.”
Before the day’s settlement point arrived in this world, the permanent-retention attachment bearing an investigator’s future was locked inside the iron cabinet deep in the archive room.

When we left the records office and stood in the dim corridor, Estelle suddenly stopped. She leaned against the cold stone wall, as though she had finally released the tension she had been forcing herself to hold.

“Although I don’t know who that code Y was.” She looked toward the end of the dark corridor, a trace of real exhaustion in her voice. “No living person should ever be torn out by the roots and reduced to a string of numbers like that.”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:title: Chapter 22 Appendix: I’ll Let You Verify
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s1-1:
Continuance Contract · Matters the Candidate Must Agree To (final-review edition):
“1. Scan of the current complete writable personality state.
2. Identity inherited by the new body.
3. Original body enters final disposition.
4. Body specifications determined by the Maintenance Desk.
—The candidate must agree to all four items.”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s6-1: Let’s go back more than a dozen hours, to when we had not yet taken that order sheet to illegally touch the experimental area's underlying hardware.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s7-1: The time was 08:40 that morning. After hearing my review of the previous round and going alone to the White Tower to verify the records, Estelle pushed open the door to the Church records office and formally submitted a complaint concerning her bodily rights. Cold air drifted through the room.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s8-1: In response, the elder presiding over the ceremony took a final-review draft of the Continuance Contract from a drawer. For the first time, the specific clauses requiring signatures were placed directly in front of Estelle.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s9-1: The first two were routine procedures required to maintain continuity of identity. Estelle’s gaze swept over them quickly. But when it fell on the third item, it stopped.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s10-1: I had once summarized its meaning to her as “discarded,” but the wording in the contract itself was colder, and more ambiguous.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s12-1: “Third item. Original body enters final disposition.” She repeated the words softly, then raised her head. “So what, specifically, is the disposition?”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s14-1: “Administrative terminology. Literal meaning.” Sera answered without a ripple. “That is outside your inspection authority today. You only need to know that you will continue in this world.”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s15-1: Estelle was silent for two seconds. Her gaze moved to the final line, and she decided to try another opening she could verify.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s17-1: “Fine. Then the fourth item. Body specifications determined by the Maintenance Desk. Where, specifically, are those specifications written?”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s20-1: Sera pulled a yellowing specification sheet from between the thick booklet's pages and pushed it across the table. It was a public form. Estelle took it and scanned it with extreme speed.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s21-1: The public form contained only a few lines describing the new body: height, a weight range, and basal metabolic rate. There was no description of the endocrine system, no neural-interface permissions, and even the field for expected lifespan was completely blank.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s23-1: “These are all the specification parameters listed here. There are only this many.”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s24-1: She pressed her fingertip hard against the final thick black line on the public form, then looked up at the Continuance Contract waiting for her fingerprint.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s26-1: “I’m sitting here today to sign this contract in the end. I want to confirm that the actual contents attached to these clauses are limited to what appears on this form.”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s27-1: The air in the room grew viscous. Only the second hand on the wall clock continued its tireless movement.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s30-1: In the suffocating silence, I abruptly spoke up and gave a sixteen-digit system number beginning with “RX-7.”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s32-1: “That isn’t an ordinary code from the public form. It’s the hidden attachment’s unique version number in the underlying system.” I met Sera’s startled gaze. “The contract in your hands is only the outer shell. According
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s32-2: to the automated process, as soon as this contract enters the pending-signature state, the system will use this version number to secretly attach an underlying file concerning the candidate, bypassing your desk.”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s34-1: “How can a guide from a village see data at this level of access?” Sera's hand, moving to take back the sheet, stopped in midair.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s35-1: This was a trump card I had pieced together through repeated exploration and trial and error around the ruins in the more than ten worlds where I had failed to change the outcome. But at this moment, I had to fabricate a source for it that could not be disproved for now.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s37-1: “In the terminal at the old guard room outside the disaster-recovery station, I saw the logs through a classification flaw.” I answered in a low voice, throwing this intelligence
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s37-2: accumulated across multiple rounds onto the table as a bargaining chip. “The call records showed not only this version number, which is generated along with the surface
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s37-3: contract, but also its file size. It was dozens of times larger than the form in your hands, and it was marked as a secret dossier sent directly to the Maintenance Desk.”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s38-1: Estelle took over, fixing the elder across the table with her gaze. “If a secret dossier has been attached, it must have left traces in the system. We have reason to suspect that this hidden attachment is secretly bound to my consent form.”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s39-1: She pushed the contract waiting for her fingerprint another inch forward.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s41-1: “If you truly believe this ceremony is fair, why not go to the secure records room now and use your elder credentials to look up this version number? See what, exactly, the routing diagram for that hidden attachment has done to my body.”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s45-1: As the elder presiding over the ceremony, she could easily have sent an administrator outside to make the trip. She did not. Without a word, she stood, pulled the dedicated key from the reader slot on the table, and walked straight out the door.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s46-1: A few minutes later, hurried footsteps sounded again in the corridor. Sera pushed open the door and came in with a lower-layer routing diagram freshly printed from the secure records room. She sat down at the table, her face ashen.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s48-1: “I don’t have permission to access the body of this hidden attachment.” She stared at the diagram, her voice cold as ice. “But the trigger-condition list on the routing
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s48-2: diagram clearly shows two reserved positions for mandatory credentials. One is your candidate fingerprint credential. The other is an interface call to my procedural signature.”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s49-1: Sera spread the routing diagram across the center of the long table and pressed the tip of her pen hard against the red circle around the final step.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s51-1: “The system specifications are very clear. If the process does not involve depriving the original body or altering the conditions of continuance, ordinary body inheritance does not need to call on my procedure in addition to the candidate’s fingerprint for dual authorization. The presiding party is only required to intervene when control is transferred completely.”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s54-1: Estelle's finger, which had been hovering above the contract, jerked back. She looked at the draft waiting for her signature as if it were an electrified metal plate.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s56-1: “This surface contract and the underlying RX-7 attachment are bound to the same execution pipeline.” Sera slapped the pen down on the table. “As soon as you leave your fingerprint on this paper, the system will determine that you have tacitly agreed to every hidden
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s56-2: condition in the background. Immediately afterward, my procedural signature will be retrieved automatically. They trick your consent away, then use my authority as a stamping machine to forge a fully compliant bilateral authorization in the underlying system.”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s59-1: Sera said nothing more. She pulled a formal limited, deniable procedural audit order from the drawer, spread it across the table, and rapidly wrote on it.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s61-1:
Authorized data directories: Contract Specification Section. Candidate Disposition Index. Body Rights Witnessing Section.
Authorized inspector: Candidate Estelle. Accompaniment: Not approved.
This order is limited to routine system access. Anything beyond this scope is not authorized.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s63-1: She pushed the inked audit order toward Estelle. The wall clock had only just passed 09:00.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s67-1: “I’ll let you verify the sections I’m asking you to sign today.” She held Estelle’s gaze, though her peripheral vision passed over me. “I didn’t approve an escort. As for how you cross the dangerous
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s67-2: perimeter of the acoustic barrier, or whether some unrelated guide illegally follows you, that is beyond what this paper can control. But this is only a routine data-access order. If what you need
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s67-3: to inspect isn’t in the surface terminal, and you go to the underlying hardware on your own in order to find it… Step even half a pace beyond this paper’s authority, and I will not protect you.”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s70-1: Estelle reached out, took the order sheet, folded it neatly in half, and tucked it carefully into her booklet.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s72-1: “Understood. If I cross the line, I won’t say I was acting on your orders, either. I’m going to investigate this for myself.”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s75-1: Sera pushed open the door and left. The heavy wooden door closed behind her. Only the two of us remained in the records office.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s76-1: With this rare approval in hand, Estelle did not get up at once. Her gaze remained fixed on the third item in the final-review draft.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s79-1: She did not curse aloud. She only gripped her own arm tightly, her fingertips paling slightly from the pressure.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s81-1: “‘Original body enters final disposition.’” She repeated it softly, then turned to face me. Her eyes were slightly red, but her gaze was hard as iron. “I want to live, Arno.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s81-2: But I will never hand myself over to a form I haven’t even been allowed to see. I also need to see with my own eyes exactly how they intend to ‘dispose of’ this body of mine.”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s82-1: I watched her. Facing this thin document, her fingertips remained locked tightly around the back of her hand, refusing to loosen.
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s84-1: “I’m not going to talk you out of it.” I turned the false public specification sheet on the table over and pressed it face down against the tabletop. “I’ll go in with you. We’ll drag the black box behind these four words completely into the light.”
texts.chapter:v15-22c:event:text-s85-1: Only after hearing that did she relax slightly. She drew a deep breath and stood.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:title: Chapter Twenty-Two, Supplement Three: Within the Scope of Approval
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s1-1:
Body Rights Witnessing Area · Signboard at the Counter (AI Laboratory Perimeter, Candidates May Enter):
“This area provides demonstration materials for candidates to verify item by item according to
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s1-2:
their own rights.
　A witness may be requested to attend during verification. The witness certifies that the verification itself has taken place.
　The witness does not judge the content being verified.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s6-1: The limited audit order Sera issued that morning approved three data directories, item by item, in black and white. Beneath the precise restriction at the end—“Routine access only”—it also clearly stated, “Escort: Not approved.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s7-1: It was just past one in the afternoon. Less than eleven hours remained before the White Tower’s Internal Affairs Office’s ultimatum: she had to sign by midnight at the latest.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s8-1: Using the audit order, she quickly passed through the first two stations, their electronic files devoid of any substantive content, and stepped directly into the final station—the Body Rights Witnessing Area. I walked beside her as an unauthorized companion, protected by no permit.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s12-1: The space at the perimeter of the Witnessing Area was not large. A long table ran across the center, with a set of physical demonstration materials placed on its surface. Thin copper strips pressed down the edges of every page.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s13-1: There were six books in all.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s14-1: She stepped forward and held out a finger, hovering it over the tabletop.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s16-1: “The public explanation from this morning made it very clear. There are only four items in the process.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s17-1: Her fingertip moved along the row and stopped over the extra fifth and sixth books.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s22-1: The first four books corresponded exactly to the four items in the public explanation: “Current Complete Writable Personality State,” “Identity-Continuation Document,” “Completed Disposition,” and “Specification Document.” Of these four physical
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s22-2: books, she still lingered longest over the third, “Completed Disposition.” Her fingertips went slightly white as she opened it to the perfect demonstration phrases: “stable transition of vital signs,” “humane shutdown,” “painless release.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s23-1: She snapped the booklet shut. It made a dull sound.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s25-1: “What I want to know is the actual physical action the system performs when it executes those four words. First I need to find out what these two extra books are.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s29-1:
This one was not thin. It was dozens of pages long. Two characters were printed at the top: Parallel Reading.
Inside were densely packed blank forms. The large column on the left was labeled “New,” and the large column on the right “Old.” The
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s29-2: far-left sampling-time column was preprinted with a clear continuous scale from “Hour 1” through “Hour 72,” with a comparison box every ten minutes. In the lower-right corner of the back cover, a tiny system identification number was printed.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s35-1: “If it weren’t used, they wouldn’t have specially pressed damage-resistant copper strips over it and put it on the display stand.” Her fingers moved between the ruled boxes. “I’ve seen this term in a technical specification. When two bodies—the old
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s35-2: shell and the new flesh—are connected to life support at the same time, both awake and producing neural electrical signals, while the system reads the synchronization rate of the two streams of living data in real time, that is called ‘Parallel Reading.’”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s38-1: I looked at the dividing line between New and Old.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s40-1: “Normal transfer verification does require both the new and old ends to be online at the same time. If all that needed confirming was the instant the handoff was complete, this table would need only one row.” She pointed at
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s40-2: the blank boxes beneath “Old,” extending across seventy-two hours. “But this length means the system has reserved space to record the old shell and the new flesh remaining conscious in parallel for as long as three days.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s41-1: She drew a deep breath and forced down the tremor in her voice.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s43-1: “If both ends really produce independent consciousness and memories at the same time over those three days, then ‘continuation’ isn’t a transfer of consciousness.” Her finger stopped on the book titled “Completed Disposition.” “It copies a version of me into the new body, and leaves these four words for the old one.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s46-1:
In the suffocating silence, she closed the fifth book and reached for the final, sixth one.
The sixth book was almost nothing but a cover, with a single sheet of paper tucked inside. The cover read: Conditional Appendix (Filed Separately). The same tiny system identification number was printed at the lower right of the title.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s47-1: She opened the only page. In black and white, it contained only three cold lines:
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s49-1:
The conditions contained in this volume shall be adjusted together with the authorization document.
This volume shall not be presented with the contract.
Access: approval by the issuing seat.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s53-1: She stared for a while at the two identification numbers on the back cover of the fifth book and the cover of the sixth.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s54-1: Just over four hours earlier, I had reported to Sera a string of sixteen-digit system call codes beginning with “RX-7.” Sera had used those identifiers to trace the flow of
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s54-2: the hidden appendices. Now Estelle pulled the two extra demonstration materials closer and pressed her fingertip against the two tiny lines of characters on their covers.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s55-1:
The fifth book was marked: RX-7-B-SYNC.
The sixth book was marked: RX-7-C-COND.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s57-1: “The category prefix is the same as the sixteen-digit call code from this morning. They’re both RX-7.” Her finger moved slowly across the two identifiers. “These
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s57-2: eleven characters are desensitized general dossier codes. These two appendices hidden beneath the process are the ghost we saw on the call list this morning.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s60-1: She spread the slip on the tabletop. Beneath the four items from that morning, she took up her pen, drew two new boxes, and wrote “Parallel Reading” and “Conditional Appendix,” leaving them empty.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s64-1: “If there’s a reserved slot for Sera’s authorization on those, can’t we go back and ask her to issue a new order for these two identification numbers?”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s66-1: “No.” She spread the limited audit order flat on the table. “This access order was issued on the premise of ‘routine system access.’ If unexpected data appeared during a normal process, she could issue an order directly. But if she took these two identifiers
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s66-2: from the deepest layer of the system and issued an access order for them, the system record would be an admission to the White Tower’s monitoring network—that she had crossed beyond the routine process and probed a black box she was not supposed to know about.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s67-1: She looked at the two newly drawn boxes.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s69-1: “The issuing seat has the authority to approve things within the framework preset by the system, but no freedom to probe the framework itself. I can’t drag her into this.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s72-1: She turned and walked quickly to the wooden cabinet beside the door. A delivery slot was open in its face, with a thick wooden placard nailed below it.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s74-1:
Candidates shall submit applications here.
All requests to expand the scope of access shall be forwarded by this area to the issuing seat.
A response shall be issued no later than seven working days from the date of forwarding.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s76-1: A few minutes later, Toma pushed open the door and entered. He was wearing maintenance clothes and carrying the routine inspection log Gallon had assigned. He glanced at Estelle, but his gaze seemed to pass straight through me where I stood beside her, without stopping or showing surprise.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s77-1: Just before he entered, I had checked a low-level permission rule on the terminal in the corridor: “A limited audit order does not approve unauthorized escorts, and an escort is not protected by the order; however, the inspection sequence is responsible only for recording authorized access credentials and has no authority to expel entities.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s78-1: In other words, he had seen me. But as long as I did not interfere with the process, I was a mass of air that did not need to exist in his logbook.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s80-1: “I’d like you to witness two things.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s81-1: She walked to the six physical booklets, picked up the first, opened it, and closed it again. The movement was clean and decisive. Then the second, the third, all the way through the sixth, opening and closing each one again.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s83-1: “First, the public explanation lists only four items, but I have actually opened six demonstration books here.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s84-1: Toma’s sharp gaze swept across the tabletop. He immediately lowered his head and wrote a line in the book: “Candidate verifies six demonstration materials.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s90-1: “Second, I’d also like you to witness that the fifth demonstration book doesn’t even contain demonstration data. It’s entirely blank.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s91-1: Toma’s pen tip hovered over the page.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s93-1: “I can’t record that. I’m only responsible for witnessing that the action of your ‘opening six books’ has taken place.” He tapped the bold words printed at the top of his record book with the shaft of his pen. They were
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s93-2: identical to the words on the signboard by the door: “The witness does not judge the content being verified.” “Whether there are words in the fifth book is content. I don’t understand it, and I have no authority to witness it.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s97-1: “Then who is responsible for the content?”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s99-1: “The seat that issued the access permission.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s101-1: “But the order I have was issued by her. If the person who issued it can’t see the content either, who is supposed to be responsible for it?”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s102-1: Toma’s hands stopped moving. He looked at her intently from across the long table.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s104-1: “Then you can only follow the formal route. Submit a request to expand the scope of access at the cabinet, and have them forward it to the issuing seat.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s107-1: He closed the book and turned to leave. Just before crossing the threshold, he stopped.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s109-1: “Candidate. I’ve only met one person before who insisted on checking the details as thoroughly as you do.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s112-1: Toma stood in the shadow by the door, his voice flat.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s115-1: His footsteps gradually receded down the corridor, their dull echoes fading behind him.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s118-1: The Witnessing Area fell silent again.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s119-1:
She turned, tore off a sheet of paper, and wrote: “I verified six demonstration materials today. I request that the scope of access be expanded to the actual data of the fifth and sixth books.”
When she finished, she signed decisively, folded the paper in half, and slid it through the narrow slot in the wooden cabinet. The slip fell inside with a soft sound.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s123-1: “You’ve already seen that this appeals mechanism is a deadlock meant to block internal verification. Why submit it anyway? It says no later than seven working days. If it’s forwarded automatically, Sera might see it tomorrow.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s125-1: “That’s exactly why I want her to see it tomorrow. This will become the cause for her to access the fifth and sixth books lawfully.” Her hand slid weakly down from the slot. “But that won’t be my concern anymore. By the time this application reaches Sera’s desk tomorrow, I’ll most likely already have been pressed into tomorrow morning’s oath ceremony.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s128-1: Before leaving, she turned back for one last look at the long table.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s130-1: “Arno, do you know what’s most frightening about reaching this point?”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s134-1: “That if I stop now, if I don’t obtain conclusive data, I might actually sign.”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s137-1: “A hundred years of political privilege could bring medical care and clean water to Watermarsh. That’s what I want most. I was only able to work out that ‘copy the original, then kill it’ theory here
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s137-2: because it’s one in the afternoon and the pen hasn’t been placed in my hand yet. If I go back relying only on this bit of circumstantial speculation, and at midnight face that very real benefit…”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s138-1: She stared at the empty doorway.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s140-1: “I know too well how fiercely I want Watermarsh to survive. If I don’t drive the words ‘I really will be killed’ into my own face with the hardest evidence, I’m afraid I’ll trick myself into signing by telling myself, ‘Maybe the system isn’t that bad.’”
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s143-1: Back in the long corridor, she opened the booklet again and pressed her fingertip hard against the two system identification numbers she had just written down.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s144-1: The lawful route through the counter had been completely blocked by the deadline of no later than seven working days. Since the routine process could not provide an answer, she could only investigate the black boxes she was not supposed to investigate. She tucked the booklet under her arm and raised her head toward the depths of the corridor.
texts.chapter:v15-22d:event:text-s145-1: That was why, that afternoon, in order to obtain irrefutable proof before surrendering to the temptation within her, we ultimately gripped those two identification numbers, crossed beyond the relatively safe perimeter area, and headed toward the heavily sealed Cross-Index door.
texts.chapter:v15-22b:title: This Room Came First
texts.chapter:v15-22b:event:text-s5-1: Estelle stopped in front of the heavily sealed cross-index door.
texts.chapter:v15-22b:event:text-s6-1: This door was the endpoint given by the central index terminal on the level above. The physical retrieval route indicated by the two file identifiers was cut off here by a cast-iron wall. A red light blinked on the access panel, indicating that this area lay beyond the inspection order’s authority.
