texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s86-1: “This order is single-use. Return it after use.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s89-1: We stopped in the corridor. The clock on the wall pointed to 8:40.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s90-1: The audit order stated plainly that I was to accompany her without signing. That meant that from the moment Estelle crossed the threshold, every thing she did and every line she crossed would go on her own account.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s93-1: She put the order away and said she wanted to go to the rehearsal room first. I asked what she was going there for.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s95-1: “You wait outside.” She pointed toward the rehearsal-room door. “Until nine.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s96-1: She stayed inside for twenty minutes. At exactly nine, the smell of purple sealing wax seeped thread by thread through the solid wooden door. It was the rosin-scented sealing wax specially supplied to the candidate rehearsal rooms, with a slightly acrid bite.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s97-1: When she pushed the door open, both her hands were empty.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s101-1: “Twelve black-and-white markers. From the draw box—I shook it myself.” She looked at me. “I recorded them one by one and sealed them.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s108-1: She refused in an utterly even voice.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s110-1: “If you see them, this evidence won’t be valid later.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s114-1: “You only need to know one thing.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s115-1: She lifted her chin slightly and tilted it toward the closed door.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s117-1: “In the rehearsal room, the writing desk. Second drawer on the left. I put them together with yesterday afternoon’s wax seal containing the carbon core.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s121-1: At exactly nine, we left the village and headed north.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s122-1: At that time, the AI laboratory’s perimeter was still covered by an ordinary repellent sound field specifically used to drive away wild animals. Estelle’s steps stopped
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s122-2: without warning when she reached the edge of the perimeter. She looked up at the broadcast pillar above, instinctively took half a step back, and reached for her temples.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s123-1: “Even the ordinary repellent setting causes severe dizziness in peripheral-lineage people who retain a voiceprint interface,” I said beside her. “There’s a sealed maintenance earmuff in that equipment case. Put it on to cross, then switch off the silence field.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s124-1: She pressed her temples and glanced at me. She did not ask how I knew about the peripheral lineage or the voiceprint interface. She simply walked over, opened the old equipment case beside the quarantine tape, took out a sealed maintenance earmuff, checked its insulation rating, and fitted it over her head.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s125-1: She followed the old broadcast pillar to the edge of the sound field, endured the lingering discomfort, placed her hand on the exposed silence switch, and turned on the safety light on its outer side. Only then did she turn back and gesture for me to come over.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s126-1: I remembered the shape of every weathered stone along the way and every fork in the road with absolute clarity. But for me standing there, it was the first time my feet had stepped onto the soil.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s128-1: The heavy iron cover over the shaft was sealed tightly in this world, with two moss-covered stones weighing down its edge. I stepped forward and moved them aside. The rough stone scraped a bloody gash across the back of my hand.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s129-1: After we descended the shaft, there were several heavy mechanical door locks. Estelle held the flashlight behind me, its beam fixed hard on the rusted locks.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s138-1: She did not ask anything else. The beam remained just as steady.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s141-1: By the time I twisted open the last lock, I was drenched in sweat. I leaned against the cold wall, exhausted, gulping air.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s142-1: Estelle turned off half the flashlight and stood with her back against the damp shaft wall. Today she wore an ordinary windbreaker over her clothes, but the zipper was not fully closed, leaving the entire dark local candidate uniform plainly visible beneath it—in this world, she was still a candidate with a formal seat.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s144-1: “I won’t stop you from doing what you’re going to do once we’re inside.” Her voice carried a slight echo through the passage. “But there’s one thing I have to say first.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s149-1: “Whoever comes out of there—whether she carries memories exactly identical to mine.” She looked at me. “She absolutely cannot automatically take my name, and she certainly cannot take my nameplate.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s153-1: “She can claim a name for herself. But if she walks through this village using mine, then what she takes is the place I’ve survived in all these years.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s154-1: She raised a hand and forcefully lifted the hem of her coat, exposing the plate tied at her waist. It was a heavy wooden candidate nameplate, its brass edging rounded smooth by fingers. Her name was carved on the front; the year she had qualified was carved on the back.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s156-1: “It says what year I passed the initial screening and when I obtained my candidate qualification. Fourteen, on the day of the first snow.” She stared at me. “If she takes this plate, she takes every inch of bone I’ve endured from that day to now.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s159-1: I looked at the nameplate shining faintly in the dim light and said okay.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s161-1: “Write it down.” She fixed her eyes on me. “Take out your notebook.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s162-1: By the half-light she cast over me, I rested the notebook on my aching knee and wrote a line with fingers stiff from the cold.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s164-1: A newcomer may not automatically inherit a local name or nameplate. Personal statement; not drafted by me.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s166-1: She leaned close and looked down at the page.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s168-1: “What do the words ‘not drafted by me’ mean?”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s170-1: “It means this rule was declared by you yourself. I didn’t overstep and think it up for you.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s171-1: She stared at those three words for a while.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s178-1: I spread Sera’s limited audit order flat on the operating console and entered it manually into the terminal. The interface flickered, changing from “Forbidden” to a green “Review Mode.” The order was the only key to entering the Bodily Rights Witnessing Area, but it approved only half the permissions.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s179-1: Estelle went around me and called up the query interface on the main screen. She dug downward through the lower-level links of the Bodily Rights Witnessing Area.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s180-1: The “Maintenance Appendix Four” Sera had never seen and Estelle had claimed she wanted to investigate was finally retrieved from the hidden area. Two lines of undecorated system plaintext appeared on the screen:
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s181-1: Special authorization: without the subject’s secondary authorization, the system may forcibly invoke candidate body parameters to generate a physical backup entity.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s182-1: She stared fixedly at the two lines. This was what Sera had signed for twenty years without ever seeing.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s184-1: “So anyone who knows how to bypass the hardware lock can use my parameters to make a person?” Her voice tightened slightly.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s185-1: “Yes.” I crawled under the console and pried open a metal panel with a screwdriver. On the back of the panel was a faded maintenance warning: “Caution: after the main control board loses power, the write-protection relay closes with a five-second delay. Do not mistakenly connect the backup drive during this dead zone.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s186-1: “The order does say not to access or overwrite source-world records.” I disconnected the main control board’s power cable and pulled the
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s186-2: backup-drive line beside the main interface, leaving it suspended. “But what the order forbids is retrieval through the system’s ordinary procedures—the
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s186-3: hardware-direct ‘generation’ channel is something Sera doesn’t know exists. So she can’t forbid a low-level command she doesn’t know about.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s187-1: “During this five-second dead zone, whatever error the motherboard reports, the hardware is passing through directly. If we forcibly sever the peripheral voiceprint-control data line, she won’t be subject to that peripheral neural suppression anymore.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s188-1: The moment the screen alarm appeared, I used those five seconds of hardware dead time to bypass the routine permission checks. A fully sealed source file synchronized from that world last night was forcibly called up, bypassed the review interface, and mounted into the lower-level system’s print queue.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s189-1: The red light flashed rapidly, then finally turned green. The system began requesting local carrier parameters.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s190-1: “She gave this place the only allotment.” I looked at the terminal as it pulsed and spoke to Estelle. “The machine itself doesn’t limit the number of writes, but she fixed the bottom line in that authorization: I’m allowed to perform one and only one physical
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s190-2: generation at the next station. Once she opens her eyes on this platform, I’ll erase the cross-world source file I brought here completely, as she requested. If the higher-ups dispose of her afterward, you’ll never be able to produce a second piece of evidence.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s191-1: She watched the reader board blinking green. Beneath the error code, a prompt appeared on the terminal screen: “Unauthorized direct connection detected. Physical generation will trigger an indelible low-level log burn.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s192-1: “If I don’t make her, and I take this single-use order back and report it now”—she stared at the plaintext on the screen—“the higher-ups only need to delete those two lines of the appendix from
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s192-2: the back end, add another lock, and seal the file in Sera’s hands. Then I’ll be the only person who has seen the lower levels, and I’ll become a lunatic who fabricated a rumor out of thin air.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s193-1: She took off the ordinary coat and draped it over the cold chair back beside her, revealing the entire local candidate uniform that represented her qualification. Then she lowered her head,
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s193-2: personally removed the candidate nameplate from her waist, and laid it flat on the console. After that, she stepped directly onto the reader board and pressed her palm against the scanning area.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s194-1: “Make it.” She listened to the system begin reading her body parameters, her eyes on the indelible prompt on the screen, and did not turn around. “As long as the machine completes
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s194-2: this one and only physical generation, the lower-level read-only chip will burn in this timestamped generation log, along with the process by which it called Appendix Four. Put this
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s194-3: body in front of everyone, and they’ll have to explain in public why this body that walked out of the black box can call a lower-level code bearing a compliant signature from Sera.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s195-1: She stepped back to a position with a clear view of the writing platform and stood there, her hands naturally folded in front of her.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s197-1: “Write. Use up this one and only allotment.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s200-1: The writing process took a long forty minutes.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s201-1: The progress bar on the screen moved down one cell at a time. At certain points it stopped abruptly, requiring a manual press of the control panel to confirm. I pressed it six times in all. Estelle remained where she was without shifting even her center of gravity.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s202-1: A little before eleven, there was finally movement on the platform.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s203-1: At first, an extremely faint breathing sound. The machine had generated only a basic layer of white synthetic fabric for her, clinging tightly to her newly formed skin.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s204-1: Quietly, I moved the notebook I had been holding from my right hand to my left and clutched it tightly against the side closest to my heart.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s205-1: The person on the platform did not rise immediately. She lay there quietly and looked at the ceiling for a while.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s206-1: Her lips moved. Her voice was as hoarse as sandpaper, but every word was bitten out clearly.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s208-1: “This morning, in the rehearsal room. Noon, the AI laboratory.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s209-1: I stood as if nailed in place, my hand still resting on the cold control panel. I did not move it.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s210-1: After speaking those coordinates, her eyes turned slowly. Her focus finally gathered, and she found me standing over here.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s212-1: “This morning, in the rehearsal room in that world, I shook twelve black-and-white markers myself. At noon, in the corridor, I put them in the fixed drawer beside the Writing Room in the AI laboratory.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s212-2: She looked into my eyes, her voice dry. “In that world, I originally thought that one day you might cross back again, open that drawer, and verify whether I was genuine. The first blind box I left for you.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s214-1: “But I’ve woken up inside this black box. I remember sealing off Watermarsh’s authorization channel and cutting off the way back, which also cut off the entrance for anyone else to trace back to Watermarsh through that system.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s214-2: That route is severed. The drawer will remain forever in that unreachable world; it has become a dead end. But I still have to write down these twelve positions. They’re the order I could never possibly see from inside this body.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s215-1: I opened my mouth and found that my throat was dry.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s223-1: With fingers stiff from the cold, she rapidly wrote a string of things on a blank page of the recording board beside her. Then she tore out the page and folded it twice.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s225-1: “Find a local neutral person later and put this page in their keeping. If there’s a hearing or questioning later, unfold it in public then.” Her voice
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s225-2: was dry. She pressed the note beneath the metal clip on the recording board. “But this isn’t that world. Have you checked the drawer in this world?”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s228-1: Bracing herself with both hands, she sat up on the platform. Both hands pressed hard against either side of her body. Her shoulders exerted themselves first to lift her weight; her head rose last.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s230-1: “No. Because the Estelle here went to the rehearsal room herself a little after eight this morning and also drew twelve markers. She sealed the local originals with purple wax and left them in the rehearsal-room drawer here.” My throat tightened.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s233-1: “Good.” She rasped out a breath. “If anyone asks someday, have her write the order on paper in front of everyone first, then open what she left in the drawer today in public. Only if the two results match exactly can
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s233-2: it prove that she sealed those memories herself, and prove that she is the one who belongs here. As for me, I can no longer prove myself to anyone. Until this blind box is opened, neither of us owes the other anything.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s239-1: After she finished that decisive final sentence, she raised her head. Her gaze passed over my shoulder and finally found the person who had been standing in the shadows by the door.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s240-1: That person wore the dark local uniform and had the same face. Since the machine began running, she had stood there without moving even an inch.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s241-1: Now two identical faces looked at each other across the dim machine room.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s242-1: I stood in the passage between them. The air in the narrow machine room was so tense it seemed ready to snap. The local Estelle instinctively stepped half a pace back. Her hand clenched into a fist at her side, her knuckles whitening under the strain.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s243-1: The one who had just awakened on the platform was the first to break the dead silence.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s245-1: “You’re wearing that uniform.” Her gaze swept over the crisp clothing, and a small resistant swallow caught in her throat. “What year did you pass the initial screening and obtain your candidate qualification?”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s247-1: “Fourteen. On the day of the first snow.” Estelle ground out the answer through her teeth.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s248-1: After hearing it, the person on the platform closed her eyes, as if digesting something bitter beyond measure.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s251-1: The person on the platform slid down from the high edge first. She stepped barefoot onto the cold metal floor, her body swaying slightly because her muscles had not yet
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s251-2: fully adapted. She walked two steps forward and barely steadied herself. Three steps from Estelle, the other person turned her gaze away in vehement refusal. She stopped.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s253-1: “I’ll start by saying what I don’t want.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s258-1: Estelle drew a deep breath, suppressing the rise and fall of her chest.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s260-1: “That’s easy for you to say,” she said coldly.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s264-1: “So I’ll say one thing that isn’t easy: not wanting your seat doesn’t mean I’m less real than you.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s267-1: Only after hearing that did Estelle’s shoulders suddenly tense.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s271-1: “You haven’t said it aloud. But all morning, you’ve been preparing for this.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s272-1: She tilted her head slightly toward where I stood.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s274-1: “That notebook against his chest has been guarded tightly at the innermost side of his left hand ever since I opened my eyes. When I woke just now, he quietly changed hands once. Before changing hands to protect the notebook, he looked at you first.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s275-1: Estelle looked past her and glanced at me.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s277-1: “How did you think to watch for a detail like that?”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s280-1: She paused for a moment before continuing with the second half.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s282-1: “If I were standing where you are and saw a replica of unknown origin wake up, the first thing I’d do would be to cover my own nameplate tightly too.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s285-1: The room fell completely silent. Only the faint hum of the cooling machine remained.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s286-1: Estelle turned, picked up the ordinary coat draped over the chair back, walked over, and handed it to the other self standing barefoot there.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s287-1: She took it. When she put it on, her movements were a little awkward. She lowered her head and smoothed the sleeve open bit by bit herself.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s289-1: “This one is yours.” She tugged at the collar.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s291-1: “The coat is mine. The uniform underneath that represents the seat absolutely cannot be given to you.” She looked at the other’s bare feet on the metal floor. “Find shoes in the storage cabinet yourself. Don’t wear mine.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s293-1: “I know.” She looked at the other’s dark local uniform, then lowered her head to look at the layer of white synthetic fabric on herself. “I find this uniform skin you use when making people disgusting too.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s297-1: “The name. I’ve been Estelle for seventeen years. I can’t peel off this skin and become someone else. So you’re Estelle, and I have to be Estelle too.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s298-1: The local Estelle suddenly raised her head, her eyes stabbing across like knives.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s300-1: “What gives you the right?” She forced the words out through clenched teeth. “Walk through the village with that name and everyone will recognize my face! If I give you the name, I’m giving you these seventeen years!”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s302-1: “That’s why I won’t touch your nameplate.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s303-1: She turned and walked to the cluttered control desk. Raising the back of her hand, she swept the accumulated dust forcefully aside, clearing a clean section of tabletop.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s305-1: “But this name is my bones. I’ll give up the name only if you smash me to pieces first. As long as the nameplate is on your waist, even if people in the village get confused, they can’t take away the seventeen
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s305-2: years you lived in that position. I won’t apply for the seat, accept it, or sign anything in someone else’s place. If someone comes someday carrying papers and asks whether I want it, I’ll say no in public.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s306-1: At that, the tension in Estelle’s clenched jaw eased slightly, but her hand remained pressed firmly over her own nameplate, yielding not an inch.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s308-1: “As long as someone calls this name, you have to prove first that you aren’t me before you can speak.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s313-1: “She has no identity.” I finally could not hold back. My voice was slightly hoarse in the narrow machine room. “All the penalties and consequences of crossing the lines today go on my account.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s314-1: The two of them turned their heads in unison. Two identical pairs of eyes looked at me together.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s316-1: “Your account?” the local Estelle said coldly. “There are two identical faces standing in this room! The moment we leave, the elders’ council will investigate my name and my appearance. What are you going to use to carry this account for us? You can’t.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s318-1: “So from now on, what you call yourself and what you call me—we decide that together.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s320-1: “No matter who you’re speaking to, use our names. I want you to get confused. Once you’re confused, you’ll be forced to stop before opening your mouth; once you stop, you’ll have to think clearly about who you’re actually speaking to.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s321-1: Estelle looked silently at the other self issuing commands in the same tone.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s329-1: “If you go back to Watermarsh along the original route, only one stamped authorization remains there, and it’s mine. If you go with this face, they absolutely won’t recognize you.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s331-1: “I’m not going back. I haven’t had a way to return across worlds to that place for a long time.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s332-1: She clenched the fingers at her side.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s334-1: “Last night, on the roof in that world, when I finished signing the nine pages of authorization filled with writing,” she looked at the other person, “I added, ‘The awakened one shall no
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s334-2: longer possess the name Estelle.’ Because I thought the Estelle who woke up would become a fake that extracted value from a dead person, so I stripped her of the name with my own hands.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s337-1: “Later, before sealing it, I suddenly understood that I couldn’t rely only on those pages that would never cross worlds with me.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s339-1: “The rules had to be carved into my mind so they could wake up together with this body. And to ensure that this cross-world data could never be secretly altered by the higher-ups or extracted without limit, the system-update channel had to be cut off at the source.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s340-1: She spoke one word at a time.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s342-1: “The me in the original world personally pressed the account-closure confirmation in the system to lock this authorization channel completely. The channel was sealed, and the record became a top-secret piece of firmware that no one could touch again.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s344-1: “She had originally only chosen to stay there and care for the abandoned blank newborn. But after pressing that button, she became an ‘already deceased’ unregistered person
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s344-2: in that system. She lost all protection as a candidate, could never use any Watermarsh facility again, and even cut off her own way to regret it and withdraw. I’m not only
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s344-3: Estelle. I’m also the one standing here after carrying the personal cost of her completely burying her legal identity over there. That’s why I will never let go of my name.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s345-1: She looked at the other person.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s347-1: “You don’t have the preparation to be treated as a black-box creation in this world like I do. From the day our paths diverged, we were never the same person again.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s349-1: She had kept her fists clenched, guarding against the other taking everything from her. But when she heard the personal price the other person had paid in exchange for this one lower-level write, the hard layer of defense in her eyes suddenly wavered.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s350-1: She opened her mouth, seeming to want to argue something, but in the end no sound came out.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s352-1: “…Let’s go.” She looked away, tied the nameplate back around her waist, and put her hands into her pockets, a trace of exhaustion impossible to conceal in her voice. “We’re already standing here.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s357-1: At 12:20, we pushed open the heavy door of the Writing Room.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s358-1: Over the previous hour, she had spent fifteen minutes teaching her newly generated limbs to stand and walk, then another fifteen writing, word by word, the boundaries they had just established
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s358-2: in the archive log at the console. During the remaining time, they searched through the changing cabinets for clothes she could wear. Apart from the necessary movements, they did not speak again.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s359-1: She shuffled along in a pair of old insulated rubber shoes found in the storage cabinet, somewhat too large for her feet. Under the sunlight, the newly formed muscles and bones still moved with a faint stiffness as they stretched under gravity.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s360-1: She walked in the middle. I was on the left; the one wearing the local candidate uniform was on the right.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s361-1: We could have taken a detour, or waited until nightfall before entering the village. But before leaving the laboratory, the local Estelle made a decision.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s362-1: “The order says we’re forbidden to bring anyone without local registration into the village.” She had zipped the borrowed coat all the way up. “If I take her in, I’m violating that order. That’s exactly why we’re going through the front gate.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s364-1: “If we hide and sneak around, then when the higher-ups catch us, she’ll be a counterfeit object they can destroy whenever they want. I’m taking her through the
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s364-2: front gate and laying the fact that we’re not the same person openly in front of everyone. I’m forcing the elders’ council to open a case and determine who she is.”
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s365-1: We followed the overgrown maintenance path back to the village boundary. The midday sun shone harshly overhead.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s366-1: When we finally pushed open the White Tower’s front door, the guards on duty awaiting the weekly review and an entire roomful of noisy candidate trainees fell silent at once.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s367-1: They did not know what had happened during that hour. They also did not know the rule written in the battered notebook against my chest.
texts.chapter:v15-29b:event:text-s368-1: They could only see two identical faces, and a nameplate hanging from one of them.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:title: Targeting (Two Estelles · That Afternoon)
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s2-1:
White Tower Front Hall · Week-End Review Duty Sheet (Today):
“Time: 13:30.
Entry: Candidate Arno, verified. Candidate Estelle, verified.
One accompanying person, no badge, no local registry status.
Appearance: Identical to the preceding candidate.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s6-1: One-thirty in the afternoon was when the White Tower front hall was busiest. Two duty officers stood behind the registration desk, Boundary Guard Kane leaned by the door checking entries and exits, seven candidate trainees stood in line to collect their teaching materials, and the deacon in charge of the materials was lifting a stack of heavy books onto the long table.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s7-1: I had thought that in a place with people coming and going, with so many trainees watching, the White Tower would at least report the anomaly according to procedure first. That was the only thing we were counting on when we dared to use the front door.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s8-1: I crossed the threshold first. The duty officer glanced at me, let his eyes rest briefly on my badge, then lowered his head and made a mark in the ledger.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s9-1: Estelle in the candidate uniform followed me through the door. She reached out and touched the wooden badge at her belt, the one that marked her identity. The duty officer glanced at it and made another mark.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s10-1: Then the third person came in. She was wrapped in the ordinary coat she had borrowed.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s11-1: One of the trainees accidentally let go of the booklet cradled against her chest. It fell onto the flagstones with a loud slap. Both duty officers’ eyes snapped toward the doorway and fixed there.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s14-1: The Estelle in the coat stopped. Slowly, she raised both hands and turned them over, showing her palms and the backs of her hands. There was nothing in them.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s17-1: The duty officer lowered his brows. His voice was hard.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s26-1: The deacon in charge of the teaching materials went pale and backed away two steps before his back met the wall. The second duty officer silently circled around behind us, his right hand clamped hard on the door bar.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s29-1: The bar slid fully into place with a dull metallic click.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s32-1: Kane moved away from the door and strode toward us.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s33-1: He walked with steady steps and stopped four or five paces away. His gaze settled first on Estelle in the candidate uniform, then shifted to the one in the coat, and finally fixed on my face.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s41-1: I looked at Kane’s granite-like face and told him she was Estelle.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s42-1: Kane slowly turned his head and looked at the one in the candidate uniform.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s47-1: He did not respond. His right hand moved habitually to his belt, and his fingertip touched the Boundary Guard’s emitter hanging there, confirming that the weapon was in place.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s48-1: Then he asked the third question in a low voice.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s50-1: “You two. Which one is the candidate?”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s53-1: The one in the candidate uniform stepped half a pace forward and raised her chin.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s56-1: The one in the coat stood quietly where she was and said nothing.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s57-1: Kane’s gaze locked onto her like a blade. He stepped closer.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s62-1: I saw the veins rise on the back of Kane’s hand around the wooden stock. An intruder with an identical face and no registry status, neither fleeing nor afraid under questioning, simply standing there.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s63-1: He yanked the emitter from his belt. The brass aperture pointed straight at the person without registry status.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s65-1: “The one without a badge. Step away from her and crouch with your hands over your head.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s66-1: The Estelle in the coat did not move.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s69-1: I understood what he intended and lunged forward. In an earlier loop, I had seen him aim the highest lethal band at Estelle. The memory of that invisible weapon making her instantly lose all support and fall backward onto the slope clenched hard around my throat.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s72-1: Kane swept his left arm across and struck me hard in the shoulder, using the force to shove me away.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s75-1: I staggered back two steps across the flagstones. Human movement was slower than a fingertip. The instant he shoved me aside, his thumb pushed decisively onto the indoor restraint setting.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s76-1: It was the lowest setting used to apprehend fugitives. He did not care that the wide fan of sound would catch the lawful candidate beside her as well.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s80-1: The dead silence in the front hall remained. There were no screams, no blood.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s81-1: Then the knees of the Estelle in the candidate uniform instantly lost their strength.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s82-1: Her whole body pitched forward. Her hand groped uselessly at empty air. The wooden badge at her waist swung violently and struck the hard table leg with a dull knock.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s83-1: The Estelle in the coat caught her in a flash.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s86-1: The witness had only completed infusion that morning, and her center of gravity was already unsteady. The impact sent both of them crashing heavily onto the flagstones. But as they fell,
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s86-2: her arm clamped around the other person’s back, using her own body as a cushion and keeping the person in her arms from being hurt at all. The two identical bodies pressed tightly together.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s87-1: Among the seven candidate trainees lined up at the long table, someone let out an incredulous gasp. They instinctively backed away, gripping their own badges tightly. The invisible restraint wave had clearly covered both people, yet the one who fell was their companion with lawful status.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s88-1: Kane’s raised arm froze in midair for one second, then dropped hesitantly. He looked at the intruder who remained conscious within the restraint wave and was still shielding her companion. Immune to the restraint wave—that triggered the highest-level anomaly in the Boundary Guard regulations, one that required immediate destruction on the spot.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s89-1: He retreated half a step and raised the weapon again.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s92-1: The Estelle shielding the other person did not look up.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s95-1: The muscles in Kane’s cheeks tightened. His gaze shifted back and forth between the two girls with the same face.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s97-1: “I said move aside. The anomalous target must be destroyed.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s98-1: She raised her eyes. Reason was set hard in her irises.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s100-1: “The one you just knocked down is the lawful candidate. Do you intend to switch to the lethal setting on two people locked together, in front of all these trainees?”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s101-1: A faint stir went through the crowd. Several trainees stared in fear at the emitter in Kane’s hand, then at their fellow candidate lying there, unable to resist.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s102-1: Kane’s left hand moved toward the other side of his belt. The brass key used to upgrade the emitter’s setting hung there. He gripped it tightly, pressing his thumb against the emitter’s lock.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s103-1: The trainee in the crowd who had been gripping his badge tightly retreated another half step. His shoe scraped across the flagstones with a sharp, grating sound. All seven pairs of eyes were fixed on Kane and the weapon in his hand.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s104-1: Sweat slid down his taut cheek. He did not dare turn the key.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s107-1: That was when Sera stepped into the front hall. She had been on the second floor and had just come down the stairs, but she had already taken in the disorder across the entire hall.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s112-1: “Elder, this one isn’t from the village. She’s immune to the restraint setting.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s115-1: She walked straight up to Kane and held out one hand. Kane gripped the wooden stock tightly, the key clenched in his left hand as well, and the two of them faced each other in the center for two seconds.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s116-1: At last, he handed it over stiffly.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s117-1: Sera took it, turned it over, and twisted a concealed catch with her thumb. There was a click. The dim markings flowing around the brass aperture went dark, and the emitter’s power was cut.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s119-1: “Seal the emitter logs from midnight today onward. Give me the upgrade key.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s122-1: Sera clenched the brass key in her hand. There was no emotion in her gray eyes.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s124-1: “Because at eight this morning, an anomalous network outage occurred in the chapel, and someone unauthorized accessed the underlying system through a backup terminal. Afterward, Boundary Guard Kane applied in advance for an upgrade to the weapon permissions for the hall’s defenses, citing an investigation into potential hazards. That matter will also be investigated as a separate case.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s125-1: She turned and looked down at the two people left on the floor. Behind the long table, the trainees whispered among themselves. Some began looking down to inspect their own badges.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s127-1: “Take them to the temporary incident review bench. Everyone else, disperse as soon as the materials have been distributed.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s133-1: The small room on the side was normally used only for checking accounts. Sera had someone tear down that week’s schedule, turn it over, and hang it back up with the blank side facing outward.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s134-1: She sat at one end of the long table. Kane sat to her left, his back straight and both hands clasped tightly over his legs. The three of us were seated across from them.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s135-1: The local Estelle had recovered from the dizziness, but cold sweat still showed against her sickly pallor. When she sat down, she undid the wooden badge at her waist with both hands and placed it evenly on the table. The front faced upward.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s136-1: Sera opened the heavy ledger and glanced at the clock on the wall.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s138-1: “Review begins. This case concerns an unregistered person forcing her way in and the White Tower’s village-protection weapon injuring a candidate. Kane, state the grounds for opening fire.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s139-1: Kane stared at the tabletop. His voice was hard and toneless.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s141-1: “I saw two people with identical faces. One with registry status and one without, traveling together. There were many people in the hall, so according to procedure I first activated the indiscriminate restraint setting in an attempt to separate them. I found that
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s141-2: the unregistered person was immune. I then intended to upgrade to the lethal setting, but the lawful candidate had already fallen and the target was pressed against her, preventing me from continuing to exercise that authority during a public safety incident.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s142-1: Sera’s pen rasped across the page. When she finished recording, she turned to the witness Estelle.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s144-1: “Unregistered person. State where you came from, and why you’re immune.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s145-1: The witness was still wearing the borrowed coat.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s147-1: “I’m Estelle too. But my conditioning interface was never connected.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s148-1: Sera looked at her, then at me.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s150-1: “An unauthorized write. Calling the source-world records, creating a second Estelle, and bringing her back to the village. Arno, in the underlying operation log of your unauthorized write, did you manually remove her voiceprint conditioning interface?”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s154-1: Sera’s pen drew a line across the register, then turned to the local Estelle.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s157-1: The local Estelle slowly raised her head.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s159-1: “If I’m a legitimate candidate from this village, why was today the first time I personally confirmed that the interface existed?”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s162-1: “Only those above the Boundary Guard rank know. It is a limit-control measure retained in your bodies. Before today, you did not need to know.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s163-1: The local Estelle gave a cold laugh.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s165-1: “And after today? Since you’ve admitted it to my face, write it into my file. I’m a candidate injured by a village-issued weapon meant to protect the village. I want this opened as a case. Investigate who exactly this unregistered person is, and why she doesn’t have this lethal code.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s166-1: Sera looked at her and drew a line in the register with her pen. Then she pulled the ledger back toward herself.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s168-1: “Boundary Guard Kane, knowing that the lawful candidate had lost the ability to act and that the target was pressed against her, nevertheless did not terminate the upgrade procedure. Afterward, he intended to use the lethal setting.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s169-1: Kane closed his eyes, and his shoulders sagged. He offered no defense.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s170-1: Sera lowered her pen and wrote.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s172-1: “A weapon intended to restrain anomalies nearly caused a grave incident in full view of the public. Suspended for reflection.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s176-1: Over the next hour or so, Sera recorded every second and every movement of the entry in exhaustive detail. At 15:30, she finally wrote down the measures to be taken.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s179-1: One: Seal the emitter logs and upgrade key; the Boundary Guard involved is suspended for reflection.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s180-1: Two: Suspend the use of any voiceprint setting on the two individuals concerned.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s181-1: Three: Local candidate Estelle to be listed as an injured candidate. Separately, record the unauthorized write as a separate case.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s182-1: Four: The review bench is adjourned. Immediately open a case under the designation ‘Candidate Continuation and Bodily Safety Incident,’ and exercise emergency archive-retrieval authority to take custody of the historical evidence. Both individuals are to report for verification in the candidate training room on the second floor.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s184-1: She set down her pen crisply.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s186-1: “We forced our way through the front door only to make the White Tower open a public case and keep her from being secretly destroyed. We didn’t account for Kane opening fire, much less for you classifying it as a ‘candidate safety incident.’”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s188-1: “If I didn’t classify it that way, this would merely be a case of identity forgery. The authority available to an ordinary case could never reach the old archives buried deepest in the system,
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s188-2: ” Sera said coldly. “Only when the current system has no way to explain in public why the body of a lawful candidate from this village contains conditioning code that can make her collapse
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s188-3: indiscriminately under a village-protection weapon can I exercise emergency archive-retrieval authority to take custody of the historical evidence in the name of responding to a safety crisis.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s189-1: Sera closed the ledger and swept her gaze over us.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s191-1: “Seven trainees saw it in the hall. The technical council cannot conceal the backdoor in a lawful candidate’s body. You stumbled into giving me the political credentials needed to retrieve the old archives.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s192-1: I drew a deep breath. Only the final archive authorization in her hand stood between us and the century-old archive.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s194-1: “I have the incident index left behind in Heisenberg’s work case as the technical key. With the emergency archive-retrieval authority you’re exercising now, the final two pieces of the puzzle are finally in place.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s196-1: “Prepare the materials. Once the face that the technical council has concealed in the recording for more than a century is revealed, we’ll settle the matter of your illegal intrusion at leisure. Now, go to the training room for verification.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s200-1: The hearing adjourned. Sera and Kane left the room.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s201-1: Only the three of us remained.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s202-1: The local Estelle reached out, took the wooden badge from the table, and hung it back on her belt. Her fingers pressed the catch down hard, as if confirming the weight that had been lost and recovered.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s204-1: It belonged to the Estelle in the coat. She held nothing in it, simply looking calmly at the person sitting in the chair.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s207-1: The local Estelle raised her head. Her face was still pale, but her eyes had recovered their familiar, sharp reason. Her gaze rested on the outstretched hand for two seconds. She did not take it.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s208-1: She pushed herself upright against the edge of the table.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s210-1: “When I fell just now, you were underneath me.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s211-1: The one in the coat slowly withdrew her hand. The fabric on the outside of her elbow had been scraped open against the flagstones, revealing a trace of blood.
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s213-1: “I only changed bodies this morning. My reactions are slow. I don’t feel pain.”
texts.chapter:v15-29c:event:text-s214-1: The local Estelle looked at the scrape on her elbow, her right hand still pressing tightly against the catch on her badge. She did not expose the lie in that sentence. She only lowered her head slightly and spoke very softly.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:title: Two Drawers (Two Estelles · This Evening)
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s2-1:
Old Accident Archive · Access Conditions:
“One, the accident index from the work cassette; two, the neural signature of the current operating session. With both in place, access may be requested.”
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s3-1: At fifteen-thirty, Sera finished signing the handling measures. The hearing adjourned with it.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s4-1: Under the written order, the two Estelles should have remained in the rehearsal room on the second floor, waiting for examination. But as we left the council chamber, Sera looked at them.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s6-1: “You two, come with me. Don’t stay upstairs waiting.”
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s7-1: She led us straight down to the White Tower’s second basement level.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s8-1: The room at the end of the corridor had no sign. The iron door was coated in gray-white matte dust. Sera took a ring of keys from her waist and selected an old brass key, its teeth rounded and polished bright by the years.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s10-1: “I haven’t used this one in twenty years.”
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s11-1: The lock gave a dull, heavy click. There were no windows. The air carried the sour smell of paper slowly oxidizing. A huge row of metal cabinets stood alone in the center.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s12-1: Sera placed her hand against the cold cabinet door.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s14-1: “The machine needs those two things. You have them on you: the index you pulled from the abandoned work cassette in the ruins, and your neural signature.”
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s15-1: This afternoon, I had told them everything about the method of crossing worlds and the witness’s origin.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s16-1: Sera lowered her hand. Her eyes settled on the final line printed on the inside of the cabinet door.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s18-1: “It says ‘access may be requested.’ The machine doesn’t care who controls the cabinet. I do. Whether it opens today is entirely my decision.”
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s22-1: The dim ceiling light fell across the side of her face.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s24-1: “For more than a hundred years, no one has written a cause into the records for one particular accident. The index Heisenberg left in the abandoned work cassette pointed to a packet of old data in the deep net. Inside was a video designated H31, the last image Heisenberg left behind. It also came with an accident
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s24-2: master tape serving as its preliminary proof—a recording of an accident in which someone was executed with a voice emitter, the person in the footage collapsing to the ground and twitching. But in the accountability ledger deep inside the White Tower, the cause field for that accident has remained blank.”
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s25-1: She steadily inserted the old key into the lock.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s27-1: “No one forgot to write it. There’s a deadlock in the underlying system. Nothing from outside can be written into it. Someone has to pierce this layer of window paper. The account for forcing open the cabinet will be entered under my name.”
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s31-1: The cabinet door swung open with a heavy click.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s32-1: There were no finished tapes inside. Black storage cases were piled in a disorderly stack, rising high and covered in dust.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s33-1: Sera pressed the index sheet covered in old numbers into the card reader, then pulled out a data cable and connected it to the interface on my badge.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s35-1: “This terminal is connected to the mainframe upstairs. There’s too much scrap. The mainframe will filter through it according to the index, then use your neural signature as the sieve. The data from
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s35-2: back then contains remnants of different people’s consciousness mixed together. The machine will throw your signature into the match and pull out every fragment on the same identity-compatibility chain.”
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s36-1: The indicator lights came on one after another in the dimness, and the machine gave off a heavy rumble.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s38-1: “We have to let it grind through it bit by bit. We probably won’t get anything audible until a quarter past nineteen.”
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s41-1: The room fell into a long silence. The deliberately buried dead files were being washed out bit by bit.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s42-1: I watched the indicators flicker on and off, then turned toward the two Estelles. If this machine was about to spit out the fundamental truth about the “system” and the “world,” then before we listened to it speak, we had to make sure what cards we held.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s46-1: “The machine connected different realities. In a cross-world connection, the neural signature is its underlying credential for recognizing a person. If the versions of me in different worlds are all running under the same signature, then along this physical circuit, every compatible
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s46-2: body is attached to the same frequency. As long as I remain connected to the machine, this channel is open. If I follow the clear physical differences in your memories, filter the sensory input, and lock onto that address, I may be able to push my perception across on my own.”
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s47-1: I pointed at the rumbling terminal.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s49-1: “While it’s still running, let’s walk this path ourselves. When it speaks, I don’t want to be just a passive listener receiving its answer. We’ll come back with a working result and check its account against it.”
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s50-1: The witness lowered the hand she had braced against the doorframe.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s56-1: We endured the long wait in the rehearsal room. Seventeen hundred.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s58-1: The local Estelle switched the equipment terminal into telemetry mode. I sat in the hardwood chair opposite her and connected the data cable to the neural interface on my belt. As long as my body was connected to the White Tower’s underlying network, the system could catch the physical peak when my consciousness suddenly dropped offline.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s59-1: At around eight forty this morning, the local Estelle threw twelve physical black-and-white markers here and copied the result onto a stiff paper card, then sealed it in the second drawer on the left of the desk.
texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s60-1: And yesterday—more precisely, during the same day in the previous world experienced by the witness—from nine-thirty in the morning until a little after eleven, the original blind-test record belonging to her had also been hidden in the AI laboratory outside the village in that world.

texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s66-1: “Until you come back and write out the result from memory, I won’t say whether those twelve results are black or white. Even if you see them, you are not allowed to speak.”

texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s103-1: Until now, my crossings had all been passive falls, or backflows along fixed gaps that had been torn open. This was the first time I would seize another normal body without relying on an accident or death as the trigger.

texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s125-1: In this experiment, whose exact answer only I knew, that fragment and the inexplicable blank in his mind were the only things to leave my thoughts and fall into reality.

texts.chapter:v15-29d:event:text-s137-1: The local Estelle held a pocket watch and stared at the screen, her voice restrained.
