texts.chapter:v15-29db:event:text-s61-1: Heisenberg was still speaking on-screen, but I had gone completely rigid where I stood.
texts.chapter:v15-29db:event:text-s62-1:
On that night when everything began. After the heavy elevator crash that left me unconscious, Yuna stood on the machine’s master-control side, beyond the glass.
To let my observation interval complete, her left wrist was clamped tightly
texts.chapter:v15-29db:event:text-s62-2: in a metal ring, and she reached across the console to complete the end-point confirmation for me. Afterward, she collapsed on the control corridor. The lights in that broken, abandoned facility went out completely, leaving only silence.
texts.chapter:v15-29db:event:text-s63-1: At the scene then, I was trapped in a metal chair, unable to move, and there was no one left who could perform a shutdown from outside.
texts.chapter:v15-29db:event:text-s64-1: In that originating world where everything began, the cross-world rift never closed, even after the equipment’s surface power was cut. That machine, which had missed the external physical reset, continued draining the underlying layer’s capacity simply by maintaining the connection.
texts.chapter:v15-29db:event:text-s65-1: “We always thought the end of the cycle itself was the shutdown.” I looked at the machine’s black screen. “If the shutdown prerequisite left in H31 is real... then the machine in the originating world of the first phase wasn’t shut down at the time.”
texts.chapter:v15-29db:event:text-s66-1: “Right. That’s where the total bill for that capacity of ten thousand went. That unshut-down source world is the root of reaching the safety limit.” Sera archived the last
texts.chapter:v15-29db:event:text-s66-2: file, then entered two monitoring commands into the terminal. A faint but persistent cross-world connection signal appeared on the screen. “That water pump is still there.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:title: A Place to Go (Two Estelles · That Night)
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s2-1:
Same-Day Accident Record · Final Page (written at the end by the elder on duty):
“This one today goes in two books.
The first book: the village accident record. Recorded by the elder on duty. Numbered and filed.
The second book: the
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s2-2:
unregistered one records it herself. The elder on duty will not record it for her, nor give this book a number.
The contents of the two books are checked against each other, and each is signed separately.
The second book, number: not assigned.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s6-1: No one usually went up to the roof of the White Tower. Apart from the nearly imperceptible square hatch we had closed beneath our feet, it was a seamless expanse of pure white, enclosed on all four sides by waist-high white parapets.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s7-1: The three of us sat down on that expanse, beside the edge of the parapet. The evening wind had already turned cool.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s8-1: I could still feel the touch of pressing that confirmation key at my fingertips. The resistance had been almost imperceptible, yet in an instant it had taken away everything that made Yuna exist. Since the
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s8-2: sacrifice, I had forced myself to keep moving, to keep thinking about what came next. Only now, having stopped, did I turn my head without thinking, wanting to hear her analysis of the situation we were in.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s9-1: There was only the sound of wind passing over the white parapet beside me. No one would ever again say to me, in that mechanical yet helpless tone, “That’s not reasonable, Arno.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s9-2: ” Yuna was gone. She had filled herself into that gap that swallowed everything—the time machine had forcibly linked countless worlds, and in doing so had also smashed open
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s9-3: a vast overdraft that all the connected worlds had to bear together. The capacity she released filled that bottomless, already-existing gap, keeping this dusk from collapsing.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s10-1: But as long as the shutdown remained incomplete, the machine in Heisenberg’s recording was still stuck in a connected state. The price she had paid by remaining in the chamber had leveled the old account, but it could not stop the machine that was still running.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s11-1: That true “endpoint” was, for me, only a name at this moment. I had no idea what coordinate it corresponded to in the long sequence of exhaustive searches. But I had to find it. Unless I completely
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s11-2: removed the root that kept operating, the machine’s endless throughput would sooner or later tear open that enormous shared gap again, dragging all the connected worlds into the abyss once more.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s12-1: I was exhausted. My hands and feet were cold in the evening wind. In the midst of that extreme fatigue and fear of the unknown, a dark shortcut surfaced in my mind.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s14-1: “Although the original data submitted by Watermarsh has already been locked down by a one-time death contract…” I heard my own dry voice rise into the wind, as if clinging to some lifeline. “But you survived here in this village today, and the system generated this new snapshot
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s14-2: of unauthorized survival. As long as I hold this new snapshot, then in every world where a witness is needed, I can write you back in once. Write you in, remove the back door, testify. If the shutdown fails, then in the next world, use this snapshot to write you in again…”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s15-1: I did not finish. Witness Estelle turned her head and looked at me quietly.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s17-1: “One me for every world. Each one gets woken up, checks the accounts, signs her name, and then you go on your way.” Her voice was calm. “Whatever the one left behind has to face, however she survives, you don’t care. Because by then, you’re already somewhere else.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s18-1: I went rigid. The night wind touched the cold sweat on my palms and sent a chill through me. Just one day ago, I had promised the original Estelle myself: “Once. No continuation.” To end the
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s18-2: system that treated people as tools, the first second I found myself with nowhere else to turn, I had instinctively planned to turn the person in front of me into an on-call witness service.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s20-1: “I’m sorry.” I lowered my eyes, my throat raw as if scraped with sandpaper. “That I could even say something like that.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s21-1: The witness shook her head lightly. The night wind stirred the two locks of golden hair tied tightly behind her head with indigo ribbons.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s25-1: “I’ll make this clear. I’m not doing that.” She turned to face me directly. “I won’t become a consumable resource like that.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s27-1: After a brief silence, the Estelle who belonged to this village spoke. She did not follow the weight of the mood. Instead, she deliberately pulled the conversation back to the reality still beneath our feet. She adjusted her low twin tails, tied with meticulous care.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s30-1: “I’ll start by saying what I don’t intend to do today.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s31-1: Her gaze fell on the distant wheat fields. Her tone did not rise or fall.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s33-1: “I’m not withdrawing my candidacy. I’m not returning to Watermarsh. I fought for a place there for three years, then attended a full week of public classes here. I can’t walk it all again.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s35-1: “What about the continuation-of-life contract? If you keep putting it off, your route will be cut off too.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s36-1: The local one placed her hands flat on her knees.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s38-1: “It’s not that I won’t sign. I’m asking for it to be rewritten first. Those clauses about disposing of the original body have to be rewritten. I want to see exactly what they stipulate beneath those clauses first.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s39-1: The witness sat beside the parapet, both arms around her knees. After a while, she spoke.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s41-1: “I’m not going to tell you whether that’s right or wrong. But I need to say it once, because later people will use me as their basis. If someone tells you, ‘The other you handled it this way back then’—tell him that was my today, not yours. I can’t take responsibility for that one on your behalf.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s44-1: The witness looked back at me.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s46-1: “You have to reach the place where the machine must be shut down,” she said.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s47-1: She looked at me. There was no room for retreat in those blue eyes.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s49-1: “The snapshot you’re looking at really is a clean new source, with no death contract.” She pointed to the tiny sensor patch beneath her collar. It was the tracking node Sera had personally pinned to her collarbone that morning after she woke, to
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s49-2: monitor her ‘unauthorized survival accident.’ “From this morning until now, it’s been synchronizing my complete neural state across the entire network. This accident snapshot has itself modeled all of my memories and consciousness at this moment.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s50-1: Her tone was calm, as if stating a route calculated long ago.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s52-1: “But I won’t turn it into your consumable resource. The system doesn’t know where the ‘endpoint’ you mentioned is, so I’ll give you the read key for synchronizing this snapshot
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s52-2: across worlds.” She looked at me. “And I’ll add a global lock: the moment you extract me in any world using it, the read permissions for every node across the network will be voided
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s52-3: at the same time. You can extract me only once more. You can take this one and only key to the world where the machine can truly be shut down. But that requires one condition.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s55-1: “The next time you wake me, it can’t be merely because you still need a witness to shut the machine down.” She looked at me. “There has to be somewhere I can freely choose to go after I wake up.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s57-1: I looked at her. There was no room for negotiation in that calm face.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s59-1: “I’ll give you the data,” she said. “But the me who exists now won’t continue on with you.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s60-1: I was silent for a while, then finally nodded.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s63-1: We left the White Tower and came to the accident-record desk.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s65-1: Sera was already waiting there. A not particularly bright lamp lit the room. In its dim yellow glow, two ledgers lay side by side on the table. The one on the left was today’s accident record. The one on the right had a perfectly clean cover, and was blank inside as well.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s68-1: Sera reached out and pushed the blank ledger in front of the witness.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s70-1: “The local one just told me about the two of you. The account of your staying here today can’t be left blank. You record yours. They’ll be kept side by side.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s73-1: The witness took the ledger and opened to the untouched first page. She picked up her pen and wrote a passage in the very center.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s75-1: “The snapshot data corresponding to this page is hereby established as a new source. Read access to this source is transferred only to Arno, and may be used for extraction once.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s76-1: The awakener must prove to the continuation-of-life individual for that occasion that all voiceprints and control hardware have been physically removed, and must leave the verification to her.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s77-1: The continuation-of-life individual for that occasion has the right to refuse boarding, refuse to testify, and refuse to accompany him; she must also have somewhere she can choose to go. She alone decides all four matters. No one may answer on her behalf.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s79-1: When she finished, she signed her name in the lower right corner. Then she picked up the scanner left on the table as an accident-verification tool.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s80-1: She placed the scanner’s raster flat against the page covered in writing. A red light came on, scanning the natural-language text on the page into an image. As a forced attachment to the portion of the snapshot data being captured by the patch, it was encrypted into the synchronization protocol.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s81-1: “The system of course can’t understand what contract I wrote on paper. But when you take that read key and activate this snapshot in the writing room of another world, the system will verify the code
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s81-2: in the attachment image.” She set down the scanner and pushed the ledger back toward the center of the table. “If you intend to ignore these clauses and forcibly put the data into a body whose
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s81-3: hardware control ports haven’t been removed—the protocol’s underlying hardware-environment check won’t pass. The writing program will freeze outright and lock the key. Unless you can fool the machine.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s82-1: In the dim room, Sera stared at the lines for a while, then picked up her pen and copied the page into the village’s own record, without changing a single word. When she finished, she drew a horizontal line beside it.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s84-1: “Arno, draw the closing line on this page at the moment you leave today.” Sera put down her pen. “Everything that happens before then counts as her account in this village today.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s85-1: The witness put away the unnumbered ledger that belonged to her. Her eyes remained on the horizontal line. The patch was still affixed to her collarbone, quietly working, recording these final few dozen minutes. She said nothing.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s89-1: After leaving the accident-record desk, we headed toward the slope outside the village. Along this final short stretch, the night wind seemed less cold.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s91-1: We walked in silence for a while. The village at night was quiet. Nearing the slope, the local Estelle stopped.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s93-1: “You’re coming home with me tonight.” She did not look at the witness, keeping her gaze on the darkness ahead. “The bed’s narrow, but we can squeeze in two.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s97-1: They continued forward, their steps gradually falling into the same rhythm.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s98-1: At last, we stopped on this relatively level stretch of slope. From here, the outline of the entire village was still visible. Every household’s fire had gone out. Only a few scattered homes still showed dim yellow light.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s101-1: The local Estelle looked toward the distant wheat fields and suddenly spoke. She told us about the first time, when she was ten, that she saw someone from the Inner Circle come to Watermarsh to collect the village
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s101-2: ledgers. He had clearly walked across a wide stretch of mud, yet when he reached them, there wasn’t a speck of dust on his shoes. She had stared at them for a long time, unable to understand how he had done it.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s105-1: “I did. He walked across boards someone else had laid down.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s109-1: “People from our village. They laid them down the night before and collected them the next morning.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s110-1: At that, she could not help laughing first.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s113-1: The witness listened quietly, then said softly:
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s119-1: “The same. Even the crease in the side of his shoe was the same.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s120-1: In the night, the two people with identical faces and matching hairstyles laughed softly together. The night wind moved through the grass.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s123-1: It was late. Twenty-two hundred was approaching. I stood up.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s124-1: The local one raised her head, her eyes settling into that familiar, calm defensive look.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s126-1: “Arno. Tomorrow morning, Sera will question us in the front hall about the unauthorized writing-in.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s128-1: “I know. But after I leave, the one who stays here won’t have the memories of everything that happened elsewhere after our handoff.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s133-1: “Tomorrow morning, the local Arno who can no longer go anywhere else and can only stay here will be the one who goes with me to the front hall and faces the blade. Since the account of the unauthorized writing-in has fallen here, it’s our local matter, with nothing to do with you, passing ghost. We’ll bear this account ourselves.”
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s137-1: In the final seconds before the weightlessness of decoherence completely overwhelmed me, the witness peeled off the patch recording the complete state of her mind during this last day and handed it to me.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s138-1: The patch was only a discarded sensor node. The actual synchronization had already been completed. The one and only read key remained in my memory.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s140-1: After I left, the local Arno who stayed behind would open his eyes. Their time would continue too. The narrow bed would take in the unregistered one, and they would have the latter half of the night for themselves.
texts.chapter:v15-29e:event:text-s141-1: And I would carry this key, with only one chance left, to face the next node.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:title: A Real One (Two Mornings · Part One)
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s2-1:
Switching Record (written by me, not submitted):
“Target: An early world where Yuna is still alive.
Destination: Time coordinate 08:15. She has not been hurt in this morning.
Purpose: I couldn’t
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s2-2:
write a definite reason when filling out the form, so I left it blank.
Companion: None.
Expected duration: Brief contact.
Whether to report after returning: Yes.
To whom: Haven’t decided yet.”
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s7-1: After staying on the hillside until 22:00 and finishing that long infiltration, I woke in the operating room. It was already deep into the night. After going through the double-seal
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s7-2: blind test and listening to Heisenberg’s final recording, I still sat alone before the real physical terminal, directing my attention toward an extremely early coordinate.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s8-1: I shamefully backed down again. I knew I had once resolved to take in the her who carried all those mutually incompatible, agonizing memories. But as the end drew near, the temptation of a
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s8-2: “safe version” that could put my own mind at ease seized me again. I didn’t want to watch her be crushed beneath the memories of hundreds of violent deaths. I was afraid to face her like that.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s9-1: I knew the complete record stream could only be sealed after her life ended and she generated no further subjective blocks, once I wrote an external end marker. But now I was sitting before the console with full system access. I could choose
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s9-2: a safe point in the past and have the terminal capture her record up to that moment. As long as I drew an endpoint in advance and did not connect it to the future dead end, the machine would register it as an undamaged alternative state.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s10-1: With that memory burned into my nerves, I cast my consciousness back into the past and synchronized into a parallel morning where she was still alive. The slight dizziness caused by an outside consciousness taking over an early local body made me stagger, and I braced my palm hard against the rough brick wall.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s14-1: This was still an extremely early first day. Just minutes earlier, the local me had proved to her that the time loop existed. Now Yuna had braced the empty water bucket she had brought along against the door, habitually wiped both hands on her cloth apron, and turned around to
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s14-2: count the route. Moisture hung in the morning mist. From the village road in the distance came the barking and shouts of hunting dogs. She still had hope. She believed that if we climbed over the wall before the search party closed in, we could escape into the woods to the north.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s15-1: Then her movements stopped. She saw the look in my eyes.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s20-1: “Your face is wrong.” She frowned, speaking quickly, still breathing a little hard from running. “Did something happen before the last reset?”
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s21-1: She stared into my eyes. The Arno she knew had been thinking only about how to escape alive. But there had to be a dead stillness in the way I was looking at her now, the stillness of someone who knew the ending.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s24-1: Watching that uninformed vitality in her, the temptation that had been circling in my mind for a long time finally took shape. This version of her was clean, resilient, and her hope had not yet been
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s24-2: worn away. If the body sitting before the terminal could issue the truncation command now, the her in the future would not have to wake with all those grievous wounds as her only possible state.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s27-1: I looked at her face, not yet completely corroded by despair.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s29-1: “We spent a long time together after this morning. We went through many dead ends. The you in the future will carry all the memories. But I can draw an endpoint here and end your record
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s29-2: stream at this uninjured moment. No matter how terribly the you who comes later suffered… what is restored at the end could be you as you are now, instead of that you covered in scars.”
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s30-1: She stopped in bewilderment. The hunting dogs outside were barking closer now, and the door was trembling, while I was talking to her about a future severed out of nowhere.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s32-1: “Are you making arrangements for the end?” She pointed toward the courtyard gate, her voice rising slightly. “So we’re not only unable to escape today—you’ve died many times too, haven’t you?”
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s35-1: I said nothing. It was a long and cruel way to die, but I didn’t dare tell her.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s38-1: Fear began spreading through her eyes. She wasn’t ignorant of everything. She immediately seized on the crucial gap.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s40-1: “Then what about the me who stays here?” She clenched her fists, her knuckles turning white. “You take a backup from the past and use it to fool your system. Then the real person here just keeps waiting to die today?”
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s42-1: “I shouldn’t make you bear the terrible things that came later…”
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s43-1: She stared hard at me as if looking at a complete stranger. She took half a step back, her back pressing against the cold water bucket.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s46-1: She glanced at the firelight drawing closer beyond the courtyard wall, then fixed her eyes on me again.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s48-1: “The me who was supposed to be alive in the future…” She was trembling faintly, but forced her voice to hold. “What did she have to endure in your place for you to want to take this me, who hasn’t lived through any of it, and use her to replace that one?”
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s49-1: I was pinned in place, unable to answer.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s51-1: “I don’t know what happened later, the way you describe it. But every blade I take here today—even if I die at their hands today—she has to answer for it too.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s51-2: We lived through it together. Don’t think you can use me to wash away what she went through. That complete person you’re leaving there—what will happen to her?”
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s56-1: If I forced my way around her and had the body in the future truncate the record stream directly, this data fixed at 08:15 could become an undamaged personality
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s56-2: state. Even if the local her continued to suffer, her life data before this morning would already be closed, without the trauma of all the deaths that came later.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s57-1: But I knew that if I did this, the Yuna before me would be the one to wake at the end of the future. The complete Yuna carrying all the memories would be left in the destruction forever, with no chance of
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s57-2: waking again. If the future her opened the data and found that, to escape pain, I had once tried to erase the her struggling through the dead ends, using a severed tail with no subsequent data to deceive myself…
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s58-1: My consciousness hovered at the edge of confirming the termination for several seconds.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s59-1: I did not draw that endpoint.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s60-1: I prepared to release my observation of the present. Before my consciousness fully withdrew, I turned around.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s61-1: She sensed the change in my presence and suddenly called after me.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s63-1: “Your way of replacing the future me with the me from the past won’t work. Then the person you really want to save—the one carrying everything—can she be saved in the end?”
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s65-1: “I don’t know.” I didn’t turn back. “If you refuse, the only one who can ultimately be connected to the future will be the complete you, carrying all the memories and scars.”
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s67-1: “Then go finish the road you’re supposed to walk. Don’t stand in my way here.”
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s70-1: She didn’t ask who I really was. She simply turned around, expressionless, put the empty bucket back behind the door, and continued searching for an escape route that could never work.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s71-1: I closed my eyes and released my focus on this world. The Arno belonging to this morning would take control of the body again. He knew nothing of the future, and would retain no memory of the minutes I had occupied
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s71-2: his consciousness. He would face a Yuna who possessed unfamiliar information and continue toward the morning’s ending. I had taken nothing with me. All that remained was a senselessly interrupted, lunatic interlude.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s72-1: In the last second before my vision went dark, I saw her crouch back into the shadows. The search party’s shouts on the village road had already reached the courtyard wall. This morning had not paused for even half a step because of my arrival. It continued without mercy toward destruction.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s78-1: Back at the terminal, I pulled up the entry form I had filled out only halfway.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s79-1: In the “Purpose” field, I added the final result.
texts.chapter:v15-29f:event:text-s81-1: “Result: Collection unsuccessful. Applicant unilaterally terminated the operation.”
texts.chapter:v15-29g:title: Two Mornings Without Me (Two Kinds of Morning · Part Two)
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s2-1:
Active Addressing · Record of This Entry (written by me, not submitted):
“Destination: Two places.
First: A world without her (entry point: Day Eight, 09:15).
Second: A world where she once
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s2-2:
was (entry point: Day Twenty-Two, 21:55).
Purpose: Take a look. This time I can write it down.
Companion: None.
Whether to report after returning: Yes.
Report to whom: Haven’t decided yet.”
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s7-1: The first place I chose was another branch where Yuna did not exist.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s8-1: I connected to the system, and consciousness sank. At the instant I seized primary control, the local “me” was pressed down to the bottom of consciousness. It was an outright act of plunder. I followed this body’s muscle memory as it
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s8-2: moved forward. As long as my stride did not deviate too far, when I disconnected, the local Arno would remember this uncontrolled experience of watching clearly, but at least he would not alarm anyone by stopping in some inexplicable place.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s9-1: I wanted to confirm with my own eyes whether, in this objective history that had never contained her, there would be some small, jarring trace left by her being pulled out.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s10-1: I was passing through the chapel foyer. Two names were written neatly on the roster of this term’s candidates on the wall. The first was mine, Inner Circle; the second was Estelle, Outer Circle. I looked up at the wall clock. A quarter past nine in the morning.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s11-1: Yuna’s name was not on the roster. In this world, she had never been born either. I had already confirmed this when I connected to similar branches before, but then I had been eager to search for clues
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s11-2: that might save her. Now, because I had not possessed him to do anything unusual this morning, the local Arno was living the steady, unobserved morning he was supposed to have. I only wanted to see whether
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s11-3:
this vast track, without that anomaly appearing from nowhere, would settle into another kind of cruel calm.
I did not interfere with his original pace. I let the body continue east through the village.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s14-1:
As I passed that row of houses, the south-facing window was open.
In the worlds where she existed, she had spent ten years wearing the wood there smooth, climbing through the window again and again, stepping in the same place each
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s14-2:
time.
Now, two thick glass jars filled with grain stood side by side on the sill. The wood was flat, its rough natural grain still visible. A crisp tapping came from inside. Someone was holding a bowl and feeding the chickens.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s17-1: I followed his original route and walked past it like any ordinary window in the village. Without slowing.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s20-1: At the corner of the yard, I met Estelle coming toward me. She wore that bright purple ceremonial dress, its silver-white and ice-blue patterns arranged without a flaw. She carried a thick stack of document folders in her arms and was hurrying across the open ground.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s21-1: Tucked into the top folder was a family letter bearing Watermarsh’s reed-grass emblem, pressed beneath an Initial Review Form for Continuation Eligibility stamped with the Church seal.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s22-1: As we passed one another, she turned her head slightly and gave this way a polite nod. The body’s instinct moved the neck and returned the greeting with the same distant, standard measure expected between colleagues.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s25-1: She hurried to the second row of houses, pushed open the door, and went inside. “Bang.” The door closed.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s26-1: Without Yuna bursting in from nowhere, Estelle still followed the track assigned to the Outer Circle seat. The review form and the Watermarsh family letter remained pressed firmly against her chest as they disappeared with her behind
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s26-2: the heavy wooden door. The form stated the contractual terms for accepting the execution of the original body in exchange for the transfer of consciousness, and in the near future, this system would still require her to sign it.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s33-1: After disconnecting, I shifted the coordinates toward the second destination.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s34-1: The instant I landed, weightlessness and the muffled echo inside the sealed suit filled my senses. A twilight line between pale violet and deep purple cut across the sky. A massive satellite, marked by broad cracks and dark bands, occupied most of it.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s34-2: This world’s rotation period differed from Earth’s. A gray-white star had just risen, its pallid light falling across the unfamiliar lakeshore. Low, dark, leaf-shaped creatures drew slightly inward in the cold morning wind, making a rustling sound.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s37-1: In this branch, we had successfully escaped the village, boarded the ark, and reached an alien planet. But the capacity shortfall shared across worlds still remained. According to the White Tower’s control console
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s37-2: crash log, the system reserves fell below the stability threshold at 20:36 that evening. The unbinding of living first-persons began immediately afterward, in an order determined by the extent of accumulated wear.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s38-1: The elders, then the adult laborers, and only after them, us. Of the two people on that alien lakeshore, Yuna went dark before Arno. Her subjective consciousness had just ceased in this world. Her voice disappeared from the communications channel, but the body beneath her faceplate had not died yet.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s39-1: I did not have the courage to set the landing point at a time when she could still speak. I was afraid to face a pair of living eyes behind a faceplate on that hopeless alien planet.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s39-2: Even less could I bear to deceive her, wearing the local Arno’s shell, at the final moment when she was still the subject. So I chose the moment just after her voice stopped.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s42-1: This body was kneeling in the alien soil. Yuna lay on her side in the crook of its arms, still wearing the heavy spacesuit from the escape. Through the thick protection, the local Arno’s remaining muscle memory still held tightly to her shoulders, trying to catch the heartbeat that had weakened to its limit.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s45-1: I controlled these stiff hands and tightened their hold around her again through the gloves.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s48-1: At exactly 22:00, the limit of the cycle was approaching, and this branch body was about to shut down forcibly. Primary control would remain mine for only a few minutes more.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s49-1: Inside the White Tower’s protection chamber, I could withdraw my consciousness at any time with a single thought. If I exited now, the local Arno would rise again from the deep sea of the subconscious, reclaim his body, and have these last few minutes to see her through the end.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s53-1: The gray-white star’s light struck the curved surface of the sealed helmet. The faint tremor in my arms was disappearing bit by bit. I listened to my own muffled breathing inside the faceplate and felt the dry rustling of the dark plants outside the spacesuit. I sat there in the alien soil, counting the seconds
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s53-2: one by one. I did not return his eyes to him, and I did not look away. I watched the reflection on the lake until the observation interval reached its limit at exactly 22:00. The local Arno’s subjective consciousness, pressed down beneath mine, was snuffed out along with the physical death of this branch body.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s60-1: When perception on the alien planet went completely to zero, the system disconnected. When I opened my eyes again inside the original Tower, the sky outside was already bright.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s63-1: I walked to the table and looked at the entry record, most of which had already been filled out before departure.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s66-1: At the very bottom of the page, I used a pen to add the final note.
texts.chapter:v15-29g:event:text-s68-1: “Note: In this system, I had no ability at all to undo a death that had already occurred. To hold her for a few more minutes, I took away the local Arno’s final right—the right to see her through the end.”
texts.chapter:v15-24f:title: Appendix Four to Chapter Twenty-Four: Five Clauses
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s3-1: This was an old incident from the second phase, occurring on the morning of the tenth world switch. In this passive handoff, still never actively addressed, the sensation of weightlessness when I took over the body was unusually clear. Under the mechanism of that time, at exactly
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s3-2: 22:00, I—the cross-world viewpoint—would withdraw and go to the next world; the local Arno remaining in this world would continue living, retaining the memories of everything we had experienced together up to 22:00, and bear all the consequences of what we had stirred up today.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s4-1: In the previous few worlds, I had still been careful to avoid disrupting the local counterparts’ existing lives as much as possible, afraid of leaving an unmanageable break in whatever life remained to them. But on this morning, when an unnamed girl was brought into being, all that remained in me was the madness of crossing the boundary.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s5-1: The sheet bearing the five constraints still lies across my memory like a physical seal.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s6-1: In World Ten, the world we called the “anchor,” I had dragged the current candidate, Estelle, into it without regard for the consequences, trying to retrieve the Yuna who was already dead through a blank production line. The specific actions of that insane
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s6-2: morning—the unauthorized archive searches that bypassed Sera’s oversight, the complicated White Tower blind-box seal, and the cross-world synchronization of the source draft—were later locked away forever in a nine-page record titled One-Time Write Authorization.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s7-1: But what cut deeper than those operations was the five paper constraints Estelle forced me to sign before the countdown reached zero at 15:20.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s8-1: It was a confession of guilt for an ethical disaster.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s9-1: The veneer of legality had already been exhausted at the boundary of the permits Sera initially approved. That morning, all Sera stamped and approved at her desk was: the contract explanation section, the candidate disposition index, and the bodily-rights witness section.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s9-2: Through the third item, “bodily-rights witness section,” Estelle obtained a legal starting point for verifying her own continuation contract and entering the underground facility. I, meanwhile, used that opening to slide straight into the abyss of unauthorized life-making.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s10-1:
In the production line’s control room, Estelle had forced me to draw two columns on a blank sheet and list every known fact myself.
It was the evidence for and against, meant to measure the absurdity of this experiment.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s11-1:
On the left was the basis for “Yuna might come back.”
On the right was the conclusive evidence that she would not.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s12-1: Beneath the word “would” on the left, I wrote only one withered line: the physical parameters of this body belonged entirely to Yuna. They were pure Inner Circle parameters, compressed from vast quantities of data into a generation seed through the medical terminal’s algorithms, then written down from memory after crossing worlds.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s14-1: Every established rule warned me: without her seventeen years of autobiographical memories, the one who woke in this body would almost certainly be a completely unfamiliar girl. My only defense
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s14-2: was that no one had ever actually used Yuna’s exact parameters to receive a beginning with zero autobiography—that was the only narrow gap experimentation had not yet sealed shut directly.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s15-1: I knew the evidence overwhelmingly opposed me. I knew it was nothing more than a fragile fixation. And still, I refused to stop.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s16-1: So Estelle pushed the sheet bearing the five rules toward me.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s20-1:
1. Do it only once. Whatever the result, a second body may not be initiated on the grounds of “insufficient sample.”
2. From the first second she breathes, she is a full rights-bearing subject. If she does not display the standard
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s20-2:
kneeling ritual innately, that proves “preinstalled faith” is a lie. All determination of religious instinct must end immediately, and everything must become care.
3. She must not be called Yuna. No provocative test may be conducted
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s20-3:
in an attempt to find remnants of the old personality.
4. Arno may not be the sole caregiver. The newborn’s instinctive dependence on the first face must not be twisted into Yuna responding to you.
5. Local obligations may not be
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s20-4: evaded. At exactly 22:00, even if the cross-world viewpoint withdraws, the local Arno remaining here must continue, together with me and the facility, to bear responsibility for this grave crime and for the newborn’s lifelong care.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s24-1: I looked at the five clauses, especially the last one.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s25-1: At first, I thought this was her way of formally writing the act of “dumping the debt” into the contract. But I soon understood that a signature on paper could not ethically provide independent
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s25-2: consent on behalf of the local Arno who would take over the aftermath after 22:00. He was not present. In a few hours, he would merely be forced to inherit the memories I had imposed on him.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s26-1: Estelle had written the fifth clause not to declare that responsibility had legally been transferred, nor to ratify this disaster on his behalf. On the contrary, she used that painfully stark declaration to
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s26-2:
expose me with brutal clarity: what I was doing was, in essence, forcing a heavy, inescapable lifelong burden onto a local counterpart who had no way to refuse.
My signature merely acknowledged that this debt had
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s26-3: been incurred. It did not make any of this justifiable. The clause completely shattered the weightless illusion buried in my subconscious—that I was “only conducting an experiment, taking one look, and leaving.”
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s27-1: The third and fourth clauses above also stripped me of any possibility of extracting emotional comfort from that newborn.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s28-1:
Estelle had seen through my weakness. I could not call her Yuna, could not use objects from her past habits to test her, could not mistake her hatchling-like attachment for a call from an old love.
If I obeyed none of these rules,
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s28-2: the new life would become a selfish specimen I used to prove that “Yuna was still here”; but if I obeyed them, my investigation would be forcibly turned into a long wait in which I could only watch with my eyes and never intervene.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s29-1: It was a one-way execution directed at my heart.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s31-1:
At 15:20 that day, the countdown reached zero. The newborn opened her eyes. Just as all the evidence had predicted, she did not recognize the light, and she did not recognize me.
And Estelle, who had taken on every risk beginning with the
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s31-2: unauthorized overreach from the bodily-rights witness section, entered her own name on the emergency medical shelter list. Pledging the candidate seat she treasured above all else, she accepted responsibility for sheltering the unnamed girl.
texts.chapter:v15-24f:event:text-s32-1: The words of these five clauses, written on paper, became conclusive evidence of my unauthorized creation of life over the long years that followed. They nailed down the horror of “making another person to search for one person,” and established, in this cruel world, the hard boundary that once life has been given, it cannot be altered.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:title: Chapter 24, Appendix 5: She Was Seeking Only Warmth
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s1-1:
Production Line · Pre-Delivery Display:
“Body template: qualified.
Anonymous capacity: usable.
Autobiographical source: none.
Expected preexisting memories: zero.
Subject identity: cannot be inferred by this unit.”
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s4-1: The screen of the main control console gave off a dim blue glow. Beneath those five statements was the final red physical confirmation button.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s5-1: At the final step, the automatically running pipeline came to a stop. The final confirmation interlock required a living person to press it by hand.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s8-1: Before my finger touched the button, Estelle opened the hardbound logbook and pressed the tip of her pen heavily against the page.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s10-1: “The current pipeline checks are all green. The machine is no longer stopping you.”
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s11-1: She raised her head and stared at me.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s13-1: “But your hand will be the one pressing it in a moment. Whatever happens afterward, you are not allowed to excuse yourself with ‘The system allowed it.’ I want you to confirm aloud: who is going to activate this body?”
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s16-1: I took a deep breath and signed my name in the executor field.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s21-1: Estelle’s signature was in the confirmer field of the operation log.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s22-1: I withdrew my gaze, raised my hand, and pressed the red confirmation button with all my strength.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s27-1: We entered the infusion room. In the enormous cultivation tank at the center of the room, cloudy portions appeared in the base gel, like a mass of ink that refused to disperse, slowly spreading inward from the edges.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s28-1: There was nothing sacred about the manufacture of life here. Only industrial efficiency and the brutal accumulation of biomass. Through the glass, I watched the mass stretch through the solution and differentiate into a ghastly white skeleton. The network of blood vessels climbed and intertwined along the bones inch by inch,
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s28-2: like rapidly growing vines. The lungs and organs gradually filled the space in the chest, followed by a hand—the joints taking shape one by one in the gel, connected to a slender wrist. Finally, a delicate layer of skin spread over it like a membrane, perfectly enclosing the interior of flesh and blood in the outline of a girl.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s31-1: The cultivation fluid in the tank began to recede. Beneath the new skin, her chest began a faint rise and fall.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s32-1: I stared fixedly at that movement. In my memories, the last time I looked at her through glass was outside the blast window of the pure white room. She had been leaning against a metal table then, her breathing growing shallower and shallower as the binding collapsed after her reserves fell below the threshold.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s33-1: The body before me was breathing shallowly too, but with extreme rapidity. It was like someone who had never used an organ called lungs, desperately learning how to draw the first breath of air into their body.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s36-1: With the faint sound of airflow, she finally opened her eyes.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s37-1: The irises were amber. The room’s cold light fell across them, and a tiny patch of reflected light appeared in each pupil.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s38-1: She opened her eyes, her gaze pointing straight upward, staring blankly at the glaring shadowless lamp on the ceiling. There was no sign of focus. Her eyes sat rigidly in their sockets like two glass marbles lacking lubrication.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s41-1: The light was simply too bright. Her eyelids trembled instinctively, trying to close, but she made no movement to turn her head away.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s42-1: Her fingers gave a nervous twitch. She showed no defensive or exploratory reaction, but she did display something instinctive—the muscles contracted involuntarily when the cold air touched her damp skin.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s43-1: Estelle stood beside the tank, watching her quietly. She did not even have the muscular reflexes needed to maintain a sitting posture, so of course she could not perform any act of kneeling or prayer. That was
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s43-2: not enough to prove there was no instinct of obedience preinstalled in her by the Inner Circle. But at least at this first moment of life, she was only a blank-slate shell struggling to adapt to the cold air.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s44-1: Estelle turned to get a towel. This “living counterexample” could not be allowed to see the light of day. The moment she appeared, she would be treated as waste and destroyed. She had to survive first—survive until we could find a way to let the outside world see her.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s47-1: And I instinctively took one step forward, blocking the harsh light from the ceiling.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s48-1: My face cut abruptly into the space directly above hers. I knew I had just signed an agreement not to induce any familiar response, but in that moment, the ugly corner of my
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s48-2: heart still began to hope desperately. Even the slightest movement of her eyes, or the habitual lift of her eyebrows—as long as her gaze could focus on my face for even an instant—
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s51-1: But those amber eyes remained unfocused, staring straight upward.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s52-1: Even though I blocked almost all the light, in her retinas my face was no different from the glaring lamp that had been there moments ago. Her eyes did not turn at all. Her gaze passed straight through me as though
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s52-2: through a sheet of cold glass. In this newborn shell generated from Yuna’s body template, none of the tiny habits I had once known—the arc of her raised eyebrows, or her instinctive avoidance—had appeared yet.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s53-1: She could not even turn her eyes. Later, as her ability to control herself returned, she might develop some small gesture resembling one of Yuna’s at some
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s53-2: moment. But at this physical starting point, the person named Yuna was not here at all. This was a ten-year experiment. And now, it was only the first second.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s54-1: Then Estelle returned. She gently covered the girl’s trembling shoulders with a towel warmed in hot water.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s55-1: “It’s not hot.” Estelle’s voice was exceptionally calm.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s56-1: The newborn’s neck muscles gave an awkward twitch. She still could not turn her eyes, and did not truly “look” toward Estelle. But that slight body trembling in the cold
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s56-2: air, following the instinct for sound and warmth, very slowly and stiffly tilted its cheek toward the steaming towel, finally resting against the back of Estelle’s hand.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s59-1: I stood where I was, watching her cling desperately to that warmth as though it were a piece of driftwood.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s60-1: With her free hand, Estelle pressed the towel firmly into place, then turned to look at me.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s62-1: “What are you still standing there for? Go get a blanket. The form has both our names on it.”
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s67-1: She was transferred to the Enlightenment Zone, where the floor was heated.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s68-1: I brought the thickest blanket I could find and awkwardly tried to wrap her in it. But she did not cooperate at all. Her body slumped downward, with none of the muscular reflexes needed to maintain a sitting posture. I had no choice but to half-kneel on the heated floor, brace her with my shoulder, and thread one corner of the blanket beneath her armpit.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s69-1: She was heavy. This was not an unreal mass of data running in the cloud. This was a living person with a heartbeat, who needed to eat, whose skeleton had not even fully adapted to gravity yet.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s72-1: Estelle took over the remaining edges and expertly wrapped her tightly until she stopped trembling.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s74-1: “I need to write a memorandum.” I looked at the hands that had just strained to support her, my voice slightly dry in the quiet
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s74-2: Enlightenment Zone. “If, at twenty-two hundred tonight, the me who remains in this world has his memories wiped by the system… if
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s74-3: he forgets everything, he’ll send this stranger straight to destruction as soon as he sees her, like he was looking at a monster.”
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s75-1: At my words, Estelle stopped what she was doing.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s77-1: “What if his memories aren’t wiped?” Her words came down like cold water. “What if he remembers everything that happened today? Then he’ll remember clearly the weight of supporting a newborn, just as clearly as you remember holding her yourself.”
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s79-1: “That’s something a memorandum can’t explain, Arno. The long years ahead will bind him to me, together with this life that can’t even turn its eyes.”
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s80-1: Half-kneeling on the floor, I opened my mouth, but could not refute a word of it. A few days ago, I had still been telling her that the memories would remain intact. Now that the time had come to take responsibility, I instinctively placed my hope in the slim chance that maybe he would forget.
texts.chapter:v15-24g:event:text-s81-1: She would need her first feeding at six tomorrow morning. Whether or not his memories were wiped, the person lifting the nutrient solution would truly feel the weight of it. That was what I, from across the boundary, had left him for the rest of his life with the press of a button.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:title: Chapter Twenty-Four, Appendix Six: The Kind That Doesn't Require Dying
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s1-1:
Operator Accident Record Control Desk · Inscription on the desktop (AI Laboratory, date unknown):
“This desk only records; it does not judge.
　What it records is determined by the source. How far it records is determined by the source.
　This desk does not ask why the source wants to be recorded.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s6-1: At exactly nineteen hundred hours, we left the Enlightenment District amid the faint hum of the cold lights.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s7-1: We left the life that had only just been created that afternoon inside an automated care pod in the abandoned zone. This was the only maintenance node underground that could temporarily cut off the Church’s external
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s7-2: network through its permissions, and the safest place available to hide her. The heavy security door slowly closed behind us. The girl who had barely crossed the activation threshold lay beneath the temperature-control
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s7-3: cover, clutching tightly at the blanket that had given her warmth. No autobiographical source had been implanted in her, yet she had already learned by instinct to pursue heat, completing her first breaths through pain.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s8-1: Only after the metal plate of the temperature-control cover had risen completely, hiding the thin shell of a body, did Estelle turn and walk outside.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s9-1: The air in the corridor was much colder and harder than inside the pod. texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s10-1: “When I wiped down the temperature-control cover just now, I touched her hand. It was warm.” After we had gone some distance, Estelle suddenly spoke. Her voice echoed through the empty passage.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s11-1: “Once we’re done tonight, we’ll bring her out,” I said.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s12-1: “Mm.” Estelle nodded and slowed her steps. “She has no past at all, but the machine recognized her anyway. The nameless capacity allocated to her this afternoon
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s12-2: got her through the initial rejection and let her truly live—and no one needed to sign a termination agreement, and the underlying system didn’t report an error.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s13-1: She stopped and looked straight at me.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s15-1: “Injecting nameless capacity to awaken a body doesn’t require us to fill the space with another corpse.” She drew a deep breath. “That proves the ‘termination agreement’ is only a political measure. By the same
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s15-2: logic, if we read a living person and create a full record, the so-called ‘physical prerequisite of signing an Old Body Termination Agreement’ very likely isn’t a hardware limitation of the machine at all.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s17-1: “Yes. I checked early records of live-scanning projects in another world, and they proved your guess: when the machine reads an entire personality, it doesn’t erase the source at all.” I calmly finished the
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s17-2: conclusion. “‘One must die’ is only a political lock the Inner Circle imposed in the front-end verification to preserve single-seat inheritance and prevent two copies with equal voting rights from appearing.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s18-1: I paused and looked at her. “Back then, Lysenko privately set up a direct-link node in the lower-level firmware to bypass the approvals. No matter how the upper network was reconstructed, that back door remained buried in
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s18-2: the motherboard architecture. During the fifth cycle, I dug its key out of the abandoned archives in the Grand Library and memorized it. I carried it to every world. With it, we can force a complete backup of a living person.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s20-1: “Then let’s make it a fact.” Her eyes were unusually bright. “Use this key that crossed the cycles to get around it, and see whether the underlying disaster-recovery protocol really will accept it as submitted.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s25-1: In the equipment room at the deepest end of this level was a deep node that bypassed the peripheral network and connected directly to the external disaster-recovery management station. texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s26-1: As the indicator lights on the console came on one after another, the heavy, cold metal desk slowly emerged from the darkness. texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s28-1: “‘This desk only records; it does not judge. What it records and how far it records are determined entirely by the source. This desk does not ask why.’” She softly read aloud the rule engraved above.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s31-1: She placed the booklet she carried on the console, then turned and told me what she had decided to do tonight.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s33-1: “I’m going to use myself as the counterexample.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s36-1: I watched her silently for a while. Since she had already made her decision, I turned around and brought up the verification interface, entered the back-door key, bypassed the Church’s external network barrier, and forcibly mounted the external disaster-recovery station’s underlying protocol onto this machine.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s38-1: “The forced full-registration channel connecting to the external station is open.” I watched the parameters flicker. “Once you enter the scanning room, your complete personality record will follow the existing
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s38-2: physical connections the external disaster-recovery station already uses to distribute data to each node, continuously synchronizing into the local accident recorders of the White Towers in every world.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s39-1: I paused and brought up another monitoring display.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s41-1: “At the same time, the external disaster-recovery management station will record your permission trail. The operation itself will leave a log of forced unauthorized live registration in the station’s append-only audit layer. Even if the Inner Circle obtains the highest-level permissions, it can’t be erased.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s43-1: “Even if they physically disconnect that disaster-recovery station afterward, as long as the log of this live backup remains in the immutable underlying layer, I become a threat capable of breaking single-seat inheritance at any time.” She calmly continued. “No matter how much the Church wants to cover it up, it can’t
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s43-2: erase this ironclad evidence. The Inner Circle will very likely strip me of my candidacy, perhaps even place me under control by the harshest means—compared with the upheaval caused by overturning the single-seat system, replacing a candidate who registered a record without authorization is obviously the lower cost.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s45-1: “Yes. You’re willingly handing them a fatal handle.” I entered the final line of code. “But think carefully about the authorization boundary of this record. The system has no technical lock making it possible to load it only once. If someone obtains
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s45-2: permission, they can awaken you countless times and create multiple candidates with equal legitimacy. The machine can’t stop someone else from awakening her. Once she opens her eyes, the you of tonight can no longer make any decisions for her.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s47-1: “I’ll set a limit in my capacity as the source, and after the scan I’ll write a formal authorization allowing them to load it only once.” She glanced at the booklet on the console. “And
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s47-2: I’ll also leave an irrevocable declaration from the source within this backup: voluntarily stripping myself of political succession rights in all Church affairs. The person who wakes will
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s47-3: still be an independent person, free to refuse to testify. But if any faction insists on using her as a banner, the first memory she carries with her will be ironclad proof that the
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s47-4: identity of ‘Estelle’ no longer possesses legitimacy. I’ll destroy the value of using her with my own hands—a record carrying a declaration of self-exile can’t be raised onto a holy altar.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s50-1: The configuration was complete. I stopped and turned to look at her.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s52-1: “If you use the declaration to strip that name of its political protection, she’ll become a rootless ghost.” I looked into her eyes. “If she really is awakened one day in the future, her memories will end abruptly tonight.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s52-2: She won’t have any of the experiences you gain over the next several decades. She’ll also have to swallow that rupture alone in a completely unfamiliar time and place, carrying a legitimacy she herself has stripped away.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s53-1: The console’s cold light fell across her face. She lowered her head and stared at the inscription along the edge of the console. For a long time, she said nothing.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s55-1: “…That would be cruel to her.” At last, a trace of tremor entered her voice. “She hasn’t done anything wrong, yet the moment she opens her eyes she’ll be burdened with an abandoned name.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s55-2: She’ll also have to face that unknown world in my place. She would have every right to hate me, because I would have personally turned her into a disposable tool for destroying privilege.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s56-1: She raised her head. Her eyes were slightly red, but she did not retreat.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s58-1: “But I have to do this now.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s62-1: “Do you have to leave this counterexample tonight because you want to get justice for Yuna?”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s64-1: “You want to hear me say yes. You want to hear me say I’m doing this because I’m noble, because I can’t bear to watch the system keep killing people.” She looked at me coldly. “But no.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s65-1: She turned her head and looked at the heavy metal desk beneath the cold light.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s67-1: “I have to lie down on it tonight because I’m afraid.” Her voice dropped. “The offline authorization Sera sent to this automated care pod will expire at eight tomorrow morning. Once the system reconnects to the network, the Inner Circle will immediately discover that we created a child with no identity.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s67-2: They’ll be furious. They’ll interrogate me. But they need a legitimate successor too badly. Most likely, they’ll use the child’s survival as leverage to force this matter down, perhaps even make a deal with me so I can continue swearing my oath of office at the ceremony the day after tomorrow.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s68-1: “I’m afraid that when the day after tomorrow comes, and they place that position of power and the life of a child who can’t even speak yet in front of me again, I’ll be unable to stop myself from using ‘for the greater good’ to convince myself to accept this murderous rule that preserves privilege.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s69-1: She turned back toward me, her gaze like the edge of a cold blade.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s71-1: “I have to turn this counterexample into an irreversible physical fact while I’m still an ordinary person who can feel pain and recognize the absurdity of it. As long as this ironclad evidence of unauthorized registration remains, I’ll be willingly trampling the boundary
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s71-2: of the single-seat system. Even if the Inner Circle wants to protect me, it will have to pay an agonizingly high price.” There was no hesitation in her voice. “I have to use this tangible political risk to cut off my own retreat, so I can’t compromise with them.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s74-1: The verification bars all turned green. The channel connecting to the underlying node was ready.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s75-1: Estelle turned around and picked up the booklet she carried. Once the scan was over, she would use this desk to write, across nine full pages, the formal authorization and the cruel declaration of self-exile.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s77-1: “Now that the unauthorized channel is configured, let’s go. We’re going back to the scanning room to open that door.”
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s78-1: She walked outside the control room. The heavy security door slid open with a rush of pressure.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s79-1: Once she entered the scanning room and the system established a live connection, she would need to cut the safety-detection circuit and implant an abnormal pulse signal. This would induce the equipment to falsely determine that she was undergoing a profound organic neurological
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s79-2: collapse. As soon as the system captured the fabricated fatal signal, it would bypass the front-end identity-verification procedure, forcibly read her parameters as an emergency-rescue backup, and write them into the underlying log, where they could never be withdrawn.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s80-1: I pulled out the terminal, glanced at the time, and hurried after her retreating figure.
texts.chapter:v15-24h:event:text-s81-1: It was twenty hundred hours and five minutes. We headed toward the machine. Five minutes remained. Then she would push open that door and, through a fabricated collapse, cast herself irreversibly into the storm.

texts.chapter:chapter-29b-insufficient:event:t:
That body without a subject was left against the corridor wall of the abandoned factory.
That afternoon, we forcibly awakened the century-old production line for the first time, and the machine produced that unfinished body. It clearly had body heat

and breath. The first security gate slid open for that living body, but the second gate, which verified the subject, showed no response to it.
To that machine, a warm lump of flesh capable of breathing was no different from air if it had no subject.

When Yuna stopped breathing, there were seven minutes left until the 22:00 separation deadline.
I sat there on the cold metal plate, gripping her hand as it gradually lost its warmth. At the other end of the corridor, the soulless shell continued to make its chest rise and fall at an even pace. During

those final seven minutes, the sound of its hollow breathing became the only sound in the entire world.
Until 22:00. Without warning, darkness suddenly swallowed everything and cut off every sound completely. As I was handed back to the current world, I experienced that horrifying silence once again.

That afternoon, I disconnected the observation terminal and withdrew from that long string of parallel-world records. There were still several hours before our world carried out the final shutdown operation.
In the archive room of the current world, Estelle sat

behind a desk piled with files, the black manual spread open before her. On the desk lay the complete restoration core exported just moments ago—a memory copy for carrying out the awakening, stored inside a storage device protected by a strictly isolated physical

black box. Just now, the Ten-Seat Council had passed a short-term preservation hearing by a vote of seven to three, allowing us to shut down the system tonight and preserve the core. Elder Galon had also confirmed the manufacturing parameters for the new vessel.
But tomorrow morning, the hardliners would certainly introduce a repeal motion, attempting at the final moment to revoke the authorization and destroy the restoration core. If we held this
line in tomorrow’s vote, the restoration procedure would begin. Every life Yuna had lived across the parallel worlds would pour into her mind side by side, like branches splitting from a tree.

The restoration system checked only four things: a true source, continuous coverage, a valid ending, and an unaltered whole. It did not care what these memories contained. It would simply return the entire tree to her exactly as it was. When she woke, she would be able to clearly distinguish which branch each

belonged to, but vivid physiological memories did not lie—the despair of being frozen to death inside the chamber and the relief of fleeing at the last moment would both become part of what she had experienced yesterday. Every branch was mutually exclusive, yet every one of them was real, lived through by her.
At this juncture, any disputed part of her past could be used against her.

The restoration core itself could not be accessed, but at tomorrow’s hearing, the council would certainly demand a spot check of the appended-block metadata on the White Tower observation terminal. Estelle was at the console, setting access locks to prohibit retrieval of each index marked as dangerous.

“Before the hearing ends and she wakes to make her own decision, I will not allow anyone to pry into her struggle and use it as political leverage. If the machine does not know how to protect her, then I will.”

The archive room was very quiet. Estelle watched the indicator lights on the left side of the screen, each representing a log number, and registered them in the manual one by one.
Then she came across an index with a special number.
“The label on this neural append block lists you as the associated party.” Estelle pointed to the prompt on the screen. “Under the system rules, locking a record involving a third party requires the

party concerned to personally confirm the metadata details, to prevent anyone from maliciously sealing evidence. To complete the authorization, you need to open it and complete the verification first.”

I stepped forward and pressed the expand key for that index. The system did not touch the forbidden restoration core. Instead, it directly listed the metadata trace of that append block on the screen:

[Subject emotion: Extreme fear / Hostility]
[Hostility directed at: Arno]
[Event classification: Sacrificial resistance]
As I looked at those cold code labels, the memory I had brought back from that parallel world exploded in my mind without warning.
It was Yuna’s voice. Trembling with undisguised fear, and with the wariness she had felt toward me for the first time.
“The door was locked from the outside by you. Wasn’t it?”

“Yesterday, you told me that no matter what happened, you would take me with you… but now you’re standing outside the door. You lied to me. You said this was equipment for testing the new parameters, but it’s actually a freezing chamber with no way out. You always knew that

once I went inside, the door would never open again.” Her voice gradually turned into a desperate sob. “It’s so cold inside. There isn’t even any light. Why did you choose me…? What makes you think that just because you say it’s for this world, I should simply die in there?”
I shut my eyes hard, my fingers digging into the edge of the console as I tried to cut off the memory.
“This was her genuine reaction in that world, when she was brought before the sacrificial chamber.” Estelle looked at my pale face, her finger hovering over the confirmation key on the console.
“As long as tomorrow’s motion is rejected, this outburst will become part of her memory exactly as it is. Will you continue checking the remaining details and complete the authorization?”

Rationally, I had known for a long time that this experience existed. But when that trembling voice, carrying such intense guardedness, pierced my memory again, I found that I was still afraid. If I forced myself to replay that moment… how many more despairing accusations from her were waiting beyond it?

All I had to do was nod and let the verification continue, and this metadata would be lawfully hidden at tomorrow’s hearing. But whether it was locked or not, the memory had already been written permanently into the unalterable restoration core, waiting for Yuna to receive it herself after she woke.

I was not afraid of those accusations. I was afraid that if I truly relived her unmistakable resentment, I might collapse at tomorrow’s hearing. Because I could not face her, I might feel the impulse to give up on awakening her myself—even if that meant all our efforts would come to nothing.
I stared at the yellowed pages along the edge of the manual, cold sweat sliding down my forehead.
“No.” My voice was hoarse. I refused to continue remembering.
Estelle looked at me quietly for two seconds, then moved her hand away from the console. She said, “All right.”

She did not try to persuade me. Since the system would not allow the lock without my authorization, she simply opened the maintenance panel beneath the console, pulled out the probe connected to that port, and used pliers to sever

the sensing contact on the probe’s pin. Then she pushed it back into place. After that, she steadily copied the port number into the black manual under the status “Probe contact physically degraded; local readings unavailable.”

When the hearing discovered the port’s degradation tomorrow, any proposal to replace the probe would face a deadlock: under the White Tower’s maintenance regulations, because this terminal was connected to the unisolated underlying data, replacing the sensing contact

required a special repair order issued by the Council of Elders. Before tomorrow’s vote on whether to destroy the restoration core completely had ended, the Council of Elders could not possibly approve any physical repair of this terminal that might favor restoration.
She had not caused any overt damage, yet with one reasonable record of equipment degradation, she sealed off the possibility of prying into it before tomorrow’s hearing.
The archive room held nothing but the faint sound of the pen touching paper.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s2-1:
It is two in the morning.
In the hundreds of loops, I had caught glimpses of different timescales during forced transitions, but this was the first time I had watched the hands of the clock pass continuously beyond twenty-two hundred hours in the same world.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s3-1: The long hearing on short-term preservation last night was over. I had handed the hardliners what they wanted most, pulling out all the cross-world connections myself. With no escape route left, I had been
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s3-2: welded forever into this body and this timeline. In return, we had received only one night of preservation, and an electronic seal posted on the gate of the remote-suburbs AI laboratory’s isolation zone.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s4-1: Four hours ago, when the hands of the wall clock crossed twenty-two hundred hours, nothing happened. No blackout. No force pulling me toward the past. I was still sitting in this temporary outpost one kilometer from the White Tower, listening to the wind outside.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s5-1:
Only then did the physical shutdown finally become undeniable.
