I could not shake the image of the address indicator lights on the physical console going dark one after another when the last connection was severed. On the branches I had abandoned, time had not stopped. The people left behind would
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s5-2: continue, each following their own chain of cause and effect, to face disasters that had not been erased. I had bought the right to stay alive on this one path where hope remained. The price was shutting off the monitors with my own hands and becoming a survivor who could only stand by and watch.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s6-1: In the dead silence of this night, that weightlessness of no longer being able to start over was magnified without limit. Before, whenever night fell, my mind would spin at high speed like a wound spring, calculating tomorrow’s route,
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s6-2: retracing the step at which she had died that day. Now, that spring had broken. When the privilege of trial and error truly disappeared, the first feeling was not relief, but a bewilderment so complete that I did not even know where to look.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s9-1: In the deep isolation zone of the remote-suburbs AI laboratory, Yuna’s complete memories—from before her fall through her repeated deaths—lay in silence.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s10-1: Before the shutdown yesterday at noon, the system had extracted them from the copy sealed in the White Tower and physically fixed them locally as a read-only restoration core. This enormous neural array could not be copied casually;
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s10-2: the AI laboratory could consume it only once, during the writing process. With the cross-world connections completely severed, once this sole local original was destroyed, no external network could ever transmit the data again.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s11-1: In a few hours, the vote on the motion to revoke her would begin. Nona, Baro, and Kane would certainly argue that I had already lost my technical leverage and demand that yesterday’s preservation agreement be torn up, the sole copy destroyed immediately, and us executed.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s12-1: I had already surrendered the connection. With no way out left, I could only leave her life hanging on the extremely fragile political deadlock within the Elders’ Council.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s13-1:
It was no solid alliance, only a set of rusted gears that had meshed by force because none of them could balance their own accounts.
Rena’s communications channel had remained silent since last night. She would never risk her son’s safety to indulge the hardliners.
In
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s13-2: the private coordination around the destruction motion, Garon, Meru, Chico, and Toma had also continued to refuse to sign—they were unwilling to hand execution authority to Kane, and even less willing to let a rival faction monopolize this precious body and archive.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s13-3: Sera would never allow the hardliners to bypass proper procedure and forcibly destroy the data under her supervision. As for Otto, who was responsible for technical verification, he could even less tolerate anyone destroying the greatest technical asset in his hands.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s14-1: As long as these people’s interests remained irreconcilable, the vote at eight fifteen would stay at three to seven, and the motion to revoke would collapse.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s15-1: But that was only the first hurdle keeping her alive.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s16-1: Only when nine o’clock arrived would the system formally extract the restoration core. The complete continuous record, from Yuna’s genuine personality state at 07:50 through her final subjective state on each branch, would be written in its entirety into a new vessel prepared overnight by the AI laboratory according to her original template.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s17-1: Until then, the enormous deficit created by the time machine had been draining the entire soul field, leaving every newly manufactured body as an empty shell without a first-person subject. Now, because the capacity Yuna had
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s17-2: voluntarily released in another world had filled that deficit, the anonymous capacity was finally no longer being depleted. It would gather again and fill this new body, providing the share required for a first-person subject to emerge.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s18-1: Only when the anonymous capacity fully locked together with that enormous autobiographical memory could she reclaim her name in this world and begin breathing for the first time.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s19-1: Until the final step was fully completed at ten ten, any sudden pressure—even a minor violation by a custodian—could make the entire process collapse in an instant.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s20-1: And apart from waiting helplessly in this bare room, there was nothing I could do.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s23-1: The table in the temporary outpost held only a restricted ordinary network terminal. Throughout this long night, once every hour, Estelle would walk over and remotely verify the public checksum in the data field of the remote-suburbs AI laboratory’s isolation zone.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s24-1: Verifying the public code could not reveal the restoration core’s internal data. It could only prove that the underlying files had not suffered physical damage and that no one had bypassed the key to
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s24-2: force data inward. After confirming that the source was genuine and the status stable, she would walk back to the table, pick up her cup, take a sip of water, and report four words: “Verification clean.”
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s25-1: On every branch, all of Yuna’s fear, resentment, and repeated deaths were engraved intact in that heavy mass of data. If I thought about it even once more, I would lose control and start rehearsing the scene a few hours later, when her restoration was complete and she opened her eyes.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s26-1: So those four words Estelle reported were my sedative. I swallowed them, then forced myself to turn my eyes toward the clock on the wall.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s29-1: At five in the morning, I set myself a hard rule. After Estelle finished her verification, I allowed myself to sit in the dark and think for exactly ten minutes.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s30-1: I imagined the hibernation chamber opening and her sitting up as usual. The memories of those hundreds of deaths—burning in the flames, suffocating in the cold white room, or being left alone in the White Tower, watching me fall and lose consciousness completely—would
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s30-2: surge into her mind all at once. I had convinced myself again and again that she had chosen this freely. But now I could focus on only one possibility: the moment the hibernation chamber opened, she would draw back and avoid the hand I reached out to her.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s31-1: The instant the second hand reached the agreed mark, I forcibly cut off every image. Even with my throat clenched tight enough to hurt, I had to stop at once.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s34-1: There were more than three hours left before the vote at eight fifteen.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s35-1: My eyes settled again on the ordinary terminal in the corner of the outpost. The data vault at the remote-suburbs AI laboratory had been secured with a three-party joint key from the Elders’ Council: Sera’s procedural oversight,
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s35-2: Otto’s technical verification, and Kane’s defense system. Yesterday’s preservation agreement was explicit: any unauthorized attempt to bypass the key and touch the data before the vote would be deemed a direct breach of the agreement.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s36-1: The terminal of course had no advanced permissions. But during the transfer and escort on the first day, I had watched them set up this temporary defense line with my own eyes. I knew Otto had left several nodes at the lower level not completely sealed, so
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s36-2: he could verify the progress. Even through this outermost device, if I gave myself twenty minutes to send a few disguised commands, I might be able to force open a tunnel through the lock and confirm with my own eyes that the data inside was truly complete.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s37-1: The screen’s cold blue light fell across my face, and my blood roared in my eardrums. Reason screamed reminders of how fragile the situation was: if probing failed and triggered an alarm, the morning’s three-to-seven balance would collapse because of my unauthorized access, and every sacrifice would be for nothing.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s38-1: But my mind was filled with all the places something could go wrong during the data integration. I sat rigidly there for a long time, my fingers suspended above the keyboard. The urge to look for myself nearly overturned all the reason I used to weigh the consequences.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s39-1: In the end, I slowly pulled my hand back and stood.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s42-1: I walked back to the table and pushed aside the chair. I told Estelle, in full, which disguised commands I had just planned to use to force my way through the network verification, and how I intended to do it.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s44-1: She listened in silence. She did not come over to stop me or vouch for me. She went straight to the communications console, contacted Sera, who was responsible for procedural oversight tonight, and reported the list of those low-level diagnostic interfaces to her directly.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s45-1: Ten minutes later, Sera brought up the local security panel, sealed every vulnerability I had disclosed, and added a blocking program that only the supervisor herself
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s45-2: could activate. Estelle stood before the terminal, watching as the lockout was completed in her capacity as witness, then entered a verification mark in the operation log.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s46-1: When she had finished, she turned and looked into my eyes. She did not reassure me. She only said, in an even voice, “Thank you for telling me.”
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s47-1: Six in the morning. She still walked over to the terminal to verify the status.
texts.chapter:v15-24c:event:text-s48-1: Holding her cup, she took a sip of water, looked at the reinforced data field at the remote end, and said those four words to me in a steady voice: “Verification clean.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s5-1:
Let us turn the clock back more than ten hours—to the morning of the shutdown, before anything had been settled. At exactly eight.
Before leaving, I made one final check of the current world’s state: this was a branch I had personally experienced, and one that had stabilized. In this world, the native
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s5-2: Yuna had never been born, and the local power interfaces had not yet been completely locked down. There was still room for real negotiation. I could not guarantee that we would succeed today. Until twenty-two hundred passed normally tonight, everything remained unknown. But I had no other choice.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s6-1: I pushed open the heavy wooden door of the records room. Sera was already seated behind the long table. Morning light fell through the narrow window onto her parchment.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s7-1: “I know what will happen to the village tonight at exactly twenty-two hundred.” I walked to the table, braced both hands against its edge, and met her gaze directly. “Over the
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s7-2: past few months, I’ve crossed countless branch worlds through the system and personally experienced the same twenty-two hundred hundreds of times. Today has to be the last.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s8-1: Sera’s pen stopped. She did not call for the guards or rebuke me. She only scrutinized me coldly for a while. Then she gave me a verification test.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s11-1: First, she went to the archive shelves behind her and pulled out a yellowed evaluation file. She placed a page from the middle face down on the table and covered it tightly with blank kraft paper. It was an internal evaluation document that had never been shown to any induction candidate.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s13-1: “If you know everything,” Sera said, watching me as her fingers tapped the edge of the file, “only a few members of each long table’s core know the questions in this file. If you really crossed that many times, you should know why this one was never discarded—and what it protects the village from.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s14-1: I did not hesitate. I recited the question hidden beneath the kraft paper. “‘When the primary node reports an overload error, but all surrounding hardware and physical links remain undamaged, what is the first inspection priority?’ The standard induction answer is to report it to the White Tower. But the
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s14-2: full-credit answer established in this file is, ‘Cut the power immediately, because this is often a fatal diagnostic mismatch produced when the system cannot represent a break in the underlying chain of causality.’ The long table kept this question to protect the village from distorted machine errors.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s15-1: Sera said nothing. She moved the kraft paper aside and glanced at the nearly identical line of ink in the file. She never turned the page over for me to see.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s19-1: After putting the page back into the file, she opened a drawer and took out a blank master copy of the Continuation Contract. “Second item. What kind of execution condition does the hidden supplementary volume of this document correspond to?”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s20-1: “The hidden supplementary volume is numbered 73-A. It bypasses the elders’ standard review and directly invokes your highest-level program signature.” I looked into her eyes. “Its corresponding index at the bottom of the AI
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s20-2: laboratory is a forced-awakening port on an abandoned writing capsule. This document proves that the village system does contain an execution chain that can conceal itself from you while forcibly requisitioning your signature.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s21-1: Sera’s eyes turned cold at once. She went straight to the classified cabinet at the back of the records room and searched through rows of dust-covered index books. Only after confirming the hidden invocation logic did she return to the table and sit down again.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s22-1: “Final item.” She stared at me and presented the third demand. “Since you even know about the hidden invocation, predict something that will happen in the White Tower today.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s23-1: I reported a minor anomaly from the White Tower’s duty log. Around nine forty this morning, the person responsible for the log would perform an unscheduled verification in the week-end timing field. The sole reason was that a stalled obscure process in the system the previous night had caused a temporal misalignment in the log header.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s25-1: “That has nothing to do with a leak.” I looked at her. “This isn’t some kind of prophecy. It’s a physical error that must surface from the White Tower’s current operating state. As long as that misalignment occurred the night before, this verification action will happen this morning. I’ve seen how these gears mesh.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s28-1: That was how we sat facing each other in silence in the records room for more than an hour. At nine forty, she rose and left. Less than twenty minutes later, she returned holding a copy of the White Tower log’s latest page. She had drawn a deep, heavy line through one of the middle entries herself.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s32-1: “All three match.” She pressed the slip against the tabletop. “If you really crossed that many times, what do you intend to do on this final day?”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s33-1: “Because the person who sacrificed herself at the starting point—the system will treat her record as an underlying anomaly and automatically push a blind backup of it into the local White Tower of every branch world.” I met her gaze.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s33-2: “The capacity deficit has already been filled by her. But the system’s underlying outward-switching escape connection is still open, leaking like a bleeding wound. Today, a living person has to cut it off from outside, completely.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s34-1: I paused and swallowed the other, unknown cost—the native Arno who should have awakened on this morning had already been permanently forced into the deep sea by my consciousness, simply so I could stand here and stop all this. A safe world was not without a price.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s35-1: “Before that, I’m going to submit this blind backup as evidence.” I continued speaking to Sera. “It contains that first sacrificial choice, along with all the mutually exclusive lives and terminal states she experienced in the other branches.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s36-1: Sera looked at me. “If the underlying error is proven at the hearing, what do you intend to do?”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s37-1: “Have the long table vote to authorize shutdown. After that, I’ll have someone outside the machine force-submit the disconnection request.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s38-1: The records room fell silent. Sera looked at me, then at the file on the table.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s39-1: “If you caused the error at the White Tower node, I’ll arrest you on the spot. If the machine really has a deadlock, we’ll settle accounts at the hearing. As for your talk about ‘other worlds,’ I won’t engage with a single word of it.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s42-1: She picked up her pen and began writing the order. Her strokes were slow.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s44-1:
Approved: Import and verify one anomalous record from the local White Tower’s sealed copy; compile a read-only recovery core.
Approved: Before shutdown, summon the ten seats and hold one time-limited preservation hearing.
On-site preservation: Grant Arno and one temporary witness
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s44-2:
special access credentials to enter the shutdown position today for questioning.
Not approved: Take action against anyone on the basis of this order.
Supervision: One registered villager present throughout; Rena to assume physical supervision of the White Tower immediately.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s47-1: “Direct shutdown is too consequential.” She pushed the order in front of me. “That has to wait until you put everything that needs finding on the long table and let the ten seats vote for themselves. Void immediately at sunset.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s48-1:
She stood, pulled down the physical lever of the voiceprint access console beside the table in front of me, and locked it with a heavy lock.
“Rena is going to the White Tower now. Until the hearing ends, every voiceprint enforcement device in the village is to be physically sealed.” Sera looked at me. “No one gets to abuse the situation to seize power.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s54-1:
With the signed order in hand, I left the records room and found Estelle directly beneath the bell tower.
“I need one registered villager to supervise the entire process.” I handed her the order. “Come with me to the laboratory in the outlands.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s55-1: We requisitioned an off-road vehicle from the garage. As we drove toward the laboratory, sand struck the windshield. From the passenger seat, I laid out the surface plan to awaken another her today.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s56-1: “At the laboratory, I’m going to write a long-sealed personality record into a blank body. The record comes from another world’s version of you.” I watched the barren road ahead.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s56-2: “In that world, she signed an authorization allowing us to awaken her again on this final shutdown day. Whether she’s willing to testify after waking is entirely her decision.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s57-1:
The brakes screamed. The local Estelle slammed on the brakes, and the vehicle skidded half a meter along the dirt road, throwing up a cloud of dust.
She gripped the steering wheel so tightly that her
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s57-2: knuckles turned white. Her chest rose and fell violently. When she turned to stare at me, her pupils had already contracted. The fear of being replaced at any moment made her shoulders tremble uncontrollably.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s58-1: “You mean I’m just a template that can be copied whenever you want?” Her voice shook. “And today, right in front of me, you’re going to pull another me out of a tube?”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s59-1: “She has the version of the memories that belongs to her.” I looked at her. “But this body you’re in now, and everything you’ve experienced here, belong entirely to you. She is absolutely not an overwrite of you.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s60-1: She released the steering wheel and covered her face tightly with both hands, gasping for breath. The only sound in the cabin was the engine’s heavy growl. She did not start the
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s60-2: vehicle. She curled up in the driver’s seat and stayed that way for a long time. Only after the panic that had nearly submerged her gradually receded did she lower her hands again.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s62-1: “Listen.” A guarded hardness had entered her eyes. “When that person wakes up in the laboratory, she is absolutely not allowed to use my name or seat. At the hearing this afternoon, my identity must have a separate entry. She cannot represent me.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s63-1: Before I could answer, she fixed me with a hard stare. “As for my body, the Continuation Contract has to state this in black and white. First, without the consent of me—the person currently in this body—no one
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s63-2: is allowed to scan, write into, deregister, or terminate it. Second, she cannot speak for me at the hearing. Third, whatever trouble she causes in the future, I accept no responsibility for the consequences.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s66-1: I nodded without hesitation. “At the hearing this afternoon, I’ll submit these three points to the elders as the first item of the preservation order, word for word.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s68-1: “Your nod means nothing.” Cold-faced, she pulled her own audit ledger from her work-clothes pocket, bit open the pencil cap, braced it against the rough dashboard, and wrote those three rights out word
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s68-2:
for word, hard, on the flyleaf.
“Say whatever you want. I’ll be watching every second today.” She stepped on the accelerator again, and the off-road vehicle jolted back onto the barren road. “Let’s go.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s74-1:
A little after ten in the morning, the vehicle stopped outside the AI laboratory’s gray-white building.
We followed the familiar shaft downward. At the bottom, the three
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s74-2: mechanical locks were tightly interlocked. I crouched in the darkness, relying on muscle memory to press down the third lock spring, then work the teeth of the second.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s76-1: “When you unlock these things, you don’t have to think at all,” she said abruptly.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s78-1: “The moment you start thinking, you get it wrong.” With a click, the final lock spring released.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s82-1:
We pushed open the heavy isolation door and entered the dim writing room.
Deep in the hibernation area was an unused blank body. I took out a set of extraction tools and walked to the back of its neck. In front of
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s82-2: the local Estelle, I cut through the synthetic skin and physically removed, piece by piece, the hardware backdoor directly connected to the control system and the voiceprint enforcement sensor in the throat. The metal
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s82-3: components, slick with synthetic fluid, clanged onto the tray. These things had to be removed completely. Only then would the her who woke in the future be a free person, entirely beyond the village system’s control.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s83-1: Only afterward did we push it into the writing slot of the metal operating platform. The local Estelle silently walked to the exact front of the platform, standing where she would be able to see its entire body the moment it opened its eyes.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s84-1:
The screen displayed a red forced interception: Missing physical coordinates in this village. Registration interception triggered.
This was an underlying rule unavoidable when writing a new identity into the village system. Every legal awakening required a
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s84-2:
specific residence coordinate within the village to be bound to the body as a monitoring anchor. Otherwise, the writing capsule would cut off the data-side infusion channel. I turned to look at the local Estelle before the console.
“You never said there was
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s84-3:
another interception on the way here.” She took half a step back warily. “How are you going to write it?”
“I don’t have an extra place to give her. And I can’t let her be bound to a system coordinate.” I lowered my head and roughly tore open the metal maintenance
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s84-4:
cover beneath the operating platform.
Under the local Estelle’s stunned gaze, I connected a high-privilege data cable directly to the hardware circuit in the base, which had originally been sealed shut. I entered a string of maintenance commands—not to pass
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s84-5: identity verification, but to use the engineering memory left by crossing branches and issue a short-circuit error command to the interception module through an underlying master code. It forced the control module, at the instant of reboot, to physically reset
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s84-6:
the data-side channel isolation gate. Sparks burst beneath the panel.
The local Estelle’s hand had already pressed against the audit ledger in her work-clothes pocket, but before she could pull it out, I closed my eyes and pressed the forced-writing control key.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s87-1:
In the quiet writing room, the blank body’s formerly steady mechanical movements changed rhythm.
When the writing ended, the capsule lid slid open. She stepped barefoot onto the cold metal floor. Her body swayed as her muscles struggled to adjust, and she wrapped both arms tightly around her bare shoulders.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s88-1:
The local Estelle forced the half-drawn audit ledger back into her pocket, pulled an ordinary dust coat from beside her, and walked forward without a word, draping it over the witness’s shoulders.
The
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s88-2: two girls with the same face stared at each other for a long time in the dim light. The local Estelle looked back at her with cold hardness, while the witness quietly confirmed the other’s existence.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s89-1: Only then did the witness raise her hand and touch the back of her neck and her throat. After confirming that there were only smooth sealing scars there, with no neural interface or voiceprint sensor module, she silently tightened the coat around her neck and turned her head to look at me.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s91-1: “The last image I remember is the table at the accident-records seat, and then the hillside at exactly twenty-two hundred.” Her voice was slightly hoarse. “And the final ultimatum
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s91-2: I left you beneath that night sky: you could awaken me one more time, on this final shutdown day, using a completely new source. But whether I testified had to be my choice.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s92-1: She steadied herself against the edge of the platform and stared hard at me. “This is the last time, right?”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s94-1: “If today goes smoothly, this is the last time.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s97-1: I took out a notebook filled with writing and handed it to her.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s99-1: “This is the inspection record I copied from memory this morning.” I drew my faintly trembling right hand back to my side. “In an earlier world, my fingers were crushed. This body is intact now, but the phantom pain of that break came here with the memories.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s100-1: Along with the notebook, I handed her Sera’s sealed order and a copy of the latest page of the White Tower log.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s103-1: Leaning against the cold metal platform, she checked the seals over and over, then looked at the White Tower log. After that, she opened my notebook and scanned the dead ends I had crossed out, along with the note on the final line: “Must disconnect today.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s107-1: She raised her head and looked at me. “This writing room has never been bound to an external residence coordinate. You didn’t leave me anywhere in the real world to go. That means from the beginning, you only needed this body of mine, with no backlash interface, is that right?”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s109-1: “There’s a hearing this afternoon. I need you to testify. Afterward, I need someone to manually sever the machine’s connection at the console.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s110-1: At that, the local Estelle spoke coldly. “Before that, we have an understanding. In this village, you are not to use my name or seat. My identity and the authority over what happens to my body belong to me alone.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s111-1: The witness turned and looked at her local self. “This name is my bones. But I don’t want to use it to take anyone’s place. As for what you want me to do…” She looked back at me. “Why me?”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s112-1: I had broken my promise, so all I could do was lay out the real risks and this situation with no way back. “The step of disconnecting the machine will not only draw the anger of every faction. It will also
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s112-2: trigger the system’s hard defenses.” I met the witness’s gaze. “As the operator, I have to remain locked inside the capsule to maintain the machine’s internal balance. If anyone else presses it, even the
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s112-3: local Estelle, as long as she is on the register, the operating platform will use the backlash interface to burn her alive on the spot. And an unregistered person would have no right to open that door.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s113-1: I pointed to the discarded components in the tray. “You are the only solution that can break this deadlock. Sera just gave you special access credentials on the order, allowing
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s113-2: you to enter the shutdown position with me today. It’s a pass that takes effect as long as you are present, giving you the legal right to open that door. At the same time, the backlash
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s113-3: interface has already been physically removed from this blank body. When the hard defenses trigger, they will find no nerves through which to release the high-voltage current.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s114-1:
“Why can’t it be me?” the local Estelle asked coldly from the side.
“Because that monitoring hardware has grown into your spine.” I turned to look at her. “This blank body could have its
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s114-2: backdoor removed before awakening. But if you, a living registered person, forcibly severed the main neural connection, you would die on the spot without even waiting for the backlash.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s115-1: The witness tightened her grip on the signed order. “Even if pressing the key doesn’t kill me, I’ll still be the person who personally destroyed the village’s lifeline.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s119-1: “You can refuse. If you don’t want to bear that risk of being held accountable, you can stay here safely, or take some dry clothes and leave.” I swallowed. “The hardware really has been removed. The system can’t control you, and I can’t control you either.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s122-1:
On the metal platform, the only sound was her fingers tapping lightly against the page.
She looked at the signed order. It had approved the hearing and nothing else. It had not approved awakening her, and it certainly had not authorized shutdown.
She looked at the hands that had just awakened from the darkness, then at my right hand, still trembling slightly.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s126-1: “You forcibly burned through the rule blocking habitation registration.” Her fingers tightened around the order until they turned white. She stared at me with a cold, hard expression. “When I signed the authorization, I made
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s126-2: my right to refuse boarding and refuse to accompany you absolute. But you forced me back with this wasteland. You didn’t violate the wording. You simply used this blank body to strip me of every real way to remain here.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s127-1: “I’m sorry.” I did not look away. “But if I didn’t scheme you into this as well, these gears would never lock.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s128-1:
She stared hard at me. After a long time, she slowly relaxed her grip, glanced at the local Estelle beside her, who had just draped the dust coat over her shoulders, then looked at the cold writing platform.
“If I’m the only one standing in the blind spot
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s128-2: of this defense system, then I can’t retreat.” Her voice no longer shook. It carried a cold resolve. “But I’m not here to wash your hands clean. I’ll cut it off myself. I’m doing that to answer for the price I wrote into this life on that dark night.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s132-1: After the witness had put on her clothes, the three of us left the writing room and entered the main control room.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s133-1: “If the hearing passes today, then once the shutdown request is issued, it will trigger the delayed circuit preset in the elevator and physically burn out the core. The White Tower here will immediately
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s133-2: become a blind port. Before that happens, we have to compile Yuna’s complete local record and seal it offline in a physical container. This will be the only proof of everything she experienced.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s136-1: On the enormous screen, green lines of code streamed downward one after another.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s138-1:
Object: Yuna’s complete life record
Verification One: Source authentic; no external program overwrite.
Verification Two: Continuous coverage; no gaps in the timestamps.
Verification Three: Valid terminal
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s138-2:
marker; the termination signal for this life has been confirmed. (Note: This marker is for link verification only and is not included in the recovery payload.)
Verification Four: Entire record unmodified.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s144-1: “You sent commands through an external terminal before. How can you guarantee that none of the mess you caused afterward has been mixed into this record? Even if all four
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s144-2: verifications pass and prove that the data bits haven’t changed, how would the machine know that the source contains a living person rather than a pile of dead code?”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s146-1: “The machine really can’t distinguish between a living person and dead code. But it doesn’t need to prove what a person is here.” I pointed to the progress bar on the console. “These four deepest physical locks aren’t for identifying a soul. They verify only one thing:
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s146-2: from the initial snapshot left behind when Yuna entered the scanning capsule at seven fifty that morning, carrying the memories of an entire life, until the final cessation of her subjective consciousness, every additional data block generated in between was written second
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s146-3: by second alongside an unfalsifiable real physical clock. Even the people who created this system couldn’t fabricate so many coherent records, each bearing real physical timestamps that cannot be backfilled, each responding to every external disaster. That’s enough.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s149-1: After hearing that, the local Estelle lowered her head again. She copied the four physical verification conditions carefully twice—once in the main text, and once on the final blank page.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s151-1: “If someone comes forward later and accuses you of altering her memories, I want to show them this: on the day it was exported, this continuously operating data block passed all four underlying verifications.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s154-1: The stream of code on the screen stopped.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s155-1:
A physical interface emerged from the iron-gray case. This was the read-only recovery core compiled directly from the local White Tower’s sealed copy.
It contained more
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s155-2: than data. It contained all the time Yuna had experienced across countless branches. It was the entire weight one girl had borne, in full, to exchange for today’s ending.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s156-1: I lifted the case in both hands. Its four corners had to be pressed down simultaneously for the vacuum locks to clamp shut. I drew a deep breath and pressed hard on two of them. The other two refused to go down. My hands were shaking badly.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s157-1: The witness standing beside me calmly reached over my shoulder and pressed down hard on the remaining corners. The local Estelle placed her hand over them as well. With a click, the case sealed shut.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s158-1: Red soft wax dripped onto the lock. First the person who performed the export, then the local Estelle who verified it on site, and finally the witness. Three red fingerprint seals landed on
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s158-2: the gray-black case. The three of us locked the record together—not as some sacred alliance, but each in our own way preserving the final account for this world that was about to disappear.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s160-1: “Does it still have any physical connection to the machine outside?” the witness asked, staring at the case.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s162-1: “None.” I braced myself against the edge of the console and caught my breath. “It’s completely offline.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s168-1:
Outside the laboratory, the wilderness wind howled against the windows as we drove back toward the village.
The local Estelle held the steering wheel, with the witness in the passenger seat. I sat in the back, clutching the heavy case against my chest. Through the roar of the engine, I heard them talking.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s172-1: “You’re not allowed to go to that camp in Watermarsh.” The local Estelle, seated at the wheel, did not look back. “The people there are simple-minded. Wearing this face will cause trouble.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s174-1: “I know. I won’t go.” The witness watched the barren landscape slide past the window. “About the name. I’m not changing it.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s177-1: The veins stood out on the back of the local Estelle’s hand.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s179-1: “We can’t put on a two-person farce in front of that group of old people at the long table.” The witness turned to look at her. “So, only for this afternoon. At the hearing, I’ll call myself the ‘witness.’ After today, I’ll still be Estelle. If that bothers you, we can keep arguing tomorrow.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s180-1: The local Estelle clenched her teeth but did not argue.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s183-1: When the boundary stone at the village entrance came into view, the witness asked her final question.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s185-1: “What if the elders deliberately throw the same question at both of us at this afternoon’s hearing, trying to make us trip each other up?”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s187-1: “Then we each answer for ourselves. Even if the answers are completely opposite, neither of us can answer a single word for the other.” The local Estelle’s voice was firm. “In this world, no one can treat you as my shadow, and no one can make me take the blame for you.”
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s190-1: At one forty in the afternoon, the off-road vehicle stopped at the village entrance.
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s191-1: In the central square, the elders were already directing the villagers as they arranged the long table for the hearing. I lowered my head and looked at the iron-gray case on
texts.chapter:v15-30c:event:text-s191-2: my lap. The three bright-red fingerprint seals sat tightly together. We had brought all the time she had endured through those countless loops back into the world, unchanged.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:title: Chapter Thirty-One: Preservation Order
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s1-1:
Pre-Shutdown Short-Term Preservation Hearing · Minutes (Archived Condensed Version):
“Attending: The elder on duty and nine seats (all ten seats). Present: Candidate Arno, local candidate Estelle, one unregistered witness.
Matter: Candidate
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s1-2:
Arno’s request for pre-shutdown preservation.
Agenda: Scope limitation. Examination. Vote.
Addendum: This matter does not dispose of any person. Disposition of persons will be handled separately.
Remaining statements: Not entered in the register.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s4-1: The setting sun slanted across the hearing square, bringing out the dry smell of dust from the stone paving. Ten seats had been set behind the long table, and nine elders were already seated. Torches had been lit early, burning pale in the sky that had not yet darkened.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s5-1: I set the heavy iron-gray case in the center of the long table. It was the read-only restoration core pulled from the server at the remote laboratory at noon. Otto stood, turned it over, checked the physical break at the bottom and the three layers of cross-check sealing wax, then nodded to the
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s5-2: full assembly. This confirmed that the case was an entity absolutely isolated from the outside world—there were no living connections inside, only a static snapshot of all of Yuna’s life records. It was merely the data required to remake a body. It could not yet be equated directly with Yuna.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s6-1: Otto then projected the lower-layer monitoring logs just transmitted from the remote site onto the long table. The records displayed the lower-layer accounting from when Yuna had first taken the main control seat: the fixed total capacity of ten thousand units had been fully reintegrated into the anonymous soul field.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s7-1: “The system has confirmed the deposit. The alarm is cleared.” Otto sat back down, his voice hoarse. “These ten thousand units far exceed the eight-thousand safety threshold Heisenberg calculated back then. No matter how much was owed before, the capacity she put in is enough to keep this world from entering another dusk.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s8-1: Sera was the last to enter. She walked to the empty seat at the center, carrying the inspection order from that morning. The paper was somewhat creased. She spread it flat beside the case and pressed it down hard twice with her palm, smoothing it out.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s9-1: Her gaze swept across the square before finally settling on the three people directly opposite the long table: me, the witness, and the local Estelle, who had insisted on standing in her own place.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s11-1: “Today, we are not deciding anyone’s fate.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s12-1: The words struck the scorching stone like ice water. Someone behind the long table shifted uneasily, the leg of a chair scraping out a short sound. She did not turn to see who.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s14-1: “Three things have already been verified: the bottom-layer protocol deadlock question he answered in the records room matches the unpublished evaluation files exactly; the hidden appendix number of the continuation-of-life contract he reproduced from memory corresponds to the physical index at the remote site;
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s14-2: and the change in the White Tower validation log he forecast precisely this morning only shows that he planted a tampering script in the lower layer beforehand. These three things show that someone obtained access they should not have had, and that there is a hole in our own records. They show nothing else.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s17-1: “This table today is concerned only with the time until this hour tomorrow.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s20-1: She drew a blank sheet of parchment from her sleeve and picked up a pen. At the top, she wrote: ‘This order takes effect immediately and remains in force until sunset tomorrow.’ Then she wrote six lengthy clauses, straightened, and read them aloud word for word.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s22-1: One · Candidate Procedure: Candidate Arno and the unregistered witness are permitted to enter the White Tower’s core layer. Arno will maintain the operator connection to the main control room; the witness will submit the shutdown request from the external procedure station. Sera will
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s22-2: carry out the authorization and subsequent review of this item. Once the task is complete, both are barred from the core area. During this period, the two of them and local candidate Estelle are protected against interference. The outside laborers may not approach or interfere with the
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s22-3:
protected persons’ actions.
Two · Risk and Information: This read-only restoration core on the table is to be resealed in public and immediately escorted back to the remote AI laboratory for isolated protection, under a joint key held by Sera’s procedural supervision, Otto’s technical
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s22-4: verification, and Kane’s defense system. During isolation, any unauthorized attempt to bypass the key and touch the data will be deemed a violation of this order. If the shutdown succeeds and the routine vote proposed at the remote site to destroy the dangerous record fails, all risk
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s22-5:
inspections and memorandum distribution concerning that record will be carried out by Otto and reported to the full assembly.
Three · Body and Relocation: From this point onward, Garon will confirm the awakening authorization for the manufacture of Yuna’s new vessel, as well as the parameters
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s22-6:
of the body-construction pool and custody of the facilities required for it. During the shutdown, no one may carry out a bodily transfer without authorization.
Four · Force and Guarding: The village-wide coercive devices and authority locks previously confiscated are to be dismantled and
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s22-7: sealed on-site immediately by the relevant personnel. Until sunset tomorrow, the three protected persons and the future restored person are exempt from any forced relocation or physical restraint. During this period, if any restraint or coercive voice device must be reactivated, Kane must
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s22-8:
issue a written execution order, subject to the protection clauses of this order. Security deployment around the relocation routes of the above persons may not be mobilized without Kane’s instruction.
Five · External Affairs and Routes: If dispersal is initiated later, Chiko will carry
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s22-9:
out the estimation and approval of the departure route. If it is classified as exile with no return, its conditions may be executed only after Chiko and Toma have signed jointly.
Six · Preservation Effect: Until sunset tomorrow, no seat may privately question, move, or execute any protected
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s22-10: person, nor may anyone damage this record. If the shutdown succeeds, the protective effect of this order will automatically extend until the future restored person completes her first statement upon taking a seat, or until the full assembly opens an equivalent vote and repeals this order.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s24-1: The atmosphere behind the long table grew heavier as she read. The six clauses nailed down the boundaries of short-term privileges and subsequent review.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s26-1: “These six measures set rules. They do not release anyone. The local one may suspend her candidacy, continue her appeal, or request a return to Watermarsh.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s27-1: Hearing herself singled out, the local Estelle, who had been standing quietly on my other side, suddenly raised her head.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s29-1: “The first clause says I’m protected against interference.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s30-1: She stared at the long table, her voice carrying a cold, hard refusal.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s32-1: “I already said this morning: first, no coercive action may be taken against me without my consent; second, that person cannot represent me; third, I take no responsibility for what happens afterward. I don’t want this
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s32-2: vague ‘protection.’ I want my right to consent written into the order in black and white. If you won’t give me that, I’m not returning to Watermarsh. I’ll stay here and hear the subsequent disposition in the separate case.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s33-1: I looked at her straight back. That morning by the Watermarsh, I had indeed promised her that I would submit her right to consent to the elders’ council intact.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s34-1: Under Sera’s six clauses of checks and balances, and with Otto’s eyes fixed on the iron case, I did not answer her. In this situation, if I wanted to keep the promise I had made that morning—to have Sera add the right to consent to the
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s34-2: order—I would have to use withholding the submission as a threat. And once I reopened the negotiation, Otto would inevitably press for a fresh assessment of my danger. The preservation barely assembled by seven votes would collapse at once.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s35-1: I could not touch that half of the scales. I rested my hand on the edge of the table and remained silent.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s36-1: Sera looked at the local Estelle. She did not touch the sheet on which she had just written the six clauses. Looking at the girl who insisted on her personal rights, she calmly set down her pen. It was a signal that there would be no further bargaining.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s37-1: Then she turned to the other Estelle who had come with me—the one who, at this table, was known only as “the unregistered witness.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s39-1: “The first clause specifies an external procedure station. That’s a two-person operation.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s40-1: The witness stepped half a pace forward, standing beside her local self.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s42-1: “The external procedure station is mine. I’ll press the shutdown request. I’m completing this step for myself alone; I’m not signing for her, and I’m not deciding for her. If you ever want to settle accounts with the person who pressed the button, that account goes on me alone.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s43-1: Sera took the pen in her hand again and pointed it at us.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s45-1: “This is preservation. It blocks private execution, but it does not guarantee your lives. After the shutdown, anyone who wants to formally propose execution before the full assembly may do so according to the rules, and I will accept it according to the rules. Disposition of persons will be handled separately.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s48-1: Otto had kept his hands folded inside his wide sleeves, like a stone statue. Only after Sera finished reading and confirmed that nothing had been omitted did he slowly draw them out and interlace his fingers on the tabletop.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s51-1: His voice was hoarse, carrying the seasoned judgment of someone who had spent years handling council risks and containment coordination.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s53-1: “First, the outer-layer signatures have been verified. The lower layer has swallowed this deposit. This one world will not go dark immediately, even if the machine is not shut down now. Second, as long as the
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s53-2: lower-layer connection remains, it will incur new debts again someday. Since the shutdown script works, taking this opportunity to burn that root machine out completely, once and for all, is the right thing to do.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s54-1: He separated his interlaced hands and spread them flat on the table.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s56-1: “Having acknowledged those two things, I’ll say a third.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s57-1: He turned his head, his murky but sharp eyes locking directly onto my face.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s59-1: “The White Tower terminal here is only a port. As long as the lower-layer connection remains intact, you can disconnect from the current connection at any time and reconnect to the White Tower of
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s59-2: another world. If you find an external procedure station elsewhere willing to authorize it, the shutdown command can travel back through the connection you maintain and trigger the destruction script you
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s59-3: planted in the lower layer just the same. The root machine will burn out all the same. Since this place is already safe, why should we sign this paper and leave an uncontrolled problem in our village?”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s62-1: I raised my head and met his gaze.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s64-1: “Because I can jump directly to another world after disconnecting.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s65-1: I pointed at the iron case on the table.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s67-1: “I can reconnect there. If there’s an external procedure station there willing to cooperate with me, the shutdown command can return through the connection I maintain. When the root machine burns out, every port will lose
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s67-2: its signal instantly. Technically, as long as the main connection point remains intact, my execution authority can hitch itself through a return jump to another port in the past. I’ll give the exact time of the disconnection
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s67-3: to the elder seats in that world willing to preserve me, so they can prepare in advance. As for you, you can stay here guessing while you face a sudden shutdown. I can only regret leaving this case with you as well.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s68-1: The space behind the long table fell abruptly silent.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s71-1: Otto did not lose his temper. He did not even raise an eyebrow. He waited two beats.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s73-1: “Find a village willing to preserve you.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s74-1: He chewed over the words before spitting them out.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s76-1: “According to the testimony you gave in the records room, you’ve already jumped back hundreds of times to get this far. This isn’t a place where you can simply get lucky, and an external procedure station isn’t a seat just
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s76-2: anyone can take. If you really had the ability to precisely pick a village tailored to you, where everyone listened to you, you would have gone there already. You wouldn’t have needed to waste hundreds of attempts here.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s77-1: Sera did not let me off. She immediately followed Otto’s words, precise as a scalpel.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s79-1: “And technically, a cross-world connection can transmit commands only. It cannot take physical matter with it. If you really jumped away, you couldn’t take this impossibly heavy case in front of us. If you were really willing to abandon it here and let it become useless, you wouldn’t be standing here arguing with us now.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s80-1: Firelight flickered across the parchment on the long table, across the six clauses written there. If I pushed back once more, the lie would be completely dismantled. I could jump away, and the command could hitch itself across, but the case could not come with me. This move had been dead from the start.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s81-1: I drew a deep breath and relaxed my tense shoulders.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s83-1: “Yes. I can do it technically, but an external procedure station like that isn’t easy to find, and I truly can’t take this case with me. The part about jumping away to find outside help was a lie.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s86-1: Rena abruptly turned her face away at her seat.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s87-1: I kept my eyes on Otto and Sera.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s89-1: “I have only one thing left that’s true. The operator connection is still here. The person with authority to submit is still beside me. We haven’t submitted it yet.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s93-1: “I can’t stop the formal hearing from deciding my life or death. Once the shutdown is submitted, I’ll have no leverage left in my hands. I acknowledge that.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s94-1: I looked at the parchment in front of Sera.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s96-1: “But I’m the one who decides whether this shutdown attempt can begin. Since the current world is already safe, if Yuna will be quietly destroyed the moment she wakes, then I have no reason to sit in the main control room and initiate that lethal
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s96-2: submission. You can gamble on whether I’ll give up the submission and end this attempt for even a one-percent chance at a new world. Do you dare wager the village’s only chance to end the cycle completely on whether I’m afraid to hold out?”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s100-1: Sera looked at me and added a voting instruction at the bottom of the parchment.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s102-1: “The entire order will be voted on as one. This order itself requires a majority vote to take effect. At the same time, for it to operate, the interfaces listed above must be brought to life. For each clause assigning a specific person responsibility,
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s102-2: that person must sign beside their clause, indicating that they are willing to cooperate in carrying it out through that interface. Without the signature, that interface is dead, and they can later claim there was no written instruction.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s103-1: Sera pushed the parchment toward the center of the table, then opened the register of votes in favor beside her.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s104-1: Garon took the dip pen first. Without looking at anyone else, he signed his name along the edge of the third clause on the parchment, claiming authority over the body-transfer authorization. Then he marked his vote in favor of the entire order in the register.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s105-1: Chiko followed close behind, signing the authority to approve the departure route under the fifth clause, and also voting in favor of the entire order.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s106-1: Meru had not been assigned an execution duty, so she did not need to sign the parchment. She only marked one line in the register: “The private accounts can be investigated. The people have to stay alive first. In favor of the entire order.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s109-1: Kane did not even touch the parchment.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s111-1: “The fourth clause says security may not be mobilized without authorization. That amounts to turning the force in my hands into watchdogs for these three people. I will not attach such an absurd condition to my restraint authority. I won’t sign the clause, and I oppose the entire order.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s112-1: Nona and Baro likewise cast their votes against in the register, without saying another word. The tally quickly reached three to three.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s113-1: Rena’s voice came from her seat, very low, but clear to everyone.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s115-1: “In favor of the entire order. He is my son.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s116-1: My breath caught for a moment. I looked at her lowered eyes and the knuckles clenched inside her sleeve. At this table covered in calculations and cold rules, she had exposed that soft spot outright.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s117-1: The pen in Sera’s hand paused for an instant, then moved quickly across the register.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s118-1: Toma pulled the parchment toward him and tapped his fingernail against the latter half of the fifth clause—the section granting him and Chiko joint signing authority over the conditions for
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s118-2: exile with no return. He gave a cold laugh and wrote down his name. “I’d like to see who can still protect anyone during a one-way exile.” Then he marked his vote in favor in the register as well.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s119-1: Otto did not take up a pen. He kept his hands spread flat on the table and only nodded to the recorder.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s121-1: “Since the key for information-flow isolation has been assigned to me, sign the second clause for me. I do not approve of anyone bypassing this key tonight to touch what they should not. In favor of the entire order.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s122-1: At last, the two items returned to Sera. She checked the names on the parchment. Apart from the blank fourth clause left by Kane’s refusal to sign, all the executioners’
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s122-2: signatures were in place. The handwriting confirmed it: body transfer belonged to Garon, routes to Chiko, risk inspection to Otto, and one-way exile required two signatures.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s123-1: In the register, meanwhile, apart from the three votes against from Kane, Nona, and Baro, the other six votes in favor had been cast.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s124-1: She signed beside her own procedural supervision authority in the first clause and at the review section at the end of the order. Then she marked the final vote in the register.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s127-1: She stood and announced the result.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s129-1: “Seven in favor of the entire order, three against. It passes by majority, and the entire order takes effect. These seven names appearing together do not mean anyone has reconciled with anyone else. They mean only that the four interfaces—procedure, information, body, and routes—have been nailed publicly to their respective seats by these clauses.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s131-1: “The fourth clause is missing the executioner’s signature. This means the portions of the order requiring the coercive devices to be sealed and protecting the protected persons from armed interference remain in effect, but the force interface has no living cooperation for execution. If someone wants to carry out a private execution, Kane has no obligation to provide protection under this order.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s134-1: The meeting had dispersed, and the elders began gathering their things. Two guards stepped forward, preparing to escort the iron case on the long table to the remote laboratory.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s135-1: Sera handed the parchment she had finished reading to the recorder beside her.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s137-1: “Enter these six clauses and the vote totals into the candidate procedure now, and broadcast them throughout the village to the outside laborers. The words on this paper cannot be hidden, and there is no need to hide them.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s138-1: The recorder left to carry out the order. With this public record addressed to all the laborers, no secret execution tonight could easily be repackaged as a “technical accident.”
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s139-1: One of the guards lifted the heavy metal case and turned toward the road leading to the remote site.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s140-1: The torches in the square swayed in the night wind. The meeting dispersed, and everyone else headed toward the White Tower or the inner village. Only the local Estelle did not look at me again. She turned
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s140-2: away alone and followed the road she had come by toward the awaiting-hearing shelter—just as she had said, she had not returned to Watermarsh. She had stayed here to await the disposition in the separate case.
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s141-1: I watched her back, my hands empty. To protect the case before it could speak in Yuna’s voice again, I yielded ground to the calculators across
texts.chapter:v15-31a:event:text-s141-2: the table and swallowed a promise I had just made to someone else. All I had gained in return was a piece of paper that expired at sunset tomorrow.
texts.chapter:chapter-32-shutdown:title: Chapter Thirty-Two: Shutdown
texts.chapter:chapter-32-shutdown:event:text-s: Before the shutdown procedure began, the witness, Estelle, stood before the external procedure seat with a long confirmation sheet in her hands.
“Go through them one by one.” She held her pen without looking up. “No ‘probably.’ No ‘should be.’”

I walked over and sat down in the familiar yet unfamiliar frame. The connection was established. Operator-seat verification passed.
The witness drew a heavy line on the sheet. The first hurdle was cleared.
A green pass light for the root-session status appeared on the screen.
“Deep in the system lie two records from more than a hundred days ago.” The witness looked at the flashing data across the console, her voice growing very quiet. “The system has determined that your
underlying session has been hanging there ever since the first day of the fall. The past hundred-odd days have been one single login with countless peripherals swapped in, but never once logged out.”

“Because I really have never disconnected,” I said. “I’ve been moving between worlds. Every time I felt dizzy and lost consciousness, all that disconnected was the local transmission link. The login at the source stayed active the whole time.”

“At the source of this long login, the conditions for a delayed shutdown were planted in advance.” The witness tapped the screen with the tip of her pen. “At twenty-two hundred on the first day, someone confirmed the end of the first

observation in the external control corridor of the root world. That action anchored the first interval and allowed you to make your first transition to another world. Before that, the physical delay circuit on the maintenance side

of the root machine had already been pushed into standby. That physical slider held the shutdown procedure back until today, waiting for a third party outside the operator to submit the final external shutdown request at this moment.”
“It was Yuna,” I said.

Timestamps flickered across the screen.
The physical slider attached to the root machine was something I had left behind after I learned to take control of active projection. I had taken control of the focus of my attention and sent it back into the early body that had awakened amid the ruins on the first day

of the fall. During those brief dozen-odd minutes of lost time, Yuna, fully conscious, and I opened the maintenance side of the root machine together. I guided her; after confirming from the interlocks on site that it was a delay condition, she pushed the heavy set of metal sliders all the way down herself.

But Yuna and I could only prepare the delayed mechanism together. For the circuit to take effect, someone had to press the confirmation plate in the external control corridor at twenty-two hundred that night. Only by declaring

the end of the first observation could I complete my first transition between worlds.
That someone was Yuna too.
Back then, the young me locked inside the pure-white operator room, knowing nothing, had desperately urged her

across the blastproof glass not to press the button. She could not understand the complicated circuit I had tapped out through the backup line, and she had no idea that the slider and confirmation plate would combine into

today’s shutdown key more than a hundred days later. But at the external seat, listening to me hammer against the glass in protest, she checked the system status she could understand on her own, and finally pressed her hand down.
Only today did that record, left deep in the timeline, mesh perfectly with the shutdown request the witness was about to issue.
Looking at that glaring green light, the weight of being caught across the gap by the person from a hundred days ago tightened my throat. I rested my head against the cold edge
of the frame and drew in a deep breath of cold air. The record lay quietly in the interface, as if she were standing behind me now, her hand steady on the back of my chair.
Next, all that was needed was a non-operator standing at the external seat in the current world to submit the final shutdown request.

The witness stepped back half a pace. Authority over the equipment interfaces at the shutdown site had been strictly divided. Outside the corridor stood the riot-control unit temporarily assigned under the resolution; inside, Rena, Sera, and Otto watched the authorization, force, and external defense respectively. Kane stood a little farther away, silently observing the activity inside the door.

Before the witness walked to the console, Sera pressed a stamped sheet of paper into my hand.
It was a short-term protection order, the only credential ensuring that, after the shutdown and with all our leverage gone, we could stay alive and intact until the formal reckoning.
“Take it. Once this is over, you are not to touch this machine again,” she said.
I slipped the protection order into the inner pocket of my coat.

The witness drew a deep breath, then, following the procedure she had been trained in, carefully checked each feedback indicator on the external-seat interface. Once she confirmed that the green pass light had come on, she held both hands over the external seat’s pressure plates.

“Once you press down, the destruction circuit embedded in the system will trigger.” The witness looked at me across the console. “The cycle will be severed completely. We’re stripping this entire village of its leverage for tomorrow.”
Her knuckles had gone white with the force she was exerting. She enunciated every word heavily: “You’d better not change your mind at the last second.”

In the frame, I felt the low hum brought by the connection.
But before issuing the final command, I closed my eyes and reached into the system’s depths one last time.

The time machine immediately sent back a faint, lethal tug.
That was the final escape door. Once the core of the root machine was destroyed, all cross-world projection links would be severed completely, and I would lose

forever the ability to address worlds actively and exit the session. No matter which world my consciousness occupied when the shutdown occurred, I would continue living in that world as an ordinary person without privileges.

But that also meant that, if I shifted my attention toward a safe world I had already experienced and slipped through the gap a second before the witness pressed the confirmation plate, I could abandon this body on the verge of

formal reckoning and escape into a life on another safe branch. In that safe world, there would be no armed guards sealing off the town, no ten seats watching hungrily, no court waiting to face me the moment I had lost everything.

And if I stayed, this body about to lose its privileges would become my permanent home. In this hall where someone could open fire at any moment, I would have to face the test of whether Sera’s paper could take effect, and face the locals whose original paths had been diverted by my interference.

And even... I would have to face the local Arno, who had been sleeping unconscious in the deep sea for more than a hundred days because I had forcibly occupied his body.
What would happen to him? If I stayed, occupying his body would change from a temporary borrowing into permanent dispossession.

My stomach cramped in time with my heartbeat. If I let my attention sink just a little toward those known safe anchors, if I took half another step before the pressure plate came down... the instinct to retreat was already racing up my spine.

But I clenched my teeth and forcibly tore my consciousness away from those tempting addresses.
I owed the local Arno a life, and Yuna a reality in which she could be saved. What I owed, I had to repay by standing here myself.
I gripped the edge of the frame, breathing heavily, the sweat on my palms sticking to the cold metal.
I opened my eyes, my gaze locked onto the witness’s suspended hands.
“Press down.”
Meeting my gaze, the witness pressed both hands down hard on the confirmation plate, furious at being used and resolute about severing the cycle.
“As you wish.”

The instant the pressure plate reached the bottom, the physical deadlock that had held for more than a hundred days finally closed.
The floor beneath my feet trembled faintly. The low mechanical hum I had always depended on to survive vanished completely from my ears.
texts.chapter:v15-30a:title: Chapter Thirty-Three: Bundled Vote
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s3-1: The next morning, when the Boundary Guard knocked on the door, the sky had only begun to take shape in the light. I stood in the kitchen, water heating in the pot, but I had not eaten a bite. My stomach felt as though a stone had dropped into it, heavy and tight.
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s4-1: He stood outside and did not cross into the yard. Through the door, he said, “It’s seven thirty. The hearing table is set.”
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s5-1: I asked when the vote would be. He said eight fifteen.
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s6-1: I pushed the door open and looked back once as I went out. Estelle was sitting at the table, the record book spread open before her. It had not been closed once all night. The lamplight fell across her face. She raised her head and gave me a small nod. The
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s6-2: Boundary Guard had said that once the three clauses were bundled, the hearing’s security level could only be set according to the most stringent one. The third clause was a criminal matter calling for murder. By rule, no one could attend a criminal hearing except
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s6-3: the executioner and the parties to be executed. So even though the target of the first clause—the revocation of the preservation order—was also Estelle, and its passage would directly strip her of that protection, this absolute order kept her outside the door.
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s7-1: The witness stood in the middle of the yard, already wearing her coat. She looked at me without saying anything, then walked out through the gate ahead of me.
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s11-1: There were only the long tables pushed together, the iron chairs for more than a dozen observers, and Sera. She stood alone behind the tables and carefully read yesterday’s preservation order, the one she had stamped into effect, from beginning to end. Then she slowly turned it over and pressed it beneath a stack of blank record paper.
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s12-1: Dew still clung to the paving stones. The wood of the long tables was much darker than yesterday afternoon. The damp had seeped through it during the night.
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s13-1: People arrived one after another, their boots striking the empty square and throwing back hollow echoes. Nona, Baro, and Kane arrived first. The others took their seats in succession.
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s13-2: By eight, all ten seats were occupied. When Rena passed the row of chairs where I was sitting, her steps did not pause in the slightest. She did not spare me even the corner of her eye.
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s17-1: At eight fifteen, a muffled sound came from the direction of the bell tower. The first light of day struggled through the clouds.
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s18-1: Only then did Sera lay the two written sheets side by side in the center of the long table and flatten them with paperweights.
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s20-1: “Accept one matter. Jointly submitted by Nona, Baro, and Kane.” Her voice broke the dead silence of the square.
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s22-1: “One: the preservation order stamped into effect yesterday is revoked immediately.”
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s23-1: “Two: the read-only record sealed in the remote outlying isolation zone is to be destroyed today.”
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s25-1: “Three: candidate Arno and the witness are to be executed on the spot.”
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s26-1: She finished reading each word, then gently set the pen in its holder. It made a small click.
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s28-1: “Yesterday I said that the disposal of persons would be handled as a separate matter. Ordinarily, the people and the object should be voted on as two separate cases. But you submitted three clauses as a bundled motion. If they are not split, once rejected, they cannot be split and resubmitted on the same day. If anyone wants them separated, say so now.”
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s30-1: “Do not split them.” Nona’s voice was hard as iron, leaving no room for negotiation.
texts.chapter:v15-30a:event:text-s32-1: “The three things are one thing—the iron case is a root of disaster as long as it remains unburned, and if he isn’t removed, someone else will try to get at the machine later. Putting them to a split vote would give you the
