texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s26-2: region to support this base model. Once drained, those ten thousand people would become corpses on the assembly line. And if this gap couldn’t be filled, the vessel coming off the production line could only be a ‘hollow shell’ with no first-person subject.”
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s27-1: She stared at the lower-right corner of the blueprint. In an age that treated expendables as numbers, Vera had written her real name in tiny letters along the edge of every page. Beside
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s27-2: that name was the unmistakable approval stamp of the highest authority: “Lysenko.” The designer’s real name and the ruler’s authorization had been stamped onto the same page of evidence.
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s31-1: “So this is the external pipeline Lysenko intended to use to forcibly extract capacity from ten thousand people, the one mentioned in the archives a few days ago?” I recognized the connectors.
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s33-1: “If it had ever really been activated, the camp wouldn’t look like this.” Yuna picked up a thin notebook from the bottom of the iron box. “That plan built out of human lives was interrupted.
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s33-2: Although I used this same infrastructure when I woke up, I didn’t need to fill a gap with ten thousand corpses. I rely on the natural influx of projections from the soul field, not sacrifice.”
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s35-1: The notebook’s title page bore a neat explanation: “This base model provides only a general physiological skeleton, intended to reinforce language acquisition, symbol pairing, and spatial reasoning.
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s35-2:
No factual content is written into it.”
But in the blank margin, another line had been carved in strokes so heavy they cut into the page: “Genes can build scaffolding. They can’t read for them.”
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s38-1:
Yuna pulled the project proposal and outline manuscript for the Introductory Library from the iron box.
Beneath the stated reason for filing it was a line in Vera’s handwriting:
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s40-1: “True reason: They need to know where they came from.”
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s42-1: This foundational scientific outline, an attempt to leave behind the world’s true appearance, had been sealed in the same cell as the interface blueprints bearing parameters for ten thousand people.
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s45-1: Yuna looked at the clean first draft of the cognitive skeleton in her hands, then at the lines that had tried to force human lives into the system. She stood in front of the blueprints for a long time.
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s46-1:
Before leaving the cell, Yuna folded the project manuscript and notebook for the Introductory Library and handed them to Estelle. Then she picked up the interface blueprints bearing Lysenko’s approval and the parameters for ten thousand people.
While the boundary guards were patrolling outside
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s46-2: the door, she tore the blueprints apart through the drainage outlet at the bottom of the ventilation grille. She watched the highly corrosive acid water soak the pages until they dissolved and turned gray, the murky liquid carrying the last scraps completely into the underground drainage network.
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s48-1: “These are the records of the crime she was forced to draw in prison.” Yuna stood and watched the dirty water swallow everything. “The control room only preserves the digital blueprints used to write a complete life record. The construction
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s48-2: drawings for forcibly extracting the physical capacity of ten thousand people are gone. Without these parameters to guide them, restarting the sacrificial pipelines outside would leave the elders’ council facing technical risks it couldn’t control.”
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s49-1:
She turned around without looking at the wall again.
“She built the scaffolding for this body, but what kind of life gets loaded onto it”—she looked toward the light coming in from outside—“I’ll be the one to walk out myself.”
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s53-1:
After leaving the cell block, we boarded the boundary guards’ off-road vehicle and drove away from the laboratory.
The vehicle was stopped at the village entrance. The boundary guards escorted us onto the dirt road leading to the hearing venue. Wind
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s53-2: whipped up dust. I looked at Estelle walking beside me. She was not carrying Vera’s handwritten outline manuscript; she had carefully secured it against her body. What she held was several already-printed photocopies of the Introductory Library.
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s57-1: “When we reach the table, I’ll only hand over these photocopies.” Estelle looked at the armed boundary guards surrounding the perimeter. “After the outer-gate riot, the Ten Seats increased the armed boundary guards to three layers. Using Vera’s original manuscript to expose the origin of the base model in public would be the same as forcing them to detain and destroy us on the spot.”
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s60-1:
She smoothed the photocopies flat.
“The original never leaves my side. But through the person who handled the authorization, I’ve already let Sera know that we dug the designer’s original out of the wall.”
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s64-1: “Sera can’t get the original, and she can’t seal our mouths.” Watching her movements, I understood what she meant. “As long as we—and Yuna’s body—remain in this world, the ten seats can’t truly settle
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s64-2: down. Even if they lock us up now, who can guarantee that the other nine seats won’t interrogate Yuna in private? And who can ensure that Sera won’t secretly use the boundary guards to seize the original?”
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s66-1: “It can’t be divided, and it can’t be trusted.” Estelle nodded. “These production-line devices that can’t be taken away, Yuna—the living base model that can respond at any time—and the original we refuse to surrender. Together, they’re our leverage at the table.”
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s68-1:
Ahead, the enormous hearing square in the center of the village emerged in the wind. We had returned to the village.
Under the boundary guards’ watch, we walked along the passage. The ten seats stood high above us in front of the White Tower.
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s69-1: We stopped some distance from the square. The six laborers from the outer gate were being held there. Thun’s left wrist was still suspended against his chest in a sling, fresh blood seeping through the bandages; dust had mixed with the scab on Neiva’s forehead.
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s70-1:
When Yuna approached, Thun raised his head and braced himself against the ground with his uninjured right hand. Samo stared at the distant White Tower without saying a word.
They begged no one. They had smashed the gate last
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s70-2: night and cut off their own retreat, but these silent, badly wounded bodies refusing to keep moving people down a dead-end road were themselves a political fracture the elders’ council could not safely absorb within the village.
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s71-1: On the other side of the square stood the three one-way cabins the elders’ council had put forward as a threat. From a distance, I looked at the hexagonal flanges at the bottoms of the cabins.
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s71-2: They matched the deep-space travel specifications Vera had sketched in the Introductory Library outline exactly: these were not crude exile coffins at all, but life-support transfer components
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s71-3: for the enormous multi-level Ark at the eastern launch site. As long as this deep-space transfer route remained open, it could carry not only the three of us, but these six laborers as well.
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s72-1: At the hearing table to come, the original manuscript, Yuna’s body, and this act of defiance would all be placed on the scales together. It was no spell guaranteed to force the Ten Seats to let anyone go, but it was enough to tear open a path toward the Ark through the gaps in their mutual distrust.
texts.chapter:phase2-camp:event:text-s73-1:
Yuna stopped in front of the laborers and looked at the blood on Thun’s bandages. She nodded to him.
Then she raised her head, looked past the three one-way cabins, and faced the Ten Seats above. The hearing was about to begin.
texts.chapter:phase2-three-faces:title: Three Faces
texts.chapter:phase2-three-faces:event:text-s2:
Fragment of an Admonition · Copy:
“The comportment of young girls, Article Nine: climbing, crawling through gaps, and running are not in keeping with a lady’s conduct.
It is not that you cannot. It is that you should not.
It is all for your own good.”
texts.chapter:phase2-three-faces:event:text-s5: The last few hours before the final hearing began. A full two days had passed since the White Tower shut down completely.
texts.chapter:phase2-three-faces:event:text-s6: Yuna had just ended her brief, misaligned conversation with the local Milou and returned to the underground laboratory. The terminal screen still showed the previous day’s vote:
seven to three. The village had ultimately not destroyed her before she woke. Only a few hours remained before the final judgment that would decide whether any of us could stay.
texts.chapter:phase2-three-faces:event:text-s7: Estelle, the “Witness” awakened by the AI laboratory, was still sorting files at the long table. Yuna walked over, her fingers unconsciously rubbing the rough wooden edge. Her palms still held the dampness left by clutching the hem of her clothes to suppress her emotions.
texts.chapter:phase2-three-faces:event:text-s8: “Even if we’re sentenced to permanent exile later, we still have to make some sense of this history that belongs to the village.” Yuna looked at the old records covering the table. “The village can keep moving forward with them.”
texts.chapter:phase2-three-faces:event:text-s9: The first two wooden boxes had already been sealed. They contained backups of the White Tower incident recorders, along with a cross-reference catalogue matching successive artifacts to the village’s origins.
texts.chapter:phase2-three-faces:event:text-s1: Estelle placed a hand on the latch of the third wooden box. “These are the comparison records I just finished organizing. I extracted the source tags from the White Tower’s local recorders, the absolute clock sequence from the central relay, and the authorization trails left by the external disaster-recovery station.”

She raised her head and looked at Yuna. “If only the local markers had been overwritten, it could still be explained as a system failure. But when the three sets of data are aligned, all those reset records

are crammed into the same date that has already passed on the central relay’s absolute clock, and every trace corresponds to an active human authorization at the external disaster-recovery station. The

only explanation is that, within the same physical span of time, this machine fully experienced countless realities taking different paths. Anyone who reviewed this cross-validated data would discover

that there was more than one timeline. You were involved. You have the right to decide whether this data remains a sealed personal log of yours, or becomes public evidence the Ten Seats can verify later.”

Yuna stepped forward and placed her palm over the rough wooden lid.
“I agree to submit them as physical evidence at the hearing,” Yuna said calmly. “But after the Ten Seats verify them, I require access to this section of the archive to be strictly restricted. Whatever conclusions are

inferred from it, they must not be accompanied by speculation about how I died in other worlds. If it ever needs to be made public to the entire village, all source inferences involving the metadata must be completely omitted. Only the timeline objectively verified in this world may remain.”
Estelle nodded and affixed a seal bearing an access restriction to the box.
What remained on the long table was the most sprawling and difficult-to-classify collection of records. It was the final group of files Estelle had marked with the seal: “The Church’s Origins.”
“The machine’s core has burned out. The White Tower is completely disconnected.” Estelle stopped writing. “If we just scatter these records and throw them out there, the village’s entire
way of life will collapse in an instant. We need to sort out the roots of the Church of Convergence, and tell them which half has rotted through and which half still has to be kept alive.”
The long table was covered with old records from the era of the Great Collapse.

Among them were several Orders for the Detention and Adjudication of Heretics from the early period of the takeover, as well as the oldest Register of Relief Grain Distribution. No comparison was needed. The degree of wear along the paper edges and the broken threads of the bindings alone showed how repeatedly the

later stewards had gone through them. Beside several relief registers lay a few persecution orders in silence. Most of the handwriting had long since faded, but at the signature, the distinctive way each stroke was tapered at the end and the manner in which the ink had bled along its edges were exactly the same.
texts.chapter:phase2-three-faces:event:text-s2: At the other end of the table, Yuna was opening an early prayer manual. Its cover had no wax seal for protection against moisture, only mottled water stains. Estelle pushed
the signature on a persecution order together with the signature field of the prayer manual. It read: Lydia. The signing habits on all three documents overlapped perfectly.

This earliest recorder of the rules had written a brief procedure for communal prayer in the original draft. But beside the instruction concerning the comportment of young girls, there was a note clearly added hastily afterward:
“The west side of the tower has collapsed. Good girls should not climb.”

Yuna stared at the line.
“She tied the purely physical danger of the west side collapsing to the identity requirement of being a ‘good girl,’” Yuna said quietly.

Estelle opened several later copies. “But in the official copies left by the elders, the first half—‘the west side has collapsed’—has disappeared. They kept only the second half, erased the physical danger, and turned it into a pure rule of conduct.”

Yuna’s finger stopped on the words “Good girls should not climb.” The pain she had just forced down while recognizing the local Milou out of alignment with her now crawled back up along the corners of her eyes through the handwriting on the page.
texts.chapter:phase2-three-faces:event:text-s3: “One year, Milou suddenly wanted to climb the abandoned cooling tower. The metal supports there had already rusted through. They couldn’t bear any weight.” Yuna spoke softly, a faint tremor still lingering in her voice. “I rushed over

and dragged her down by force. I could have explained how low the yield strength of rusted metal was, told her what the gravitational potential energy would do… but the words that came out of my mouth were exactly the same as the elders’.”
She withdrew her finger. “I shouted: Good girls shouldn’t climb.”

She turned and looked at me. It was the same logic I had used in countless worlds without her. No explanation, no verification—only an unquestionable conclusion laid over all her choices. In another world,

using the earlier body, I had pushed the delayed-shutdown metal slider in that falling elevator. At the level of its original motive, that act of leaving only a conclusion and no room for choice was no different.
At that moment, Estelle tapped the table and pushed together a grain requisition order and a record of heretics executed by divine will.
texts.chapter:phase2-three-faces:event:text-s4: “One document is grain seizure. The other is murder.” Estelle looked at the files. “Both documents even bear the High Elder’s seal, and both met resistance. Thirty years ago, during the coldest winter, they forcibly requisitioned the stored

grain from every outlying tent to keep the settlement alive, and shot three people on the spot for leading the refusal to pay. The latter happened five years ago, when the elders serving as stewards claimed to have received divine guidance

and executed a villager’s family for hiding ancient books. Both killed people, but the first did not trigger a subsequent uprising, while the second became the spark that brought down that corps of stewards. Where, exactly, was the difference?”

“The underlying accounts.” I met her gaze. “The requisition thirty years ago was an extreme deprivation of survival resources, but the paper listing the harvest figures for the entire village was posted in the square. Everyone

could calculate how many people would starve after sixty days if everyone ate separately. They shot three people who refused to pay. That shot did not provoke the entire village to rise up—not because the villagers thought those

three deserved to die. Those three may truly have only wanted to save their families’ food. There was no uprising because everyone standing before that account understood: if the strongest people in the group weren’t sent to

take the food, they themselves wouldn’t make it through that winter. The force of that suppression did not come from legitimacy. It came from a countdown to the deadline of death that anyone could understand. The execution five

years ago needed no numbers and showed the condemned nothing they could dispute. If the words ‘divine will is inviolable’ were enough to seal off every possibility of questioning, then power no longer had to answer to facts.”

Estelle pulled the files toward her. She did not directly refute me, but added a footnote in the margin.
—“Compulsory distribution must correspond to a verifiable ledger of survival, not an
ineffable divine will. The necessity and lethal limits of enforcing compulsory measures shall be adjudicated separately by the subsequent council. This physical evidence is hereby recorded.”
This was not a casual note written merely to organize old records. At the hearing later, this footnote would be presented alongside the physical evidence before the Ten Seats deciding the new order.
The thickest stack of old Church records was finally packed into the fourth box.

Yuna stood and walked over to the ventilation opening by the exhaust fan. I followed, watching her carry all the deaths and futility that had truly happened. I wanted to speak, but could not find the right words.
texts.chapter:phase2-three-faces:event:text-s5: “This morning, you told me that in the falling elevator, using the perspective of the earlier body, you saw the physical switch for the delayed-shutdown circuit.” Her voice was quiet beneath the roar of the exhaust

fan. “You said you had tried to leave the choice to me. But when I faced the extinguished facility, worked out the rules of the main process for myself, and tried to press that confirmation plate in a desperate

gamble, you still stopped me. Even though, in that earlier body, you ultimately tried to bring all of this to an end for me, guiding me to push down those heavy metal sliders myself… you still couldn’t bring me back.”
She turned and looked at me calmly.
“Being deprived is being deprived. Sincere protection cannot erase the fact that I was not free. I don’t like the way you stopped me and tried to make the decision in
my place.” She paused. “But the me trapped inside the cage always knew there was someone outside holding back everything for her. I knew you truly wanted me to live.”

“So the account is not settled, Arno.” She looked at me. “The cage you tried to keep me confined in has already been smashed apart. We both have to face the final hearing later. From here on, we have to walk the road together.”

I did not apologize again, and I did not defend that decision that had crossed the line. I knew she no longer needed either.
“Okay.” I met her gaze. “Together.”
Looking into her eyes, my shoulders, tense for the entire day, finally began to sink.
texts.chapter:phase2-three-faces:event:text-s6: Not long afterward, Sera arrived at the underground laboratory with several people. She had come to collect the boxes of files early and place them in storage.
The accompanying workers lifted the first three wooden boxes from the table. Sera stood before it, her gaze falling on the final box, the one marked with the seal reading “The Church’s Origins.”
“Later, the hearing will judge whether any of you are allowed to remain.” Sera placed a hand on the heavy wooden lid. “Regarding the old rule that knowledge belonged
only to the elders, everyone at the gathering just now passed an order repealing it. From now on, no information will be classified as a ‘restricted zone’ again.”

She paused and looked directly at us. “But I will keep this box of files on my desk. I will decide the pace at which it is released to the village. They still cannot withstand the shock of suddenly losing the support of their faith.”
Yuna looked at the hand resting on the box, her fingers tightening slightly.
texts.chapter:phase2-three-faces:event:text-s7: “If you hold it too tightly, one day it will be smashed apart too.” Yuna looked across the long table at Sera.
Sera did not answer. She only nodded quietly, then turned and left with the files.

The panel overhead was pulled open, and the border guards came down to notify us that we were being transferred to the isolation cells aboveground. On this evening, so long that it seemed to have no end, we finally climbed the stairs to the surface and walked into the afterglow of sunset. Waiting for us would be the final hearing that would decide where all of us went.
texts.chapter:chapter-31-reckoning:title: Chapter Thirty-One: Reckoning
texts.chapter:chapter-31-reckoning:event:text-:
Summary of the Reckoning Case File (before the final hearing):
“In attendance: presiding examiner Sera; Otto, verification and examination; and eight other seat representatives. Observing: local candidate Estelle (independent determination). Family member one (reserved).
Party: candidate

Arno. Witness: Estelle. Unregistered woman: Yuna.
Separately scheduled case: insubordination by six workers from the outer maintenance team.
Matter: shutdown of the White Tower and border-crossing case.
Received: multiple disposition proposals in parallel.
Resolution: pending deliberation.”
Yesterday evening, less than twenty-four hours after the White Tower shutdown, Yuna finished her time in the village and was returned to the isolation cell aboveground.

From outside the reinforced glass of the isolation cell, we could see the dim tool room at the edge of the platform. After being put down, the six laborers who had taken part in the outer-layer insubordination were being held there. Two days had passed since the White Tower shutdown. This was the evening of the third day—the night before the final judgment arrived.
Watching those figures beyond the reinforced glass, witness Estelle turned her head.

“The insubordination of these six has already become a mess the elders’ council has to settle separately.” She lowered her voice. “Whether they send them back, keep them detained, or pretend nothing happened and return them to duty will all become new entries on tomorrow’s long table.”

“The elders’ council is caught in a bind now too.” I looked away. “Too many people saw the confrontation. Send those six back to the outer settlements, and the fracture will spread at once. Detain them or silence them, and there’s no way to disguise it as a facility accident.”
“So at tomorrow’s hearing, besides deciding what happens to the three of us, the elders’ council will have to settle their case on the table too.”

“We need to force open a gap and put a procedure for individual choices before the long table.” I said, “Whether they bow to the elders’ council in exchange for returning to duty, or persist in their insubordination and have their identities permanently stripped and be expelled from the village. Tomorrow, each of them has to make that decision for themselves.”
The fluorescent lights inside the cell were harsh.

Kane, chief of the boundary guards, came with the register to record them. It was a standard administrative form, used to establish temporary files for the accused before a hearing. From the other side of the bars, he asked Yuna her name. She answered. He asked where she was originally from:
“I have no place of origin.”

Kane frowned, his pen suspended in midair. He watched Yuna for a while, then asked three more questions about where she came from. Yuna concealed nothing. She answered truthfully that she was a complete subject reconstituted within the system from countless parallel, mutually exclusive lives.

After listening, Kane remained silent for a long time. The current forms had no option for “cross-world.” He could not fill in any existing outer or inner district, because that would mean Yuna, as a resident

of that district, had the right to demand the corresponding trial representative and a seat for defense. In the end, he wrote nothing. He closed the register and left the blank field behind as he walked away.

As night approached, the person delivering meals was the copyist who ran errands in place of the clergy. She pushed the tray toward us through the gap at the bottom, leaned against the iron bars, and rubbed her aching wrist. In her hand was the old steel pen wrapped in nonslip tape, the one used to record case files and statements.
Yuna watched the pen in silence.
“You wrapped it too high,” Yuna said, softly but with certainty. “Move it down half a finger. After a day of writing, your wrist won’t ache as much.”
The copyist looked doubtful, but unwound the tape and moved it down, then made two empty strokes. The point where her wrist bore the pressure was indeed much more comfortable.
“In one of the life-lines, I did the work you do.” Yuna looked into her eyes. “In that complete life on that page, I held the same kind of steel pen and did it for six years.
I wrote things of gratitude for people, things asking for blessings. I knew how to choose the words so that those who bowed their heads to speak would feel they had been heard.”
The copyist stopped. A trace of incomprehension showed in her eyes, but she did not ask. She simply hurried away.
Yuna withdrew her gaze.

“In this world, someone else is already sitting at that desk. She’s good at it too.” Yuna spoke softly. “I found that the only thing I had left to give her was telling her how to move the tape down half a finger.”
After night fell, the boundary guard keeping watch temporarily withdrew to the outer side. A familiar figure came to the bars of the isolation cell. It was my mother, Rena.
The situation outside had been taut all afternoon, but Rena stood beyond the iron bars with a calm expression.

“At tomorrow’s final hearing, besides seats for the accused, the elders’ council has the authority to initiate a public custody procedure in the name of an existing elder.” Rena looked toward Yuna in the corridor light, her voice low but carrying an unmistakable force. “You’ll sit in the reserved ‘family member one’

seat. It is an allotment for sheltering minors or unregistered persons. As long as I publicly promise at the table, in my capacity as your custodian, to accept you and provide you with a verifiable family anchor, the elders’ council cannot bypass the lawful custodial relationship and proceed directly to execution.”
Yuna stood inside the iron bars and listened quietly.
“Auntie Rena,” Yuna said. “This afternoon, I passed by Uncle Gallon and Aunt Meru’s yard. I didn’t go closer. In the courtyard, Meru came running over and asked who I was.”
Rena’s grip on the bars tightened slightly.

“That little girl looked at me with nothing but curiosity about a stranger, and a little caution.” Yuna looked at her. “In this world’s records, I have never existed. Although the long table allows you to establish this

new custody, if it is to withstand execution, the newly established anchor has to be verifiable. Otto’s examination will follow. He’ll demand that you prove the course of our life together. You have no such thing to

produce, and he’ll turn this sudden custody into collusion. I can’t ask you to stake yourself on behalf of someone with no history using a promise that can be broken so easily. It would drag you and Arno into danger.”
Yuna took a step back, retreating into the shadows.
“Leave that seat empty. As for me, I’m not willing to trade a relationship without foundations for a life, and I can’t shift the danger onto you.”
Rena looked at Yuna for a long time.

“If you don’t take that seat, they’ll treat you as an ‘unregistered woman’ with no protection from any political entity. Once the vote passes half, you’ll be executed like those heretics who crossed the border.” Rena’s voice tightened. Her fingers clutched the iron bars, her knuckles whitening with the force.
“Then let me face the long table as an unregistered person.” Yuna spoke softly.

Rena stared at Yuna’s outline in the shadows, her chest rising and falling. She looked as though she wanted to reach through the bars and seize Yuna by the shoulder, but in the end she only released her grip with a violent jerk. The iron bars gave a dull clang. Without looking back, she hurried down the corridor.
After Rena’s footsteps had completely faded, witness Estelle leaned against the wall and looked toward me.

“Tomorrow, there will certainly be people on the elders’ council who do everything they can to keep the three of us at the hearing.” She looked beyond the iron bars. “‘Joint supervision’ is the likeliest proposal they’ll put on the table. Everyone gets a little research value, and the outer settlements won’t be provoked.”
“If Otto puts that proposal forward, I’ll lay out on the long table every cost they don’t want to calculate clearly.” I continued along her line of thought. “Who gets to interrogate
us alone, who is responsible for guarding two unregistered persons, who determines the parameters for the next body exchange, and who can use force when the other seats object.”
“Ten seats can’t divide these supervision costs evenly, and forcibly separating us would create an information gap.” A faint smile curved Estelle’s lips. “They’ll
realize that keeping us here will only keep creating struggles over new centers of power. No seat will be willing to let a rival possess these assets and this knowledge.”

“Once the long table falls into this deadlock where no one will yield, and no local disposition can gather six votes, I’ll put permanent exile on the table right there.” I said, “We won’t remain in the village, and we won’t go to the outer settlements. As

long as we can clear all the political assets from the board at once, we can obtain their shared damage-control vote. When that time comes, tomorrow at the long table, you’ll have to decide with your own mouths whether to accept this non-returnable condition.”
The dead of night on the third day pressed down over the village. By then, preparations for the hearing square were complete.

Through the gap in the isolation cell, we could see that the enormous pyre had already been erected before the White Tower. Rough timber had been stacked higher than a person and soaked through with heavy oil, giving off a pungent smell. In this village,

accustomed to ending old bodies through institutionalized procedures, if the elders’ council decided at tomorrow’s hearing that it could not dispose of us by secular means, this fire would make the three “heretics” vanish together with the knowledge they carried.
The place where Rena had stood just moments ago was between this fence and that unsettling pyre.
Yuna’s family seat, which she insisted on leaving empty; the six laborers in the tool room at the edge of the platform; and the prepared pyre. Everything was already laid out in the square.
Tomorrow would be the final hearing.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:title: Chapter Thirty-One Appendix: Lamps
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s1-1: That was a dozen hours before we walked to the long table and took our seats.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s2-1: After Rena left the isolation cell, only the three of us remained in the room. That long night became our last private meeting.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s6-1: “Once we put permanent expulsion before the long table, it will be the same as boarding an ancient ark bound for an alien star.” I looked at Yuna and Estelle. “It will be an irreversible, one-way departure. We know
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s6-2: there’s a lake at the destination, and some local organisms with dark leaves. But the long-term changes in the atmosphere, whether the soil will be toxic, whether we can grow food we can digest—all of it is unknown.”
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s7-1: Yuna listened in silence. Her hands unconsciously clenched the hem of her clothes, her knuckles whitening. It was one of the few times she let her fear of losing control show. Even if that lake truly existed, going somewhere where even breathing
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s7-2: might require readjustment, where every bite of food would be a gamble with her life, was still as heavy as iron hanging overhead. She lowered her eyes and remained silent for a long time, so long that I thought she might change her mind.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s11-1:
When she raised her head again, the fear in her eyes had not disappeared. But something sharper had pressed it down.
“The clause I added to the contract back then. Other than shutting down the machine, recite the second half for me,” she demanded.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s13-1: I answered without hesitation: “‘Then live well there.’”
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s15-1: “That’s right.” Her voice was slightly tight, but her words were clear. “A dead place where even survival is a luxury… is still better than staying in a box where anyone can decide what happens to me. You don’t actually need to ask me about this.”
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s16-1: She tilted her head and thought for a moment, seeming to find that wording insufficiently precise. Then she corrected herself:
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s18-1: “No. You asked through the proper process. That’s the right way.”
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s20-1: She looked straight at me. “If you propose expulsion before the long table tomorrow, I’ll agree.”
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s23-1: As soon as she finished, before I could respond, she added something on her own.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s25-1: “But there’s another reason you didn’t ask about.”
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s31-1: “A few hours ago, when Aunt Rena suggested that I sit in the family section, I refused.” She lowered her eyes to her folded fingers. Some of her usual
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s31-2: sharpness receded, revealing a rare stillness. “The registers here were filled long ago. I don’t want to fabricate an identity and squeeze into a place anymore.”
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s32-1: She raised her eyes again and took a deep breath. “But on that alien star whose ecology is completely unknown, at least the register will be blank. I can write my own name into it.”
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s36-1: She lifted her chin slightly. “This is my own way out, Arno.”
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s41-1: After confirming Yuna’s position, I turned to Estelle.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s42-1: She sat across the rough wooden table, still clutching the old register containing the underground data.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s45-1: “I won’t cooperate with your request for expulsion at the beginning of the hearing.” Her voice was quiet, but utterly firm.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s48-1: I looked at her. “Estelle, if you don’t show your hand early, then no matter which proposal they choose, you’ll be trapped. They’ll absolutely keep you here as leverage.”
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s49-1: “I know.” Her fingers dug hard into the rough cover of the register, whitening her knuckles.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s50-1: “Then why wait?” I asked, unable to understand.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s53-1: “Because I want to wait until they read those proposals aloud in front of everyone.” She raised her head. In those eyes accustomed to watching coldly from the sidelines was a stubborn, burning heat.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s53-2: “What the long table is about to do is cut me apart from the one in the White Tower, mark us both off with a price down to the skin and bone, use her to control me, and use me to squeeze her dry.”
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s54-1: She hugged the register tightly against her chest, as if holding on to the last line of defense she had left.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s55-1: “If I take the initiative and ask them to send me away right from the start, they can pretend they never had any bad intentions and dismiss me with clean hands.” She gritted her teeth. “I refuse. I want them to
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s55-2: read those schemes they can’t show in the light aloud for the people outside to hear. Only then will I tell them that, as one of the three outsiders who must be dealt with, I agree to board the ship and leave.”
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s61-1: I leaned beside the narrow window high in the isolation room and looked outside through the gaps in the rusted iron bars. That was when I saw the lamps along the village road.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s63-1: Starting from the slope outside our cell, people stood scattered here and there all along the village road to the distant square.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s64-1: At the far end of the road, eight torches high above the square crackled in the night wind. Beyond the torches’ glow was a silent crowd.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s65-1: Some carried storm lanterns, their yellow light falling across the rough edges of their clothes. Others carried nothing, half their bodies hidden in the darkness. Among them were the villagers who had kept their
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s65-2: doors and windows shut all day, as well as outsiders in maintenance suits—the night-shift workers stranded inside the boundary after the shutdown lockdown these past few days. At that moment, they were mixed together.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s66-1: Every so often, the night wind carried a few muffled coughs or the faint rustle of cloth. No one shouted, and no one tried to charge through the boundary guards’ line, but even in the darkness, some unrest that had not gone out could still be felt.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s67-1: They simply stopped there along the only road to the hearing grounds, using one dim lantern after another to light the village road in broken patches.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s68-1: I stood before the bars for a long time, my view filled with the distant torchlight.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s69-1: Estelle came up behind me. We watched the long, silent line of people through the high window for a while. Neither of us said anything.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s74-1: Several hours later, just as the first light began to pale the sky, Chiko appeared outside the isolation room window. He was wearing that old robe that hung loosely on him. The boundary guards outside seemed to have received some kind of tacit permission and did not drive him away.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s76-1: “Did you call those lamps on the village road here last night?” I asked him quietly through the iron bars.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s77-1: He made no attempt to hide it.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s79-1: “All I did was have a maintenance worker who rotated out during the day carry a message outside at dusk on the day before the hearing: the next long table will decide the life or death of nine people.” Chiko looked
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s79-2: at me, weariness born of long experience in his eyes. “You three plus the six laborers makes nine. As for the local Estelle being held in the White Tower, she was never on the judgment list. But look outside—”
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s80-1: A gust of wind passed. He hunched his neck and tucked both hands into his sleeves.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s82-1: “You think I wanted a scene like this?” He exhaled a cloud of white breath and looked at the morning fog outside. “The White Tower has stopped operating. If the long table can quietly deal with nine people behind a closed door today, tomorrow it can deal with anyone in the village the same way.”
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s87-1: The long day dragged past in dead silence. Around noon, to avoid the unrest murmuring outside, the boundary guards temporarily transferred us underground to the experimental area for detention.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s88-1: When evening finally fell, a boundary guard vehicle carried us, along with the six laborers brought over from another isolation area, back into the village. Figures had already gathered in the deliberation square before the White Tower. We were escorted toward the enormous unlit pyre.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s89-1: The crowd stationed outside along the way had already been cleared back into the distance by the boundary guards. But when the hearing grounds’ torches lit the entrance to the square again, everyone could see the dozen or so unlit storm lanterns left beneath the stone steps.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s90-1: They had been deliberately left behind when the crowd was forced to withdraw during the day. They had not been dropped in haste. They had been placed neatly on the steps, some even hung from the stone pillars beside them. Whether the outer boundary guards
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s90-2: had received someone’s tacit permission or had their own reservations, they did not clear away these obstructions. At the boundary between the last light of dusk and the torchlight, the cold lanterns stood openly along the only road to the hearing grounds.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s93-1: Before the hearing formally began, everyone was already seated around the long table. Sera stood alone at the entrance to the road for a while. She simply watched the lanterns in silence as the evening wind passed over their glass panes, producing faint hollow sounds.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s94-1: When she walked back to the presiding seat and faced the people in the hearing grounds and the hundreds of eyes watching from far outside, she did not immediately unfold the sheet describing the voting procedure before her.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s96-1: “Last night, there were people on the village road leading here.” Sera’s voice sounded stiff in the broad hearing grounds.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s99-1: “The lamps they left behind when they were forced to withdraw are still outside.”
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s100-1: She picked up a pen and drew a hard line across the very top of the sheet describing the voting procedure before her.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s102-1: “For every proposal, we’ll make the motion here, record the names here, and enter it into the final text on the spot.” Sera raised her head, her gaze moving slowly across each elder seated around the long table. “The final text takes effect as soon as deliberation ends. After the session, it will be posted directly on the noticeboard outside the boundary.”
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s103-1: She slapped the pen onto the table with a sharp crack. “If anyone has an objection, raise it now. We’ll begin by voting on this procedure.”
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s104-1: One Inner Circle elder frowned and was just about to say something.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s105-1: Otto sat in the corner, his fingertip digging hard into a wooden note tablet. Through the open doors, he glanced at the empty storm lanterns by the entrance. Then he suddenly cut off the voice that was about to protest.
texts.chapter:v15-31b:event:text-s107-1: “…None.” He pressed the wooden tablet onto the table and said in a low voice, “Record the names.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:title: Chapter Thirty-One: Final Hearing
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s2-1: On the evening of the third day after the White Tower shutdown, the final disposition hearing to decide whether we stayed or left officially began.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s3-1: As the various proposals were dragged through a long struggle in the night, torchlight wavered across the stone-paved square. Sera held her pen, lifted her eyes from the agenda, and pointed straight at me:
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s5-1: “On the first day, the preservation vote was seven to three, approving a short-term preservation order. On the second day, the breach-of-agreement execution vote was three to seven, and they failed to kill you immediately. Today we go
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s5-2: through every proposal for final disposition again. First item: execute on the spot. We’ve just confirmed it. Still only three votes—not half. Under the rules, we move on to questioning the subsequent plans. Finish what you have to say.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s6-1: Bracing my hands on my knees, I slowly stood from the statement seat.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s9-1: “Three points. One: the day before yesterday at twenty-two hundred, the timeline passed normally. No reset. Two: the coupling core maintaining the cross-boundary connection has been physically burned out. The shutdown is completely irreversible. Three: the variable she released back then has already filled the gap.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s10-1: The witness, Estelle, calmly pushed three pages across the long table—the shutdown-night observation log bearing her signature, the inspection record confirming the local port’s telemetry disconnection, and, last,
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s10-2: a receipt for the variable intake exported from the White Tower’s lower level ten years ago. The receipt recorded that, at that moment, the local port had received a capacity injection exceeding eight thousand units.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s11-1: The machine had no global ledger. It would not directly announce that the gap had been erased. But this injection, exceeding the safe computational capacity Heisenberg had recorded back then, together with the fact that there had been no reset the evening before yesterday, was enough to piece together the final result—the price had already been paid.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s12-1: The three pages lay neatly side by side on the long table, white enough to hurt the eyes.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s15-1: Across the table, Otto did not even look at the three pages. He simply lowered his eyelids, set the string of wooden tokens on the tabletop, and worked them forward with his thumb, one by one, slowly.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s17-1: “Yuna paid for the gap with her life back then. That debt was settled long ago,” he said quietly, without a trace of fluctuation in his voice. “So no one died when the machine stopped the day before yesterday. That wasn’t your achievement.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s18-1: He took his hand completely off the tokens and crossed his arms over his chest.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s20-1: “And burning out the core means you can no longer cross the Boundary. Those worlds will continue running independently, and you can never obtain any more information from them. Our hope of extracting secrets from other worlds through you is gone.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s21-1: Silence fell over the long table.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s24-1: “So I have no other worlds to jump to either. Jumping has to pass through that burned-out root machine, which is exactly why I admit that picking a compliant world and turning the switch into a local coercive bargaining chip was a lie meant to deceive you.” I
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s24-2: answered him without emotion. “I also said at the preservation hearing that Yuna had already bought a night in which the dusk would not repeat. The only real bargaining chip I used to exchange for short-term preservation was my refusal to cooperate with the shutdown.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s26-1: After a long while, Otto slowly reached out and rolled forward the wooden token that had stopped halfway.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s28-1: “Second proposal: collective absorption. Give the three of you residence in the Inner Circle, but strip you of every authority, with all ten seats of the elders’ council jointly bearing the secrets you carry.” He raised
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s28-2: his head. “But it won’t work. The hardliners will never agree. And putting three people who can release new knowledge at any moment into the Inner Circle would immediately change the balance of power at the long table.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s29-1: I did not argue. I answered at once:
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s31-1: “That’s not all. Becoming part of the Inner Circle requires trust and tied interests, and we have neither. If you forcibly pull three mutually suspicious people into it, you only add three sources of internal conflict that could explode at any moment. The second proposal was never workable.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s34-1: “If collective absorption won’t work, then take a step back and carry out a variant of the second proposal—separate confinement.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s37-1: Sera’s pen immediately moved across the paper: “Record: separate-confinement proposal, proposer Otto.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s40-1: “The three of you remain here. Three rules.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s42-1:
“First, Arno. You were born as new blood of the Inner Circle. Under the rules, you will go through the association and absorption procedures again. The Inner Circle will determine the parameters of your future bodies.”
“Second, Yuna, who filled the gap back then, receives a special extension of life
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s42-2:
on the basis of merit and is supported inside the Inner Circle. As for the witness, find another place to confine her. No one may make contact.”
“Third, what you hand over is kept by the Inner Circle. We schedule regular questioning for you. My seat decides who has authority to call up the records.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s45-1: Sera drew the paper toward herself.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s47-1: “The third point must have a dedicated audit sheet attached,” she added coldly. “The presiding seat must review it every thirty days. Once the deadline passes without a signature, all archive-access authority expires.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s49-1: “The authority and responsibility for the second point belong to the Boundary Guard. Prison keys, shift rosters, and visitation records are all handed over internally by the Boundary Guard.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s51-1: “Any archive access requires several parties to sign at once before the cabinet opens.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s53-1: “One thing at a time. Don’t make a mess.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s54-1: The long table fell silent at once. The gaps between the ten seats had been exposed in the allocation of control over the three of us.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s56-1: “The rules for control are finished.” Otto stared at me. “Your answer.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s59-1: I looked at the proposal sheet they had been fighting to revise.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s63-1: “The rules you just argued over and arranged aren’t deciding whether to protect yourselves from me. You’re deciding who, starting tomorrow, can pry extra power out of these few prison keys.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s66-1: “And when you questioned Estelle just now, you confiscated the manuscript of The Enlightenment Archive.” I looked straight at the long table. “It contains the formulas Vera wrote by hand back then—she
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s66-2: demonstrated the theoretical possibility of creating concealed dependence on a specific regulator by altering the carrier’s metabolic parameters, without triggering an alarm in the existing life-support system.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s67-1: I turned toward the risk seat and the presiding seat.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s69-1: “Since you need to guard against me today, who can guarantee that tomorrow one of you won’t secretly put this mechanism Vera envisioned into practice?
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s69-2: Once it succeeds, which of the ten seats dares guarantee to the others that they will never find some way to take control of this new body of mine?”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s70-1: The whole chamber fell briefly dead silent. Galen stared sharply at Sera.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s73-1: “As long as the procedure is compliant, I will sign. That is the entirety of procedure.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s75-1: The witness, Estelle, opened the ledger in her hands.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s77-1: “If separate supervision is implemented, can the Boundary Guard enter the cells and interrogate people alone? If the parameters for the next body are quietly altered, who can discover it first? This so-called foolproof solution is only a set of accounts that can never be balanced. Keeping the three of them here leaves the village with kindling for a civil war that could ignite at any moment.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s78-1: Old Barro struck his cane hard against the floor.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s80-1: “If separate confinement becomes leverage, then carry out the third proposal: permanent isolation! Lock them beneath the White Tower, cut them off from the outside forever, and have the full council choose dedicated guards to watch them!”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s82-1: “And.” I stepped forward, directly breaking the tacit understanding at the long table. “Keeping us in the dungeon leaves behind a living gold mine that everyone will constantly fight over. The third proposal is unworkable too.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s84-1: Sera turned her gaze toward the other side of the attendee seats.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s86-1: “Local candidate Estelle. You are an independent subject of this village and are not bound by your status as a witness. What do you request for your final disposition?”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s87-1: The local Estelle sat quietly. Her eyes passed over Otto and Sera in turn, then came to rest on the proposal sheets that had been repeatedly amended.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s89-1: “I said before that I didn’t want to return to Watermarsh and start over from the beginning. I wanted to stay and rewrite the outskirts’ covenant.” She swept a cold gaze over the long table. “But I understand now. If I stay at your table of power,
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s89-2: I can’t even keep my own covenant. I’ll only become a vessel that produces technical intelligence, a bargaining chip for you to use against one another while restraining these three. That’s more disgusting than starting over in the mining district.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s92-1: “As an independent local candidate, I have the right to apply for return to my original settlement. I request that my candidate file be sealed with the closure of this case, and that I be sent back to Watermarsh for disciplinary review there. This is my own matter. I will not sign for the witness, and I will not board your ship.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s94-1: “Record: Seal the local candidate Estelle’s file. This case is concluded. Return her to Watermarsh for review.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s95-1: The local Estelle’s case file was sealed then and there. Her candidacy was suspended, and she would take no further part in the struggle.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s97-1: At that moment, Yuna slowly came forward from the very edge of the long table. She refused the assigned slot and stood there instead as an informed party to the matter.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s101-1: “I’m not here as a spectator. I’m one of the people on that paper to be confined, and the bargaining chip you were discussing just now.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s102-1: Sera lowered her head slightly to glance at the agenda before her. She did not reach out to turn the page.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s104-1: “I will never accept any extended-life privilege you use to buy people’s support. I agreed to be restored so I could continue my own life, not so I could become leverage against Arno. I will not accept confinement or support in any form.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s107-1: Galen’s hand lifted halfway from his knee, then stopped helplessly.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s110-1: She deliberately used the most distant titles from the seats at the long table. Meru jerked her head up, fingers instinctively tightening around the edge of the table, as though trying to find the shadow of the child she had once been in this grown woman carrying the smell of smoke and gunpowder.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s112-1: “I clearly remember that you once acted as my parents. But in this world, you have only one daughter. Her name is Milu.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s113-1: Galen’s Adam’s apple moved violently. Meru bit her lip, moisture rising in her eyes.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s115-1: “You have no obligation to pretend that you still remember those things. The people who don’t remember me owe me nothing.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s116-1: Yuna withdrew her gaze, and her voice returned to calm.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s118-1: “So don’t try to make a single decision for me either.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s119-1: When she finished, she stepped back half a pace and returned to the subject’s position. Galen’s suspended hand dropped completely and struck his knee hard.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s122-1: Sera looked at the three people before the long table, her tone cold:
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s124-1: “You refuse both support and control. Should we simply send you to the outskirts? If you spend even one day there under the identity of ‘informed persons,’ the Inner Circle will never sleep soundly again.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s126-1: “Of course not.” I met her gaze without avoiding it. “The outskirts as they are now have no administrative authorization network capable of receiving us, and no common court capable of negotiating with
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s126-2: the Inner Circle as an equal. If we walk out directly, we either become technical dependents of some of you, or, to protect ourselves, lead the mine workers into a bloody war for power against you.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s127-1: I put more weight into my voice.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s129-1: “We refuse to serve as guardians of this old order, and we will never become leaders of an uprising in the outskirts. In this world, there is no peaceful role in which we can stand.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s130-1: I looked at these people accustomed to ruling the village through ledgers.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s133-1: “Throwing people out of the Inner Circle does not mean letting them live. The missing isolation populations in your old records all became numbers crossed out in the ledger after their
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s133-2: supplies were cut off. As long as the ten seats still need to establish absolute authority in the village, the exiled will always make the best objects for demonstrating that authority.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s134-1: Someone at the long table frowned.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s136-1: “Yesterday afternoon, the six workers clearing the outer road to the launch site demanded that the truth be made public and were detained for refusing orders. You will never hold a public trial for insubordination, much less release them without charge. If they don’t leave with us, all that awaits them is the abandoned mine.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s137-1: I looked directly at the ten seats.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s139-1: “I propose replacing the abandoned permanent-isolation case with a permanent-exile case: one-way departure, with no possibility of return.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s142-1: “The proposal has two columns. First column: me, Yuna, and witness Estelle, forcibly exiled permanently. Second column: give the six workers charged with insubordination on the outer side a choice. If they are unwilling
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s142-2: to serve their sentences in the mine, allow them to leave with us—on the condition that they personally confirm. Sending the people involved in the current case aboard is your way to stop creating new blood debts.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s144-1: “Motion to join the cases accepted. Record: outer insubordination case joined as the second column of the exile resolution.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s146-1: “First column. I choose one-way departure. I’ll sign it myself.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s148-1: “I also agree to one-way departure, with no return ever.” Yuna’s gaze swept across the long table. “I confirm it myself.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s150-1: Sera did not answer immediately. Instead, she turned toward the external seat.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s152-1: “Chico, check the launch-site route manifest. Toma, verify the launch-material interface before departure.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s153-1: Chico pulled the terminal panel toward him and tapped rapidly. The screen’s faint light illuminated his tense face. After a moment, he raised his head.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s155-1: “The manifest data is up. It’s locked to a one-way ejection trajectory left by the old civilization, targeting an exoplanet in nearby deep space. The ship’s current fuel is enough only for one-way acceleration,
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s155-2: escape from this planet’s gravity, and orbital insertion and landing at the planet. There is no margin for a second launch or a return flight. Once it takes off, returning is physically impossible.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s156-1: Toma heavily opened another paper ledger beside him, his rough fingers passing over several lines.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s158-1: “The launch platform’s external water intake and separation bolt are locked to single use.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s160-1: Sera turned the previous proposal facedown on the table.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s162-1: “Separate confinement and permanent detention are unworkable. Void. The route verification is confirmed. We now vote on the two columns of the third proposal.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s164-1: “I’ll say the same thing I said before: no precedent, no retreat from the line. Not release.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s165-1: Old Barro struck his cane heavily and said nothing, his face dark.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s168-1: The first two votes still stood like an iron wall. But a crack had appeared.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s170-1: “If it’s an abandoned one-way ejection trajectory,” Chico said, pointing at the route on the terminal screen, “then let them go into space and give these secrets a grave they can never leave. I vote release.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s172-1: Galen reached for the blank parameter sheet printed with the contingency plan and turned it facedown.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s177-1: “If that machine has already burned out, then the resource channel between the Inner and outer circles, established through the root machine, has already been severed. If they leave this village now, the Inner Circle
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s177-2: will no longer have any leverage over the outskirts. The consequences of the shutdown cannot be undone. Then has the candidate system maintained through this exchange of interests also reached the point of settlement?”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s178-1: Sera turned to look at her, without hesitation:
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s180-1: “Yes. Effective immediately, all candidate files in the village are permanently terminated. There will be no further selection and no reserve places.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s183-1: “I propose terminating the village-wide candidate system and voiding the basis for all exchange of interests between the Inner and outer circles.” She looked across the long table. “Who opposes?”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s184-1: Silence filled the long table. Even Kane and Barro said nothing. Everyone understood clearly: without the ability to explore outward, the knowledge and life allotments the Inner Circle used to keep the outskirts dangling had
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s184-2: become water without a source. And since tonight they were sending three people who could expose the truth at any moment off this planet, there was no reason to keep maintaining the lie that selection was anything but control.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s185-1: Sera drew a heavy line across the paper.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s186-1: Meru slowly bent down and pushed aside the scattered firewood that had rolled from the execution pyre beside her feet. The wood rolled across the stone with a dull, heavy thud.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s192-1: “I won’t sign something that cuts off their path forward.” Toma lowered his head to look at his rough fingers, his voice heavy. “I vote release.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s195-1: Otto scattered the wooden tokens across the long table. The gesture meant he was abandoning the calculation of keeping these people in his hands.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s197-1: “As long as the root machine’s core reading is confirmed at zero, the launch facilities will be physically disconnected after the ship leaves the Boundary.” He stared at me. “I vote release.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s198-1: At that point, the long table held five votes in favor and two opposed.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s200-1:
Next was Rena.
In this world, she was the mother who had given birth to and raised me. But when I, who had crossed countless worlds, stood before her, my chest churned with an indescribable dislocation and distance.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s201-1: She stood, leaned forward slightly, and silently placed herself between me and the line of Boundary Guards carrying out the order. It was a wordless act of protection.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s204-1: Six votes in favor, two opposed.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s207-1: “The word I bit down on the day before yesterday remains the word today. Once these people leave the Boundary, they are outside my sight. I will never sign for them. Not release.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s208-1: As soon as he finished speaking, he suddenly raised his hand and slowly lowered the torch he had kept raised to guard against emergencies. Following the Boundary Guard commander’s movement, the guarded torchlight
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s208-2:
around the square dimmed in row after row.
He had not changed his bottom line of compulsory control, but the extinguishing torches already acknowledged through action that the resolution’s direction had been decided.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s209-1: Six votes in favor, three opposed.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s211-1:
Only Sera remained among the ten seats at the long table.
She raised her eyelids, glanced at the control proposal covered in revisions, and pushed it straight to the corner of the table.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s217-1: The recorder checked the names. Sera signed.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s221-1: “The third resolution officially passes. Execution begins immediately.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s222-1: I watched the pen come down. The agreement on the page was not impossible to tear up. What made it executable now was the balance of ten seats each holding an interface while fearing one another.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s225-1: “Bring up the six workers from the outskirts.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s226-1: Six people in oil-stained work clothes were brought to the edge of the long table. Just now, outside the square’s cordon, the Boundary Guards’ guns had stood between us. Now, for the first time, they were truly permitted to come forward and stand before the elders’ council’s long table.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s228-1: “Yesterday afternoon, you shouted outside because you wanted a chance to speak for yourselves.” I looked at them. “This is it.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s230-1: “The resolution on the second column has passed. You have two choices now: be sent back to the bottom of the abandoned mine to serve your sentences, or accept permanent one-way exile.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s233-1: “After the shutdown, all candidate status in the village has been terminated. There is no possibility of turning back from this path.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s234-1: Meru’s hand tightened beneath the long table.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s236-1: “The destination is an unscouted exoplanet. The odds of survival are unknown. This multilayer ark currently has enough carrying capacity for you as well, but the ship has no fuel margin for a return.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s236-2: Even if you survive the landing, that planet has no industrial capacity to provide you with launch fuel or another return vehicle. No one else is being added because this list is determined solely
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s236-3: by the causal involvement in the present case: the three who must leave, and the six who have been detained. Anyone willing to go must confirm it in their own words. No one may sign for you.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s237-1:
The first worker, Naiva, raised her head, glanced at the armed Boundary Guards, then looked toward the black sky.
“If I was going to refuse orders, I never planned on living long enough to climb down from it.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s237-2: ” She turned toward the elders behind the table. “Going back to the bottom of the mine is just waiting to die somewhere else. I’d rather freeze to death in space than submit to your judgment again. I’m going.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s238-1: The second, a thin mechanic named Thun, clenched his fists.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s240-1: “Yesterday outside, we got no truth at all. If staying means we won’t even be allowed to ask why we’re moving those machines from now on, I’d rather leave. I understand the ship’s structure. I’m going.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s241-1: Samo, beaten until his face was covered in blood, spat out a mouthful of red and said hoarsely, “Those two stopped working, and I let go with them back then. Same now. I’m going.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s242-1: The fourth was an older electrician. He pointed to the scars around his wrist. “If obeying still ends like this, I’d rather take my chances over there. They’ll need an electrician. I’m going.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s243-1: The fifth drew a deep breath and did not hesitate. “My family didn’t even leave a name behind in the mine. Rather than go back and spend my whole life as expendable material with no record of ever existing, I’d rather leave my name on a contract no one can sign for me. Confirmed. I’m going.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s244-1: The youngest apprentice at the end of the line was still trembling in both legs, but he straightened his neck and shouted, “When we stood together to block the door yesterday, I’d already made up my mind! I’m going!”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s245-1: This was not an expedition filled with hope. Between two forms of despair, they used their own voices to choose the path that could leave them forever facing away from the ten-seat long table.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s246-1: The elders’ council’s old-civilization archives recorded the planet as a candidate world possibly possessing an atmosphere and liquid water, but they had never surveyed it in person. Whether its environment was harsh remained undetermined.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s247-1: Before they made their decision, I could have told them that in the previous branch I had seen that lake with my own eyes, even the dark, leaf-shaped organisms, and offered it as assurance that they could survive. But I said nothing.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s248-1: Once the ten seats became certain that the other side was habitable, these six volunteers would immediately be redefined—they would no longer be insubordinate workers being exiled, but an advance party sent by the Inner Circle to a new territory.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s248-2: The ten people at the long table would immediately withdraw the one-way departure resolution, equip them with communicators, mark them with a seal of belonging, and turn them into the Inner Circle’s overseas assets through discipline and bloodline.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s249-1: If they were to become the foundation of a new settlement, it had to be something they built themselves after landing, not something they became as dependents of the ten seats. What they were exchanging absolute uncertainty for now was precisely this freedom, planned by no one.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s251-1: “Record: The six maintenance workers in the second column have each confirmed their departure. No one signed for them.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s254-1: Night had deepened. The cordon had completely dispersed.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s255-1: There were no farewells from family, and no one stopped to look back at the lights behind them. The departure agreement had been signed. This non-returning trajectory formally severed their final connection with the village.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s256-1: Kane rose abruptly and strode toward the Boundary Guard line at the edge of the square.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s258-1: “Now that the resolution has passed, those leaving are removed from the village register immediately. I will lead the escort myself and take them to the launch site.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s259-1: Before turning away, he announced in a lowered voice:
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s261-1: “I’ll prepare the travel rations for the escort.”
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s262-1:
That night, no lights were lit around the outer edge of the square. The villagers and outer workers who had not been permitted into the Inner Circle hearing stood silently in the darkness beyond the cordon.
When Kane’s line of Boundary Guards opened a passage, they made no sound, and no one raised
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s262-2: a torch. As the group passed, someone slipped a heavy coat into Samo’s hands, while someone else placed several full waterskins on the group’s cart. There were no slogans and no farewell ceremony. Only these things passed quietly through the darkness, completing the public witnessing for them.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s263-1: I walked at the very front of the group. Rena stood behind the long table, watching me without moving. She did not offer anything as the other villagers had. She only clenched her hands tightly, her knuckles blanching with the force.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s264-1: Our eyes met for an instant in the air. She had already learned last night that the ship was one-way. When she cast that vote, she had already decided that she would never see me
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s264-2: again in this lifetime. She did not move forward, and I stopped as well. In this world, she had given birth to me but had not raised me to adulthood. And now, I was leaving her forever.
texts.chapter:v15-31c:event:text-s265-1: The Boundary Guards called for us to keep moving from behind. I looked back at her one last time, then turned and walked toward the dark road leading to the launch site.
texts.chapter:v15-31d:title: Appendix Three to Chapter Thirty-One: The Resolution
texts.chapter:v15-31d:event:text-s2-1: Late at night, on the deliberation square before the White Tower. The torchlight had already been lowered, dim light falling across the long table ahead.
texts.chapter:v15-31d:event:text-s3-1: The seven-to-three vote had been settled, and the six maintenance workers’ authorization to leave had been confirmed one by one. On the execution document bearing nine names, only the final cancellation procedure remained.
texts.chapter:v15-31d:event:text-s5-1: Sera, seated behind the long table, did not immediately reach for the heavy official seal on the table, the one representing removal from the register.
texts.chapter:v15-31d:event:text-s6-1: She opened the thick boundary register beside her.
texts.chapter:v15-31d:event:text-s8-1: “By regulation, anyone expelled under the resolution must be removed from the boundary register.” Sera looked at us. “Those six were just stamped. Of the three of you, Arno has a field of his own in the boundary register. The witness is an outsider who never obtained local registration; the register never had a place for her.”
texts.chapter:v15-31d:event:text-s11-1: “But you are different. In every record preserved by the village, this world has never had a person like you.” Sera looked at her. “But you are standing here
texts.chapter:v15-31d:event:text-s11-2: now, accepting the long table’s resolution to expel you. If the boundary register has no entry for you, I have no way to press this seal of removal onto you.”
texts.chapter:v15-31d:event:text-s15-1: “I can only draw a field now.”
texts.chapter:v15-31d:event:text-s16-1: Sera turned the register to the relevant page. It was densely covered in standardized grids.
texts.chapter:v15-31d:event:text-s17-1: She reached out, took up the iron ruler, and pressed it hard against the narrow blank margin at the very bottom of the page.
texts.chapter:v15-31d:event:text-s20-1: The pencil scraped forcefully along the cold edge of the iron ruler.
texts.chapter:v15-31d:event:text-s21-1: It was a rough black frame. On this register, continued for who knew how many years, there was now a long rectangular field that had not existed before.
texts.chapter:v15-31d:event:text-s22-1: Sera moved the ruler aside and filled the new field with handwriting:
texts.chapter:v15-31d:event:text-s24-1: “Name: Yuna. Affiliation: None. Reason: Leaving the village.
texts.chapter:v15-31d:event:text-s25-1: Duty Elder’s Note: This entry is newly created. This person is present, but the register has no field for her; provisionally recorded here for removal from the register.”
texts.chapter:v15-31d:event:text-s29-1: Yuna looked at the space drawn specifically for her on the register and slowly nodded.
texts.chapter:v15-31d:event:text-s32-1:
